positiveFlows.title: THE FIVE ALASKA NATIVE SERVING INSTITUTIONS (ANSI) OF THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF) COLLEGE OF RURAL AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT (CRCD) HAVE FORMED THE DRUMBEATS CONSORTIUM AS COLLABORATIVE PARTNERS TO APPLY FOR AND IMPLEMENT THE FISCAL YEAR 2021 USDA NIFA ANNH PROGRAM PROPOSAL, INVESTING IN SUSTAINABLE STEWARDSHIP. DRUMBEATS CONSORTIUM MEMBERS INCLUDE: BRISTOL BAY CAMPUS (BBC) LOCATED IN DILLINGHAM; CHUKCHI CAMPUS (CC) LOCATED IN KOTZEBUE; INTERIOR ALASKA CAMPUS (IAC) LOCATED IN FAIRBANKS; KUSKOKWIM CAMPUS (KUC) LOCATED IN BETHEL; AND NORTHWEST CAMPUS (NWC) LOCATED IN NOME. THESE FIVE CAMPUSES ARE STRATEGICALLY LOCATED IN REGIONAL TRANSPORTATION HUBS AND PROVIDE EDUCATIONAL SERVICES TO ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL RESIDENTS ACROSS OVER 166 ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES. TOGETHER, THE CAMPUSES PREPARE ALASKA NATIVE AND RURAL COMMUNITY STUDENTS WITH PRACTICAL, TECHNICAL AND RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP KNOWLEDGE IN THE FANH SCIENCES.EDUCATIONAL EQUITY IS PROVIDED THROUGH ISS PROGRAMS WHICH PROVIDE RELEVANT, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING TO UNDERREPRESENTED ALASKA NATIVE STUDENTS AND RESIDENTS. ISS FURTHER INCREASES UAF CAPACITY TO DESIGN AND DELIVER CURRICULA THROUGH INNOVATIVE INSTRUCTIONAL DELIVERY SYSTEMS IN ETHNOBOTANY (EBOT), HIGH LATITUDE RANGE MANAGEMENT (HLRM), TRIBAL STEWARDSHIP (TS), ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES (ENVI), SUSTAINABLE ENERGY (SE), AND FOOD SECURITY AND SOVEREIGNTY (FSS).THE ALASKA NATIVE POPULATION AS A WHOLE IS EXPERIENCING INCREASING HEALTH AND ECONOMIC ISSUES. THE AREAS SERVED BY THE CRCD CAMPUSES HAVE POVERTY RATES THAT RANGE FROM 15.6% TO 33.45%. THIS IS SIGNIFICANTLY ABOVE THE ALASKA (10.9%) AND NATIONAL (11.8%) AVERAGES (US CENSUS BUREAU, QUICKFACTS, 2018). THESE HIGH RATES REFLECT THE FACT THAT THERE ARE FEW YEAR-ROUND, FULL-TIME JOBS; MOST OPPORTUNITIES FOR WAGE EMPLOYMENT ARE IN TRIBAL GOVERNANCE, HEALTH CARE, AND EDUCATION, WITH REMAINING OPPORTUNITIES SEASONAL SUCH AS CONSTRUCTION, WILDLAND FIREFIGHTING, FISHING AND FISH PROCESSING. THE ADDITIONAL DEPENDENCE UPON REFINED FOSSIL FUELS AND SKYROCKETING ENERGY COSTS CREATE HARDSHIPS FOR RURAL RESIDENTS.HOWEVER, A WILD FOOD HUNTING AND FISHING ECONOMY IS STILL A REALITY IN ALASKA. THE ABILITY TO CONTINUE CUSTOMARY TRADITIONS OF SELF-SUSTAINING FOOD PRODUCTION THROUGH STEWARDSHIP IN THE MANAGEMENT OF LAND, GAME AND FISHERIES IS OF PARAMOUNT IMPORTANCE IN ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES TO LEARN HOW TO BE ENERGY EFFICIENT INCREASES ENERGY SECURITY.IN ADDITION, THE ACTIVITIES OF THE INVESTING IN SUSTAINABLE STEWARDSHIP ANNH GRANT ADDRESSES VIABILITY OF RURAL ALASKAN COMMUNITIES 1) BY PREPARING STUDENTS FOR PLACE-BASED EMPLOYMENT; 2) BY EDUCATING COMMUNITY MEMBERS ON HOW TO INCREASE FOOD SECURITY AND SOVEREIGNTY, INCLUDING PROMOTION OF TRADITIONAL FOOD GATHERING; AND 3) BY EDUCATING COMMUNITY MEMBERS ON HOW TO INCREASE ENERGY EFFICIENCY TO REDUCE THE HIGH COST-OF-LIVING. THE DRUMBEATS CONSORTIUM MEMBERS AIM TO DEVELOP A CADRE OF LOCAL EXPERTISE AND LEADERS THROUGH TRAINING, EDUCATION AND RESEARCH PROGRAMS BUILT AROUND THE SUBSISTENCE SCIENCES (AS DEFINED IN TITLE VII OF THE ALASKA NATIONAL INTEREST LANDS CONSERVATION ACT (ANILCA) THAT ALSO FIND A HOME IN THE FANH SCIENCES. HIGH LATITUDE RANGE MANAGEMENT IS NOT A SUBSISTENCE-BASED PROGRAM BUT PROVIDES EDUCATION IN ANIMAL HUSBANDRY FOR REINDEER MANAGEMENT FOR COMMERCIAL SALE UNDER USDA GUIDELINES.THE OUTCOMES OF THESE PROGRAMS FIND PREVIOUS PARTICIPANTS AS LOCAL, REGIONAL AND STATEWIDE LEADERS, CONTRIBUTING IDEAS AND SOLUTIONS FOR ALASKA NATIVE ISSUES RELATED TO FOOD AND ENERGY SECURITY, INCORPORATING INDIGENOUS WAYS OF KNOWING. THE GROWTH OF COLLABORATION BETWEEN PROGRAMS HAS EXTENDED INTO NEW REGIONS, WITH COMMUNITY MEMBERS BECOMING ROLE MODELS OF SELF-SUFFICIENCY BY PRACTICING TRIBAL STEWARDSHIP, SUSTAINABLE ENERGY, AND REGIONAL FOOD SECURITY.

THE HI!AG PROGRAM OF THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII (UH) TARGETS UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS TO PROVIDE EDUCATION, AND AGRIBUSINESS AND MARKET DEVELOPMENT TRAINING, TO EMPOWER HAWAII RESIDENTS TO BREAK THE NEGATIVE CYCLE OF RESOURCE AND EMPLOYMENT INSECURITY. PROJECT STRATEGIES ARE DESIGNED TO SUPPORT INDIVIDUALS AND BUSINESSES BY ENSURING EQUITABLE ACCESS TO UH, STATE, AND FEDERAL AGRIBUSINESS DEVELOPMENT RESOURCES. THROUGH THIS COHESIVE EFFORT TO SUPPORT EDUCATION AND DIVERSIFIED AGRICULTURE IN HAWAII, THE PROJECT ADDRESSES THE BROADER ISSUES OF FOOD SECURITY, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTION, SOCIAL EQUITY, PRESERVING AGRICULTURAL LAND AND HAWAII'S LIFESTYLE, AND DIVERSIFYING THE STATE'S ECONOMIC BASE. THOUGH A VARIETY OF ACTIVITIES, BOTH NEW TO THIS YEAR AND CONTINUING FROM PREVIOUS YEARS, HI!AG WILL HAVE AN IMPACT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII AND ACROSS THE STATE OF HAWAII, TO IMPROVE SCIENCE-BASED EDUCATION AT ALL LEVELS (K-16); TO INCREASE RURAL ECONOMIC VIABILITY AND JOB OPPORTUNITIES; AND TO BUILD A LARGER AND BETTER PREPARED WORKFORCE TO SERVE IN HAWAII'S FOOD, AGRICULTURE, AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT INDUSTRIES.THE HI!AG PROGRAM, WAS ESTABLISHED WITH THE GOALS OF (1) DEVELOPING AND STRENGTHENING THE LOCAL AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PRODUCTION WORKFORCE THROUGH EDUCATION AND TRAINING AND (2) EXPANDING LOCAL AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PRODUCTION THROUGH MORE PRODUCTIVE AGRIBUSINESSES. OUR PROGRAMS PREPARE STUDENTS FOR CAREERS IN THE FANH SCIENCES, AND DEVELOP LEADERSHIP ABILITIES. OUR BROAD COLLABORATION STRENGTHENS THE INSTITUTIONAL EDUCATIONAL CAPACITIES OF THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAII SYSTEM. OUR PARTNERSHIP OF NINE UH CAMPUSES, PROVIDES EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT TARGET A VARIETY OF DEGREE LEVELS, INCLUDING ASSOCIATE OF SCIENCE, BACHELOR OF SCIENCE, AND GRADUATE DEGREES. OUR EDUCATION PROGRAMS EMPHASIZE THE FOLLOWING NEED AREAS: (I) CURRICULA DESIGN, MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT, AND LIBRARY RESOURCES; (V) STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING; AND (VI) STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY. OUR FOCUS IS ON DEVELOPING STUDENT LEADERSHIP SKILLS, AND BUILDING CAPACITY, AMONG HAWAII'S RURAL COMMUNITIES, INCLUDING NATIVE HAWAIIANS AND OTHER HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS. PROJECT OUTCOMES INCLUDE A LARGER NUMBER OF GRADUATES IN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES, AND INCREASED PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF AGRIBUSINESSES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROMOTE ADVANCES IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN FANH SCIENCES THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY. TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE THROUGH THE AGRICULTURE EXPERIENCE TRACKER, ADOPTED BY THE NATIONAL FFA ORGANIZATION AND 48 STATE FFA ASSOCIATIONS, WILL CREATE A TRANSFERABLE CERTIFICATE PATHWAY ALIGNED TO SOFT SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AND CAREER READINESS PRACTICES. HIGH SCHOOL AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION TEACHERS ARE ACCUSTOMED TO THE CAREER TECHNICAL EDUCATION (CTE) PATHWAY THAT PROVIDES FANH CURRICULUM FOR DEVELOPMENT OF HARD SKILLS, SUCH AS PLANT SCIENCE, ANIMALS SCIENCE, AND AGRICULTURE MECHANICS. THESE ESTABLISHED PATHWAYS ALIGN WITH CTE PATHWAYS ESTABLISHED AT THE COMMUNITY COLLEGE LEVEL AND TO AGRICULTURAL MAJORS AT THE UNIVERSITY LEVEL. ADDING THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY AS A COMPANION TO THE CTE PATHWAY, WILL BRING AWARENESS TO THE IMPORTANCE OF ACQUIRING BOTH SETS OF SKILLS: HARD SKILLS AND SOFT SKILLS. THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATION PATHWAY IS A FOCUSED STRATEGY AIMED TO CREATE A SYSTEM-WIDE PATHWAY (HIGH SCHOOL TO UNIVERSITY) TO EMPOWER STUDENTS' SUCCESS AND PREPAREDNESS TO BECOME THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LEADERS THROUGH COLLABORATIONS WITH THE AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY, FACULTY, AND LEADERS IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION. EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EXPERIENCES SHARED WITH FELLOW CLASSMATES, COLLABORATION WITH ACRS21 ADVISORY COMMITTEE, AND INTERACTION WITH THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY WILL PROMOTE STUDENT DISCOVERY, DIVERSITY, AND DISTINCTION AS THEY PROGRESS THROUGH THE CERTIFICATE PATHWAY (I.E. THE STATED CORE VALUES OF FRESNO STATE). EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING WILL ADVANCE INCLUSIVE RELATIONSHIPS THAT FOSTER PERSONAL PASSION, POTENTIAL AND A SENSE OF BELONGING. THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY SUPPORTS FRESNO STATE'S OWN INSTITUTIONAL STRATEGIC PLAN IN ALL FOUR-PRIORITY AREAS. PRIORITY ONE- ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL DEVELOP SOFT SKILLS AND CAREER READINESS SKILLS FOR MORE HSI STUDENTS WHO WILL HAVE ACCESS TO CO-CURRICULAR SERVICES THAT PROMOTE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND A SENSE OF BELONGING. PRIORITY TWO- NATIONAL, STATE, AND REGIONAL WORKSHOPS WILL PROVIDE ADDITIONAL TRAINING, LEADERSHIP, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FACULTY AND STAFF MEMBERS. PRIORITY THREE- TEACHING MODULES, STUDENT SELF-ASSESSMENTS, AND THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL BE MANAGED ONLINE THROUGH THE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIENCE TRACKER (AET), THEAET.COM, AND THE DIGITAL AGRICULTURE SOLUTION HUB (DASH) WEBSITES. PURSUING ACRS21 CERTIFICATES WILL PROMOTE STUDENT INVOLVEMENT IN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES AND, THEREBY, CONTRIBUTE TO A HEALTHIER, MORE SUSTAINABLE CAMPUS ENVIRONMENT. PRIORITY FOUR- PARTNERSHIPS CREATED THROUGH ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL TRACK STUDENT INVOLVEMENT FROM HIGH SCHOOL TO COMMUNITY COLLEGE AND/OR UNIVERSITY. WEB-BASED TECHNOLOGY WILL TRACK STUDENT PROJECTS, SERVICE-LEARNING, JOB SHADOWING, INTERNSHIPS, AND STUDENT GROWTH IN PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT. FIVE TO TEN YEARGOALS PROJECT THAT 35,460 STUDENTS, INCLUDING 17,185 UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS, WILL BE IMPACTED BY THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY: 35,000 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, 1517 TEACHERS, 450 UNDERGRADUATE, AND 10 GRADUATE STUDENTS.THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA) SEEKS TO PROMOTE AND STRENGTHEN THE ABILITY OF HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTIONS (HSI) TO CARRY OUT HIGHER EDUCATION PROGRAMS THAT ATTRACT, RETAIN, AND GRADUATE OUTSTANDING STUDENTS CAPABLE OF ENHANCING THE NATION'S FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN SCIENCE PROFESSIONAL AND SCIENTIFIC WORK FORCE (GRANT EXECUTIVE SUMMARY). THIS GOAL MIRRORS THE STRATEGIC GOALS OF FRESNO STATE. ADDITIONALLY, JCAST SEEKS TO ENHANCE THE ABILITY OF STUDENTS TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THEIR CAREERS AND MAKE POSITIVE CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE QUALITY OF LIFE IN THEIR COMMUNITIES (JCAST HOME PAGE). THIS PROJECT'S OBJECTIVES WILL BE REFLECTIVE OF NIFA'S GOAL, JCAST'S GOAL, AND FRESNO STATE'S STRATEGIC GOALS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** BE AWARE 2 AIMS TO CONTINUE AND EXPAND OUR TRAINEESHIP MODEL TO A GREATER RECRUITING SCALE BY: (A) OFFERING A MODULAR EDUCATION MODEL THAT INCLUDES COURSES/CERTIFICATES/PROJECTS IN INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) SECURITY, DATA SCIENCE, MACHINE LEARNING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR THE OPTIMIZATION AND DESIGN OF AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; (B) PROVIDING ALL OF OUR STUDENTS WITH THE OPPORTUNITY TO GET ACCESS TO INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS (INCLUDING A CYBERINFRASTRUCTURE PLATFORM) AND MULTIPLE CERTIFICATES; (C) ADDING NEW HSI PARTNERS; (D) EXPANDING OUR USDA PARTNERS FOR SUMMER INTERNSHIPS; AND (E) LEVERAGING USDA-HSI FUNDS WITH EXTERNAL FUNDING MECHANISMS FOR A SUSTAINABLE PROGRAM.

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** SECONDARY TO POST-SECONDARY EDUCATION PIPELINES HAVE BEEN SUCCESSFUL IN BRINGING HISPANIC STUDENTS TO THE TERTIARY CLASSROOM. HOWEVER, RESEARCH SUGGESTS THAT LEAKS IN THE PIPELINES EXIST AS THESE PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN SUCCESSFUL IN RETAINING ONLY 13% OF UNDERREPRESENTED FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN SCIENCES (FANH) STUDENTS THROUGH BACCALAUREATE GRADUATION (DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, 2018) AND PROPELLING EVEN FEWER STUDENTS TO POSTGRADUATE STUDIES (TAIALLI & ORTIZ, 2017); THE STATISTICS ARE EVEN MORE DIRE IN GEOGRAPHIC REGIONS SUFFERING FROM PERSISTENT POVERTY (GOOD & LA PRAD, 2013). WHILE TARGETED INTERVENTIONS GEARED TOWARD RETAINING AND GUIDING HISPANIC STUDENTS TOWARD GRADUATE SCHOOL EXIST, THEY USE AN INTERMEDIARY TO CONNECT THE UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE INSTITUTIONS (GHEE, ET AL, 2016). IN AREAS OF PERSISTENT POVERTY AND LOW COLLEGE DEGREE ATTAINMENT, HOWEVER, REGIONAL COOPERATION BETWEEN INSTITUTIONS IN THE EDUCATIONAL PIPELINE MAY BE NECESSARY TO ENHANCEBACCALAUREATE GRADUATION RATES AND SUBSEQUENT ENROLLMENT IN GRADUATE SCHOOL.TEXAS TECH UNIVERSITY (TTU) AND EASTERN NEW MEXICO UNIVERSITY (ENMU) SERVE A REGION THAT IS 57% HISPANIC; 71% OF HIGH-SCHOOL GRADUATES IN THE REGION ARE HISPANIC, YET ONLY 18% ENROLL IN A BACCALAUREATE DEGREE PROGRAM FOLLOWING GRADUATION (TEXAS HIGHER EDUCATION DATA, 2018; NEW MEXICO HIGHER EDUCATION DEPARTMENT, 2017). THE POPULATION OF THE BORDER COUNTIES OF NEW MEXICO AND TEXAS HAS NOTORIOUSLY LOW COLLEGE DEGREE ATTAINMENT - 15% OF THE REGIONAL POPULACE HOLD A BACHELOR'S DEGREE, COMPARED TO STATE AVERAGES OF 28%, AND A NATIONAL AVERAGE OF 34% (CENSUS, 2018A). THE LACK OF DEGREE COMPLETION CONTRIBUTES TO THE PERSISTENT LEVELS OF POVERTY OBSERVED ACROSS THE REGION (GOOD & LA PRAD, 2013).THERE IS AN URGENT REGIONAL NEED TO FORM AN EDUCATIONAL PIPELINE THAT BOTH RETAINS FANH STUDENTS IN THEIR BACCALAUREATE DEGREE PROGRAMS WHILE GUIDING THEM TOWARDS GRADUATION AND SUBSEQUENT ENROLLMENT IN A GRADUATE DEGREE PROGRAM. THIS PIPELINE PROGRAM WILL INCREASE COLLEGE RETENTION RATES BY 10% THROUGH ITS INTEGRATED PROGRAMMING THAT TAPS INTO BELONGING, MENTORING, AND SUPPORT ISSUES IDENTIFIED BY FANH STUDENTS AS CRITICAL COMPONENTS IN THEIR PERSISTENCE TOWARD DEGREE COMPLETION (WIMMER & MEYERS, 2013).

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** NEW MEXICO STATE UNIVERSITY (NMSU) ASPIRES TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO TRANSFORM THE EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE, INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY AND WORKFORCE OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS IN NATURAL RESOURCE AND AGRICULTURE THROUGH A NEW PROGRAM, ENHANCEMENT. ENHANCEMENT BRINGS FACULTY ACROSS FIVE NMSU CAMPUSES, INCLUDING FOUR COMMUNITY COLLEGES, AND MENTORS UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS (GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE). WE PREPARE STUDENTS TO TRANSFER FROM COMMUNITY COLLEGE, EXCEL AT A 4-YEAR DEGREE AND ULTIMATELY TRANSITION TO CAREERS BY PROVIDING TOOLS, EXPERIENCE AND MENTORSHIP TO SUCCEED. THESE PROGRAMS ENHANCE COMPETENCE FOR PROFESSIONAL POSITIONS AND CONTRIBUTE TO WORKFORCE DIVERSITY. THIS PROJECT OFFERS GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS SUMMER INTERNSHIPS, FACULTY LABORATORY MENTORSHIPS, NEAR-PEER AND PROFESSIONAL MENTORING, AND TRAVEL TO PROFESSIONAL MEETINGS. WE TRAIN STUDENTS TO CONDUCT OUTREACH FOR INTERNSHIPS AND RESUMES TO HIGH SCHOOLS, AND 2 & 4 YEAR INSTITUTIONS. UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTSWILL INTERACT WITH THE GRADUATE STUDENTS BY DEVELOPING RESEARCH LINKED THEIR GRADUATE STUDENT MENTOR'S RESEARCH AND FACULTY SUPERVISE THESE MENTORSHIPS.WE HAVE WORKED WITH THE LEADERSHIP AT NMSU-LAS CRUCES TO INSTITUTIONALIZE ON-THE SPOT HIRING EVENTS WITH USDA FPAC, AND INSTITUTIONALIZE PROGRAMS THAT FOSTER A CLEAR TRANSFER PATHWAY. TO ACCOMPLISH OUR GOALS, WE HAVE GATHERED A STRONG AND DYNAMIC TEAM WITH BACKGROUNDS SPANNING POST-SECONDARY EDUCATION IN BIOLOGY, NATURAL RESOURCES AND AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION; HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT OUTREACH PROGRAMS; AND FEDERAL WORKFORCE PERSONNEL.

THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A SET OF COURSES AND CO-CURRICULAR LEARNING EXPERIENCES DESIGNED TO ENGAGE STUDENTS IN PROJECT-BASED COMMUNITY SERVICE CONTRIBUTING TOWARDS LASTING DISASTER RELIEF AND RESILIENCY IN PUERTO RICO AFTER HURRICANE MARIA. WE ARE WELL PREPARED TO ENGAGE IN THIS EFFORT AS OUR STUDENT-LED PROJECTS HAVE ALREADYBEEN INITIATED AS A RESULT OF A PREVIOUSLY EXISTING COLLABORATIVE EFFORT BETWEEN THESE THREE INSTITUTIONS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS EFFORT IS TO ESTABLISH A MODEL FOR A SUSTAINABLE PIPELINE OF EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIESSTEMMINGFROM HIGHLY MOTIVATING GRAND CHALLENGES SUCH AS THESE. THE PRIMARY OPERATIONAL CHALLENGE WE OBSERVE WHEN ENGAGING STUDENTS IN THIS CONTEXT IS THAT THEIR LEARNING LIFECYCLES ARE SHORT RELATIVE TO RESILIENT PROBLEM SOLVING AFTER DISASTERS, WHICH HAS ESPECIALLY LONG PROBLEM SOLVING LIFECYCLES. THUS, TO FACILITATE SUCH EXPERIENCES, WHILE MAINTAINING STEADILY DEVELOPING AND DEMONSTRABLE OUTCOMES FOR OUR COLLABORATING COMMUNITIES, OUR OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE IS TO SOLIDIFY AND STRENGTHEN OUR COLLABORATIONS WITH CURRENT AND FUTURE LOCAL PARTNERS. THE OUTCOME WILL BE A NEW CADRE OF STUDENTS WHO ARE VERSED IN LEADERSHIP, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, AND CAPABLE OF CROSS-CULTURAL AND TRANSDISCIPLINARY GLOBAL ENGAGEMENTS WHEN PROBLEM SOLVING.

THIS COOPERATIVE PROPOSAL BETWEEN DEPARTMENTS OF ANIMAL SCIENCE AT SOUTH DAKOTA STATE UNIVERSITY (SDSU), NORTH DAKOTA STATE UNIVERSITY (NDSU), UNIVERSITY OF NEBRASKA-LINCOLN (UNL), AND UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA (UMN), AND THE ALLIED LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION INDUSTRY IS DESIGNED TO STRENGTHEN THE NEXT GENERATION OF LEADERS IN THE NATION'S SCIENTIFIC AND PROFESSIONAL WORKFORCE IN FOOD AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURE.STUDENTS GRADUATING FROM GRADUATE OR PROFESSIONAL PROGRAMS RELATED TO LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION ARE FREQUENTLY LESS PREPARED THAN NECESSARY FOR SUCCESS IN ALLIED INDUSTRY CAREERS. SPECIFICALLY, THEY OFTEN LACK WELL-HONED INTERPERSONAL COMMUNICATIONS SKILLS AND PRACTICAL EXPERIENCE IN LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. MEAT ANIMAL PRODUCTION IS OFTEN AT THE FOREFRONT OF HIGHLY CHARGED DEBATES AND PUBLIC POLICIES. CONSEQUENTLY, THE NEED FOR STRONG COMMUNICATION SKILLS IN GRADUATES OF ANIMAL SCIENCE PROGRAMS, INCLUDING M.S. AND VETERINARY STUDENTS, IS PARAMOUNT. WHILE UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAMS INCREASINGLY INCORPORATE 21ST CENTURY SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, THE SAME IS OFTEN NOT TRUE FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS, ESPECIALLY WITH REGARD TO THEIR ABILITY TO EFFECTIVELY COMMUNICATE WITH A NON-ACADEMIC AUDIENCE. YET IT IS THESE AUDIENCES THAT OFTEN ARE MOST VOCAL AND EXPRESS THE GREATEST CONCERN REGARDING FOOD PRODUCTION METHODS. INTERACTION WITH FOOD PRODUCERS, PURCHASERS, AND POLICY MAKERS REQUIRES A DIFFERENT COMMUNICATION STYLE THAN IS TYPICALLY EMPHASIZED IN GRADUATE TRAINING (I.E. COMMUNICATING SCIENCE TO SCIENTISTS). IT IS CRUCIAL TO FUTURE SUCCESS OF PRODUCTION AGRICULTURE THAT ACADEMICS, PRODUCERS, AND INDUSTRY BECOME MORE INVOLVED IN PUBLIC DISCUSSION AND INCORPORATE METHODS TO BUILD AND REAFFIRM THE PUBLIC'S TRUST, WHILE MAINTAINING AN EMPHASIS ON GOOD SCIENCE. TWO DECADES AGO IT WAS REPORTED MANY INCOMING ANIMAL SCIENCE STUDENTS HAD LITTLE TO NO PREVIOUS EXPOSURE TO FOOD ANIMAL PRODUCTION, AND UNFORTUNATELY THAT TREND CONTINUES TO GROW. THIS CREATES CHALLENGES COMMUNICATING WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS DUE TO A LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEXITIES AND CHALLENGES OF DAY-TO-DAY LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION, YET COMMUNICATION WITH THESE INDIVIDUALS IS EXPECTED FOR MANY M.S. ANIMAL AND VETERINARY SCIENCE GRADUATES. RECENT TRENDS IN FARM LABOR SHOW AN INCREASING PROPORTION OF INTERNATIONAL WORKERS, COMPOUNDING COMMUNICATION CHALLENGES.THE SUCCESS OF AGRICULTURE-RELATED COMPANIES, LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, AND THE FOOD INDUSTRY RESTS ON THE "SOCIAL LICENSE" TO OPERATE WHICH IS GRANTED BY OUR CONSUMERS AND SOCIETY IN GENERAL. AS PUBLIC INTEREST IN FOOD PRODUCTION INCREASES, FOOD PRODUCTION COMPANIES ARE INCREASINGLY EXPECTED TO FUNCTION WITHIN CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY PRACTICES. SCIENTISTS ARE THOROUGHLY TRAINED IN CRITICAL THINKING SKILLS, RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES, AND COMMUNICATION WITH OTHER SCIENTISTS, BUT LACK TRAINING TO COMMUNICATE KEY OUTCOMES OF SCIENCE TO A NON-SCIENTIFIC AUDIENCE. YET INCREASINGLY, THE RESPONSIBILITY OF COMMUNICATING SCIENCE TO THE GENERAL PUBLIC FALLS TO THE SCIENTIST. THUS, INTENTIONAL TRAINING OF SCIENTISTS TO ACQUIRE SKILLS NECESSARY TO COMMUNICATE WITH THE PUBLIC NEEDS TO BECOME A KEY COMPONENT OF FORMAL SCIENTIFIC TRAINING.TWO KEY AREAS OF CONCERN, COMMUNICATION AND REAL-WORLD EXPERIENCE, ARE THE FOCUS OF THIS PROJECT AS A MEANS TO BETTER PREPARE STUDENTS FOR ENTRY INTO THE FANH SCIENCES WORKPLACE. THIS FOCUS, AND THE RESULTANT SCOPE OF THE PROJECT, WAS DEVELOPED IN DIALOG WITH INDUSTRY AND FACULTY LEADERS IN THE FANH SCIENCES; ALL PARTIES EXPRESSED AGREEMENT THAT THE POTENTIAL TO ADDRESS THESE CONCERNS WAS GREAT, BUT LARGELY UNREALIZED. THERE IS CURRENTLY NO UNIFYING INITIATIVE THAT BRINGS TOGETHER ALLIED INDUSTRIES, STUDENTS, AND TRAINING INSTITUTIONS WITH AN INTENTIONAL FOCUS ON TRAINING EXPERIENCES TO MEET THESE COMMUNICATION AND INDUSTRY EXPERIENCE DEFICITS.THE PROJECT CENTERS ON DEVELOPMENT OF A SERIES OF COMMUNICATION AND LEADERSHIP ACTIVITIES DURING A CONVENTIONAL GRADUATE PROGRAM. SUCCESSFUL DEVELOPMENT OF LEADERSHIP SKILLS IS MORE LIKELY WHEN RELEVANT LEARNING ACTIVITIES ARE INTEGRATED THROUGHOUT A COLLEGE PROGRAM RATHER THAN IN A FOCUSED, SINGLE LEARNING ACTIVITY. THIS PROJECT IS DESIGNED TO WORK IN CONCERT WITH TRADITIONAL SCIENCE AND CLASSROOM ACTIVITIES REQUIRED TO COMPLETE RESEARCH- OR COURSE-BASED M.S. DEGREES. THE SERIES OF ACTIVITIES ARE FORMULATED TO INTEGRATE PRIOR LEARNING INTO EACH SUBSEQUENT ACTIVITY TO REINFORCE EARLIER CONCEPTS.THE PROJECT'S OBJECTIVES ARE:TO DEVELOP A SERIES OF INTER-DISCIPLINARY EVENTS AROUND THE USDA EDUCATION NEED AREAS OF: CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT, INSTRUCTIONAL DELIVERY SYSTEMS, AND EXPANDING STUDENT CAREER OPPORTUNITIES.TO PROVIDE FOUNDATIONAL GRADUATE STUDENT DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOCUSED IN THE AREA OF INTERPERSONAL COMMUNICATION, LEADERSHIP, AND REAL-WORLD EXPERIENCE RELEVANT TO THE FANH SCIENCES WORKPLACE.TO DEVELOP INTERDISCIPLINARY COMMUNICATION AND LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCES FOR TEAMS OF AGRICULTURE AND NON-AGRICULTURE-FOCUSED STUDENTS AROUND KEY COMMUNICATION CHALLENGE AREAS IN THE FANH SCIENCES WORKPLACE.TO DEVELOP A CADRE OF STUDENTS WHO, IN COMBINATION WITH ALLIED LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION INDUSTRY, WILL ACQUIRE KEY ANALYTICAL AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS BASED ON REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS IN THE FANH SCIENCES TO CREATE PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS.OBJECTIVES WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH:DEVELOPMENT OF A VIDEO SEMINAR SERIES DESIGNED TO TRAIN STUDENTS IN DIVERSE COMMUNICATION TECHNIQUES THAT ARE FOCUSED ON A RANGE OF COMMUNICATION FORMATS SUITABLE FOR A DIVERSITY OF TARGET AUDIENCES.AN ANNUAL COMMUNICATION CONFERENCE, IN COLLABORATION WITH ALLIED INDUSTRY, WHERE STUDENTS PARTICIPATE IN DISCUSSIONS AROUND THE NATIONAL LIVESTOCK INDUSTRY, DEVELOP SOLUTIONS FOR CASE STUDIES BASED ON REAL-WORLD SCENARIOS, AS WELL AS PRESENT EXTENSION TALKS AND SALES PITCHES FOR REVIEW BY RELEVANT EXTENSION SPECIALIST AND INDUSTRY SALES LEADERS, RESPECTIVELY.SELF-AWARENESS TRAINING PROGRAMTWO WEEK INDUSTRY INTERNSHIPSTHINK/PAIR/SHARE EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITY WHERE ANIMALSCIENCE STUDENTS PREPARE CONCISE EDUCATIONAL MATERIAL ON HOT BUTTON TOPIC RELEVANT TO FOOD ANIMAL PRODUCTION. EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS ARE EVALUATED BY STUDENTS IN HUMAN NUTRITION AND COMMUNICATION STUDY AREAS.COURSES CENTERED ON COMMUNICATING WITHIN DIVERSE CULTURESTEACHING CERTIFICATE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPMENT OF COMMUNICATION SKILLS WITHIN THE CLASSROOMTHROUGH THIS PROGRAM, "STRENGTHENING THE SCIENTIFIC AND PROFESSIONAL WORKFORCE, " MASTER'S AND VETERINARY SCIENCE STUDENTS WILL BE BETTER EQUIPPED TO HANDLE WORKPLACE DEMANDS IN THE FANH SCIENCES AND WILL HAVE ENHANCED SKILLS FOR IMPROVED COMMUNICATION WITH THE NON-AGRICULTURE COMMUNITY. THIS PROJECT INCORPORATES LEARNING ACTIVITIES USING DIRECT INTERACTION WITH FANH SCIENCE WORKFORCE LEADERS THROUGH PROBLEM-SOLVING, EDUCATIONAL AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES, AND INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCES TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF HIGH QUALITY GRADUATES PREPARED TO LEAD THE FANH SCIENCES WORKPLACE INTO THE FUTURE.

PLANT BREEDING IS A KEY COMPONENT FOR MEETING FUTURE FOOD NEEDS IN A WORLD UNDERGOING POPULATION GROWTH A CHANGING CLIMATE AND A SHRINKING LAND AND WATER RESOURCE BASE. AN ESSENTIAL INGREDIENT FOR BREEDING PROGRESS IS THE GENETIC DIVERSITY CONSERVED IN THE USDA-ARS NATIONAL PLANT GERMPLASM SYSTEM AND SIMILAR ORGANIZATIONS. MAINTAINING AND UTILIZING THE PLANT GENETIC RESOURCES (PGR) IN THESE GENEBANKS REQUIRE A SPECIALIZED SET OF SKILLS BUT THERE IS A LACK OF HIGH-QUALITY MATERIALS FOR LEARNING THESE SKILLS. THIS PROJECT REPRESENTS A UNIQUE COLLABORATION BETWEEN SCIENTISTS AT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY IOWA STATE UNIVERSITY AND USDA-ARS TO ADDRESS THIS NEED. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO EXPAND THE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE THAT IS WELL TRAINED IN SUBJECTS RELEVANT TO PGR ACQUISITION PRESERVATION DISTRIBUTION EVALUATION AND UTILIZATION. WE WILL DEVELOP AN ORGANIZED SERIES OF LEARNING RESOURCES (VIDEOS EBOOK CHAPTERS IMAGES ETC.) COVERING PGR TOPICS; ESTABLISH AN ONLINE REPOSITORY TO HOST ORGANIZE AND TRACK USAGE OF THE CONTENT; DEVELOP AND OFFER THREE 1-CREDIT GRADUATE-LEVEL COURSE MODULES AT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY ON PGR CONSERVATION AND USE IN PLANT BREEDING AND GENETICS; AND DISSEMINATE THE DEVELOPED MATERIALS BROADLY TO COMMUNITIES OF INTEREST BOTH IN THE U.S. AND GLOBALLY. TWO GRADUATE STUDENTS WILL HELP CREATE AND EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE LEARNING RESOURCES. WE ENVISION THAT THE MATERIALS DEVELOPED IN THIS PROJECT WILL BE WIDELY INCORPORATED INTO GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE AGRICULTURAL AND BIOSCIENCE COURSES THUS ENHANCING THE UNDERSTANDING OF CROP GENETIC DIVERSITY AND ITS IMPORTANCE IN GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY. THE LEARNING RESOURCES WILL ALSO BE USED BY USDA-ARS PRIVATE COMPANIES AND NON-GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS TO IMPROVE THE ABILITIES OF THEIR EMPLOYEES TO CONSERVE AND USE PGR.

THE NATION NEEDS MORE TRAINED FORESTERS, AND IT NEEDS A FORESTRY WORKFORCE THAT IS MORE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE DIVERSITY OF THE POPULATION IT SERVES. TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL NEED, WE ARE DEVELOPING A COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE DEPARTMENT OF FORESTRY (DOF) AT MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY (MSU), MSU INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY (IAT), BAY COLLEGE (BC) AND MUSKEGON COMMUNITY COLLEGE (MCC), CENTERED AROUND THE DEVELOPMENT OF CURRICULUM FOR TWO NEW CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS THROUGH IAT: (1) PROFESSIONAL FORESTRY CERTIFICATE (PF) AT BC AND (2) URBAN AND COMMUNITY FORESTRY CERTIFICATE (UCF) AT MCC. THIS COLLABORATION CREATES A PATHWAY FOR STUDENTS TO COMPLETE A SPECIALIZED MSU CERTIFICATE THROUGH IAT AND AN ASSOCIATE DEGREE FROM PARTNER COMMUNITY COLLEGES IN JUST TWO YEARS. UPON COMPLETION OF THE TWO-YEAR PROGRAM, GRADUATES CAN ENTER THE WORKFORCE WITH NETWORKS CREATED THROUGH THE PROGRAM OR SEAMLESSLY MATRICULATE INTO DOF'S BACHELOR'S DEGREE PROGRAM.THIS PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND LEADERSHIP TRAINING AND ESTABLISH ACTIVITIES DESIGNED TO PROMOTE STUDENT ENTRY, RETENTION, AND SUCCESS IN THE NEW CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS. THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON THE HEC NEED AREAS OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT, INSTRUCTIONAL DELIVERY SYSTEMS AND EXPANDING STUDENT CAREER OPPORTUNITIES AND FACILITATING INTERACTION WITH OTHER ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT ADVANCES BOTH HEC PROGRAM GOALS OF: (1) ENHANCING THE QUALITY OF INSTRUCTION FOR BACCALAUREATE DEGREES, AND (2) INCREASING THE NUMBER AND DIVERSITY OF STUDENTS COMPLETING POSTSECONDARY DEGREES.

EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS HAVE BEEN UNABLE TO CAPITALIZE ON AGRICULTURAL INFORMATICS-RELATED OPPORTUNITIES, DESIRED IN THE MARKETPLACE. AN AGRICULTURAL INFORMATICS CURRICULUM IS PROPOSED TO BE DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH 1862 AND 1890 INSTITUTIONS. A TOTAL OF 13 FACULTY/STAFF FROM THREE PARTNERING UNIVERSITIES WILL COME TOGETHER TO BUILD TRAINING RESOURCES TO HELP STUDENTS IN AGRISCIENCE DEPARTMENTS IMPROVE THEIR ABILITY TO 1) WRANGLE DISPARATE DATA INTO COHERENT LAYERS, FOR IMPROVED ANALYTICS AND RESEARCH CAPACITY, 2) GENERATE MODELS AND ANALYTIC METHODS TO FACILITATE REAL-TIME DECISION MAKING IN AGRICULTURE, AND 3) PRODUCE DATA ARCHITECTURES AND CODE THAT ENABLE IMPROVED DATA FLOW AND INTEROPERABILITY.OVER 1300 UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS (MORE THAN 80% UNDERGRADUATES) WILL BE IMPACTED OVER 3 YEARS GRANT PERIOD BY PARTICIPATING IN TWO-WEEK COURSE MODULE, ENROLLING IN THREE NEW COURSES, AND UNDERGOING EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING BY PARTICIPATION IN DATATHONS/HACKATHONS, ONLINE DATA SYMPOSIUM, AND INTERNSHIPS.THE COURSES WILL USE PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING AND INVERTED CLASSROOM FOR ACTIVE STUDENT PARTICIPATION. COMMUNICATION, TEAM BUILDING, LEADERSHIP, AND INDEPENDENT LEARNING WILL BE EMPHASIZED THROUGHOUT. THE EDUCATIONAL CONTENT WILL ALSO BE MADE AVAILABLE TO OTHER LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES AND INDUSTRY FOR WIDER USE.

THE APPALACHIAN MOUNTAIN REGION OF EASTERN KENTUCKY CONTAINS HIGH PROPORTIONS OF FORESTLAND ALONG WITH COAL AND NATURAL GAS DEPOSITARIES. HOWEVER, THIS REGION IS THE HOME OF THOUSANDS OF HOUSEHOLDS LIVING UNDER PERSISTENT POVERTY. MANY OF THE RURAL LANDSCAPES ACROSS THE SOUTHERN APPALACHIAN REGION HAVE EXPERIENCED SIGNIFICANT CHANGES OVER THE YEARS. IN THOSE AREAS, NATURAL RESOURCE EXTRACTION ACTIVITIES, PARTICULARLY SURFACE MINING, HAVE RESULTED IN SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS. FOREST BIOMASS LOSS IS ONE OF THE PRIMARY IMPACTS OF MOUNTAIN TOP REMOVAL IN APPALACHIA. THE DISTRIBUTION AND ABUNDANCE OF TREE SPECIES AND UNDERSTORY VEGETATION ARE KEY INDICATORS OF FOREST ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY. WHILE THE MINING INDUSTRY BRINGS JOBS AND INCOME OPPORTUNITIES FOR SOME, ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS AFFECTS HUMAN AS WELL AS NATURAL COMMUNITIES. THESE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS INCLUDE REMOVAL OF TOP SOIL AND NEAR-SURFACE MATERIALS; DESTRUCTION OF VEGETATION, BIOMASS, AND BIODIVERSITY; AND POTENTIAL FOR FLOOD, LANDSLIDES, AND OTHER HAZARDS. TOXIC SUBSTANCES IN POLLUTION FROM MINING OPERATIONS HAVE ALSO BEEN LINKED WITH SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUES, SUCH AS RESPIRATORY DISEASES AND CANCER, IN THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES. LANDSCAPE CHANGES DUE TO EXCESSIVE MINING CAN AFFECT THE PROVISION OF FOREST AND OTHER ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, WHICH MAY EVENTUALLY THREATEN THE QUALITY OF LIFE IN NEARBY COMMUNITIES. BECAUSE OF THE DEPENDENCY OF THESE COMMUNITIES ON RENEWABLE AND NON-RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES IN THE LANDSCAPE, THE IMPACT OF HISTORICAL MINING ACTIVITIES, AND EMERGING THREATS (SUCH AS ENVIRONMENTAL INSECURITY), IT IS IMPORTANT TO STUDY HOW MINING ACTIVITIES IN THE PAST HAVE IMPACTED THE FOREST LANDSCAPE, ECOSYSTEM FUNCTIONS, AND QUALITY OF LIFE IN THE REGION. IT IS EQUALLY IMPORTANT TO KNOW THE VULNERABILITY OF THESE COMMUNITIES TO NEW THREATS FROM CHANGES IN NATURAL RESOURCES AND OTHER SUPPORTING SYSTEMS. INADEQUATE UNDERSTANDING OF THE DYNAMICS OF THIS UNIQUESYSTEM HAS LIMITED THE ABILITY OF RESEARCHERS TO EXPLAIN LANDSCAPE CHANGES IN THE FUTURE AND THE RESULTING IMPACT ON ECOSYSTEM FUNCTION. THIS PROJECT WILL COLLECT RESIDENTS' PERCEPTIONS OF CHANGES IN THE LOCAL ENVIRONMENT, ECOSYSTEMS FUNCTION, AND QUALITY OF LIFE DUE TO SURFACE MINING ACTIVITIES AND LINK THESE TO THE LAND COVER CHANGE DATA DERIVED FROM THE ANALYSIS OF SATELLITE DATA TO IDENTIFY SPECIFIC LOCATIONS THAT HAVE UNDERGONE SIGNIFICANT CHANGES AND NEED THE MOST ATTENTION. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO ESTIMATE LOSS IN BIOMASS AND CARBON BALANCE DUE TO SURFACE MINING AND THE EFFECTS ON CLIMATE AND PREDICT RECOVERY TIME OF THE LOST BIOMASS BY ESTIMATING VEGETATION GROWTH IN THE RECLAIMED LAND. THE NATURE OF THE HUMAN-ENVIRONMENT RELATIONSHIP IN MANY NATURAL RESOURCE-DEPENDENT COMMUNITIES IS VERY COMPLEX AND CAN BE ONLY ADDRESSED BY INTEGRATING HUMAN PERCEPTIONS TO THE PHYSICAL CHANGES ON THE LANDSCAPE. COUPLING AIRBORNE LIGHT DETECTION AND RANGING (LIDAR), UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES(DRONES), AND SATELLITE IMAGERY WITH FOREST STAND STRUCTURE AND SPECIES COMPOSITION DATA ALLOWS US TO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL FOR SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL DISTRIBUTION OF THE GROWTH AND LOSS OF IMPORTANT PLANT SPECIES ACROSS THE STUDY SITE AND THEIR OVERALL ECOSYSTEM PRODUCTIVITY (I.E., TOTAL BIOMASS OR BIOMASS CHANGES OVER TIME). THE PROPOSAL HAS TWO COMPONENTS. THE RESEARCH COMPONENT OF THE PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN UNDERSTANDING VARIATIONS IN THE CONSEQUENCES OF SURFACE MINING ON ENVIRONMENT, FOREST PRODUCTIVITY, AND FEASIBILITY OF RECLAIMED LANDS FOR AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES AND THE TEACHING COMPONENT INCLUDES ENHANCEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE CURRICULA AT KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY (KSU). KSU WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE-KNOXVILLE (UT) AND TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY (TSU) TO SEEK INPUT FROM LOCAL STAKEHOLDERS VIA FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS AND SURVEYS. TIME SERIES, GEOSPATIAL, SURVEY, AND LONGITUDINAL DATA DERIVED FROM THE PROJECT WILL BE UTILIZEDTO EXPLORE INTERCONNECTIONS BETWEEN SURFACE-COAL MINING, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND OTHER LAND-COVER CHANGE CONDITIONS IN CASE STUDIES AND STUDENT RESEARCH PROJECTS. GENERATING NEW KNOWLEDGE FROM THE STUDY OF SOCIOECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL DYNAMICS OF SURFACE MINING WILL RAISE THE LEVEL OF AWARENESS OF THEIR IMPACTS ON THE LOCAL ECONOMY AND ECOSYSTEMS. THIS NEW KNOWLEDGE WILL ALSO ENHANCE THE TEACHING AND RESEARCH CAPACITY OF THE COLLABORATIVE UNIVERSITIES (KSU, UT, AND TSU) TO EXAMINE THE SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF THE REGION. SPECIFICALLY, THE FINDINGS OF THIS STUDY CAN BRING US CLOSER TO ANSWERING THE QUESTION: "GIVEN THE LONG HISTORY OF COAL-FIELD BASED EMPLOYMENT AND REVENUE GENERATION, WHY HAS THIS REGION LAGGED BEHIND OTHER AREAS IN QUALITY OF LIFE?" THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS OPPORTUNITIES THAT INCORPORATE INNOVATIVE, PROJECT-BASED EDUCATION BEYOND THE CLASSROOM AND ENHANCED RESEARCH, CRITICAL THINKING, AND DATA ANALYSIS SKILLS. STUDENTS AND FACULTY WILL BE ABLE TO LINK SOCIOECONOMIC, REMOTE SENSING, AND MICROCLIMATE DATA TO EXPLAIN THE DYNAMICS OF HUMAN-ENVIRONMENT RELATIONSHIPS IN ONE OF THE MOST VULNERABLE AND UNDERSERVED REGIONS OF THE NATION. FREQUENT INTERACTIONS BETWEEN RESEARCH FACULTY AND EXTENSION STAFF WILL ALSO ENHANCE EXTENSION POTENTIAL AND IMPACTS BY PROVIDING NEW KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY IN ADVISING CLIENTS FACING EMERGING ISSUES SURROUNDING SURFACE-MINING PRACTICES. PROPOSED PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL ALSO PROVIDE RESEARCH FACULTY AND STAFF EXPOSURE TO INNOVATIVE AND EMPIRICAL LAND COVER CHANGE MODELS AND SPATIAL DATA PREPARATION, ANALYSIS, AND INTERPRETATION AS WELL AS OPPORTUNITIES FOR CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT AND COORDINATION OF RESEARCH AND EDUCATION EFFORTS. THE OUTPUTS OF THE PROJECT WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPACTS ON ENHANCING THE CAPACITY OF FACULTY FROM THE PARTICIPATING UNIVERSITIES TO DEVELOP PROGRAMS FOR IMPROVED AGRICULTURE, ENVIRONMENTAL SECURITY, HUMAN SCIENCE EDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION.

THE OVERALL GOAL IS TO USE A COLLABORATIVE INTEGRATED APPROACH THAT FOCUSES MAINLY ON EDUCATION TO EXPAND AN UNDER-DEVELOPED, INFANT AQUAPONICS INDUSTRY IN OKLAHOMA. THIS COMPLEMENTS THE USDA'S STRATEGIC GOAL #1 (MAXIMIZE THE ABILITY OF AMERICAN AGRICULTURE PRODUCERS TO PROSPER BY FEEDING AND CLOTHING THE WORLD) IN THAT IT IS FOSTERING GROWTH IN THE OKLAHOMA AQUAPONICS INDUSTRY, ESPECIALLY EXPANSION OF SMALL FARMS, A VITAL AGRICULTURE SECTOR CURRENTLY IN DECLINE THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY AND IMPOVERISHED IN OKLAHOMA. IT ALSO COMPLEMENTS USDA STRATEGIC GOAL #3 (PROMOTE AMERICAN AGRICULTURE PRODUCTS AND EXPORTS) IN THAT OUR PROJECT WILL PROMOTE AQUAPONICS PRODUCTS AS HEALTHY CHOICES, #4 (FACILITATE RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT) BY SPREADING THE WORD ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITIES THAT AQUAPONICS PROVIDES IN AN INCREASINGLY DRIER CLIMATE AND DEGRADED FOOD SYSTEM, AND #7 (PROVIDE ALL AMERICANS ACCESS TO A SAFE, NUTRITIOUS AND SECURE FOOD SUPPLY) IN THAT WE ARE PROMOTING AN INDUSTRY THAT WILL PROVIDE HEALTHY LOCAL FOOD TO A SEVERELY INSECURE FOOD SYSTEM IN OKLAHOMA (I.E. MOST FOOD IS IMPORTED, SUBJECT TO SHIPPING STRESS/DAMAGE, AND SUPPLY ISSUES (ESPECIALLY IN RURAL AREAS DURING BAD WEATHER).

THE INCREASING IMMIGRANT POPULATION ON THE DELMARVA PENINSULA HAS CREATED THE DEMAND FOR LOCALLY GROWN ETHNIC CROPS. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO BUILD UPON AND EXPAND CAPACITIES FOR RESEARCH, TEACHING AND EXTENSION BY WIDENING THE INVESTIGATION OF ETHNIC CROP PRODUCTION, IMPROVING PRE- AND POST-HARVEST PEST MANAGEMENT, CONDUCTING PHYTOCHEMICAL AND ANTIOXIDANT ANALYSIS ON THE CROPS, INVESTIGATING VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT TO CREATE NICHE MARKETS, CREATING UNDERGRADUATE COURSES IN FOOD SCIENCE, PROVIDING EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS IN AGRONOMIC PRODUCTION AND FOOD SCIENCE, AND CONDUCTING TRAINING WORKSHOPS FOR SMALL FARMERS ON SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION PRACTICES, VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT/PACKAGING/MARKETING, AND POTENTIAL MARKETS. PROVIDING SMALL FARMERS WITH RESEARCH-BASED PRODUCTION PRACTICES AND INTRODUCING THEM TO POTENTIAL VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT MARKETS WILL PROVIDE THEM WITH NEW WAYS TO PRODUCE INCOME THROUGH ALTERNATIVE ENTERPRISES AND IMPROVE THEIR PRODUCTIVITY. THE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES WILL CONTINUE TO BUILD PRODUCTIVE RELATIONSHIPS WITH STAKEHOLDERS, AND HIGHLIGHT UMES' RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CAPABILITIES TO COMMUNITIES ON DELMARVA AND THE WASHINGTON, D.C. METROPOLITAN AREA. PROVIDING RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS, THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PLOTS AND THE INVESTIGATION OF FOOD PRESERVATION METHODS AND VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT WILL PROVIDE EXCELLENT ENVIRONMENTS TO EDUCATE GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, SMALL FARMERS, AND THE LOCAL COMMUNITY ON ETHNIC CROP PRODUCTION AND THE PRINCIPLES OF FOOD SCIENCE. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL BE DISSEMINATED THROUGH RESEARCH TOURS AND ON-FARM DEMONSTRATIONS, INFORMATIONAL LITERATURE, MARKETING AND CROP PRODUCTION GUIDELINES, AND TRAINING AND EDUCATIONAL WORKSHOPS.

STRAWBERRIES ARE PRODUCED AND CONSUMED WORLDWIDE. THE UNITED STATES IS THE SECOND LARGESTPRODUCER OF STRAWBERRIES. ONE OF THE BIGGEST CHALLENGES THAT STRAWBERRY GROWERS ARE FACING IS FRUITROT DISEASE OF GRAY MOLD CAUSED BY THE FUNGUS BOTRYTIS CENEREA. IF UNTREATED, IT CAN CONTRIBUTE UP TO AN 80% YIELD LOSS, REDUCED MARKETABLE YIELD AND SHELF LIFE. WE WILL UTILIZE THE ADVANCES IN SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGY AND AVAILABLE GERMPLASM RESOURCES TO IDENTIFY SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS (SNPS) AND GRAY MOLD RESISTANT LINES. WE WILL DEVELOP GENOME WIDE ASSOCIATION MAPS (GWAS) FOR GRAY MOLD RESISTANCE AND ITS RELATED TRAITS. THE ELITE STRAWBERRY LINES IDENTIFIED IN THIS STUDY WILL BE FURTHER UTILIZED IN THE BREEDING PROGRAMS OR WILL BE ADVANCED FOR MULTI-LOCATION TRAILS. THE EXTENSION SPECIALISTS INVOLVED IN THIS PROJECT WILL COMMUNICATE WITH THE SMALL AND UNDERSERVED FARMERS IN DELMARVA REGION ON GRAY MOLD MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND USE OF RIGHT GENOTYPES. THE POST-HARVEST SPECIALIST WILL BE EVALUATING THE ELITE LINES WITH A VOLATILE COMPOUND TO EXTEND SHELF LIFE OF FRUITS. MOST IMPORTANTLY, THIS PROJECT WILL TRAIN POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCH ASSOCIATES, GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS MOSTLY FROM UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATION WITH MODERN PLANT BREEDING TECHNIQUES AS WELL AS HELP BUILD SMALL FRUITS BREEDING PROGRAM AND RESEARCH CAPACITY AT DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY.

DISEASE-RESISTANT WATERMELON VARIETIES ARE THE MOST COST-EFFECTIVE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SUSTAINABLE SOLUTION. WATERMELON BREEDERS ARE FACED WITH CHALLENGES TO FIND NEW SOURCES OF GUMMY STEM BLIGHT RESISTANCE AS THERE IS NO SINGLE SOURCE OF RESISTANCE IN CULTIVARS. PRESENT PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY GENETIC LOCI CONFERRING RESISTANCE TO IDENTIFY AND COMBINE QTLS RESISTANT TO GUMMY STEM BLIGHT (GSB). RECENTLY, A PLETHORA OF MACHINE LEARNING APPROACHES SUCH AS DEEP LEARNING (DL) ARE AVAILABLE TO FOR PRECISE PHENOTYPING IN PLANT BREEDING. THESE TOOLS ARE INCREASINGLY BEING USED BY THE PLANT SCIENCE COMMUNITY TO MAKE SENSE OF THE LARGE DATASETS NOW REGULARLY COLLECTED VIA HIGH-THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING AND GENOTYPING. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE EXTEND TEACHING DL TOOLS FOR PHENOTYPING AND HOLDING SPECIAL WORKSHOPS FOR STUDENTS TO APPRECIATE LATEST DEVELOPMENTS IN GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES.

positiveFlows.title: THE NEED TO EDUCATE COMMUNITIES ABOUT AGRICULTURE IN OUR SOCIETY WHILE PROMOTING THE PROMISING COLLEGE/CAREER OPPORTUNITIES IN AGRICULTURE ESPECIALLY IN STEM AREAS IS PARAMOUNT. AMARANTHUS AS WELL AS SORGHUM ARE IMPORTANT PLANTS FOR TENNESSEE AGRICULTURE AND THEIR WILD RELATIVES INCLUDE NOTORIOUS WEED SPECIES WHICH MAY CONTAIN GENES USEFUL FOR DEVELOPING RESILIENT CROP VARIETIES. THEREFORE, PLANT GENETICS RESEARCH ON BOTH CROP WILD RELATIVES (CWR) OFFERS AN EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITY TO TRAIN DIVERSE BACKGROUND STUDENTS USING MOBILE-EXTENSION APPARATUS ON ECOLOGICAL CONSCIOUSNESS RELATED TOPICS WHILE ACADEMICALLY MOTIVATING THEM. SUCH RESEARCH TRAININGS OF PRE-COLLEGE, UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WILL STRENGTHEN TSU AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES PROGRAM. THE PROPOSED PROJECT PRESENTS FOLLOWING OBJECTIVE; 1) INCREASE PARTICIPATION IN AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE RESEARCH PROJECT FROM COMMUNITIES ACROSS TENNESSEE USING A STATE-OF-THE-ART MOBILE STEM EDUCATION CLASSROOM/LAB; 2) UNDERTAKE SYLLABI DESIGN FOR DEVELOPING AND/OR ASSIMILATING INTERDISCIPLINARY CURRICULA AND EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS FOR MULTI-TIER TRAINEES; 3) COLLECT PHYLOGEOGRAPHIC AND GLYPHOSATE RESISTANCE POPULATION STRUCTURE DATA ON AMARANTHUS AND SORGHUM, WHILE EDUCATING HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS AND THEIR MENTORS ACROSS TENNESSEE; AND 4) CREATE AND IMPLEMENT A COMPREHENSIVE PLAN TO RECRUIT STUDENTS FOR DEGREE PROGRAMS IN THE TSU COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE BY ENHANCING EXTENSION AND RESEARCH CAPACITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THE PROPOSED MOLECULAR RESEARCH, EXTENSION COURSES AND TRAININGS WILL BE DESIGNED TO COVER ALL FUNDAMENTALS OF RELEVANT SCIENTIFIC PROCESSES IN PLANT GENETICS AND AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION. GRADUATE RESEARCH THESES AND EXTENSION CURRICULA, RELEVANT TO NATURAL RESOURCES AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, WILL BE DEVELOPED FOR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ENHANCEMENTS OF UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.

MAKING AGRICULTURE SUSTAINABLE REQUIRES UNDERSTANDING WHERE BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (BMPS) WILL BE MOST EFFECTIVE IN THE LANDSCAPE TO MAINTAIN THE CONDITION OF NEARBY ECOSYSTEMS, SINCE HUMANS RECEIVE DIVERSE BENEFITS FROM NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS AS WELL AS AGRICULTURAL LANDS. WETLANDS IN PARTICULAR PROVIDE A WIDE VARIETY OF THESE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, INCLUDING NUTRIENT TREATMENT, CARBON STORAGE, POLLINATION, AND FLOOD MITIGATION. PLANNING FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE IN DELAWARE IS ESPECIALLY CHALLENGING WITH SEA LEVEL RISE. WE PROPOSE TO ASSESS THE IMPACTS OF SEA LEVEL RISE ON AGRICULTURE AND WETLAND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND EXPLORE NOVEL USES OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES MAPPING FOR PLANNING BMPS. IN OUR RESEARCH (PRIMARY FOCUS), WE WILL (A) EVALUATE HOW WETLAND SERVICES CHANGE WITH PROXIMITY TO AGRICULTURE, (B) STATISTICALLY PINPOINT "HOTSPOTS" WITH HIGH DELIVERY OF DIVERSE BENEFITS AND INVESTIGATE THE BMPS PROMOTING HOTSPOTS NEAR AGRICULTURAL LANDS, AND (C) USE SEA LEVEL PREDICTIONS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MARGINAL CROPLANDS (CANDIDATES FOR DIFFERENT BMPS) AND SERVICE HOTSPOTS THAT MAY BE LOST. OVERALL, UNDERSTANDING THE FEEDBACKS BETWEEN LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS AND THE FULL ARRAY OF BENEFITS THAT OUR LANDS PROVIDE WILL HELP US INCREASE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES. THE PROJECT ALSO STRENGTHENS DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY'S RESEARCH AND TEACHING CAPABILITIES IN SPATIAL ANALYSIS. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, WE WILL (A) IMPROVE INFRASTRUCTURE AND INFORMATION-SHARING FOR SPATIAL RESEARCH, (B) DEVELOP A NEW COURSE AND WORKSHOPS IN ADVANCED SPATIAL ANALYSIS AND UPDATE MATERIALS IN OTHER COURSES, AND (C) SHARE RESEARCH PRODUCTS WITH FARMERS, PROFESSIONAL DATA USERS, AND K-12 AUDIENCES.

THE HUMAN POPULATION IS EXPECTED TO REACH 9 BILLION IN THE NEXT 30 YEARS AND THE CURRENT FOOD PRODUCTION RATE WILL NEED TO INCREASE BY 30% TO HAVE ENOUGH FOOD TO FEED THE INCREASED POPULATION. PORK IS THE NUMBER ONE CONSUMED MEAT IN THE WORLD. **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE PROPOSED FOUR-YEAR PROJECT IS BROADENING AGRICULTURE SCIENCE EDUCATION (BASE II) FOR HISPANIC STUDENTS THROUGH FLORIDA-TEXAS-NEW-MEXICO CONSORTIUM, WHICH AIMS TO RECRUIT, CULTIVATE, AND DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS, AND TO PRODUCE A HIGHLY-SKILLED WORKFORCE FOR FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES FROM HISPANIC COMMUNITIES WITH MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES: (A) PROVIDE SCIENTIFIC TRAINING OF 15 BACCALAUREATE AND 11 MASTERS STUDENTS IN FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES WITH A CONCENTRATION ON AGROECOLOGY AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE (ASA) FANH-ASA, THAT DEAL WITH THE INTEGRATIVE ASPECTS OF NATURAL RESOURCES, ECOSYSTEM SUSTAINABILITY AND FOOD PRODUCTION; (B) PREPARE STUDENTS FOR CAREER AND LEADERSHIP IN THE SCIENTIFICALLY CHALLENGING AND GLOBALLY COMPETITIVE US AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY; (C) ENHANCE THE QUALITY OF FANH-ASA EDUCATION THROUGH INTER-STATE PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN FIU-UTRGV-NMSU AND STUDENTS EXPOSURE TO AGRICULTURAL KNOWLEDGE BEYOND THEIR HOME STATES VIA EXCHANGE, JOINT RESEARCH, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENTS, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, AND JOINT WORKSHOPS AND WEBINARS. THE GREATEST IMPACT OF THE PROGRAM IS TO FOSTER A SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS, FANH-ASA-RICH EDUCATION TO STUDENTS. **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES TWO PERSISTENT PROGRAMS IN THE FANH-RELATED AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES: 1) EQUITY GAPS IN THE PARTICIPATION AND PERSISTENCE OF UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS PURSUING UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE PROGRAMS AND RELATED CAREERS IN FANH SCIENCES, AND (2) LACK OF EXPERIENTIAL ACTIVITIES TO PREPARE STUDENTS TO ENTER GRADUATE SCHOOL AND JOIN THE WORKFORCE. positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** REGISTERED DIETITIAN NUTRITIONISTS (RDNS) ARE FOOD AND NUTRITION EXPERTS WHO PLAY A VITAL ROLE IN PREVENTING AND TREATING DIET-RELATED HEALTH CONDITIONS. THERE IS A CRITICAL SHORTAGE OF RDNS, ESPECIALLY ETHNICALLY/RACIALLY DIVERSE RDNS. TO BECOME AN RDN, STUDENTS COMPLETE A BACCALAUREATE DEGREE (MASTERS STARTING IN 2024) AND 1000 HOURS OF SUPERVISED DIETETICS PRACTICE (SDP) MENTORED BY CREDENTIALED PROFESSIONALS IN CLINICAL, COMMUNITY, AND MANAGEMENT NUTRITION SITES. THE RDN SHORTAGE IS RELATED TO LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF POSITIONS IN SDP PROGRAMS AND INADEQUATE ACCESSIBILITY TO TRAINING IN RURAL AREAS, BOTH OF WHICH ARE CONSTRAINED BY INSUFFICIENT STUDENT PLACEMENTS IN CLINICAL NUTRITION SITES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, EVALUATE, REFINE, AND DISSEMINATE A SERIES OF HIGH-QUALITY SIMULATIONS (DELIVERED VIA FULL-BODY PATIENT SIMULATOR [SMART MANNEQUINS] AND VIRTUAL REALITY USING SMARTGLASSES) THAT DEVELOP CLINICAL NUTRITION SKILLS OF FOOD, NUTRITION, AND DIETETICS BACCALAUREATE, MASTERS, AND SDP STUDENTS. THESE SIMULATIONS WILL HELP REDUCE THE RDN SHORTAGE BY INCREASING ACCESS TO SDP OPPORTUNITIES; INCREASE ACCESSIBILITY OF CLINICAL SDP TRAINING THAT CAN BE DELIVERED REMOTELY; AND IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF RDN TRAINING BY PROVIDING STANDARDIZED LEARNING EXPERIENCES THAT PROMOTE STUDENT IMMERSION AND ENGAGEMENT. A SECOND AIM IS TO PREPARE FOOD, NUTRITION, AND DIETETICS INSTRUCTORS TO CONFIDENTLY INCORPORATE SMART MANNEQUIN AND VR SIMULATIONS IN THEIR CURRICULUM. A FINAL OBJECTIVE IS TO BUILD SUSTAINABILITY BY DISSEMINATING INSTRUCTOR TRAINING MATERIALS AND HOLDING WORKSHOPS THAT DEMONSTRATE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SIMULATIONS IN NUTRITION AND DIETETIC PROGRAM CURRICULA; PUBLISHING AND PRESENTING PROJECT PRODUCTS AND OUTCOMES IN PEER-REVIEWED VENUES; AND DISSEMINATING PROJECT RESULTS AND PRODUCTS TO U.S. UNIVERSITIES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** LABORATORY-BASED COURSES ARE A VITAL PART OF FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES CURRICULA BECAUSE THEY HELP STUDENTS CONNECT THEORIES TO APPLICATIONS AND BUILD BOTH PRACTICAL SKILLS AND CONCEPTUAL KNOWLEDGE. STUDIES SHOW THAT LABORATORY ACTIVITIES ENHANCE STUDENTS' CONCEPTUAL UNDERSTANDING AND IMPROVE COGNITIVE GROWTH. HOWEVER, MANY STUDENTS STRUGGLE TO GAIN ACCESS TO LABORATORY FACILITIES AND PHYSICAL EXPERIMENTS FOR A VARIETY OF REASONS, INCLUDING SHRINKING FINANCIAL RESOURCES AND SCARCITY OF EXPENSIVE LABORATORY EQUIPMENT AT MANY UNIVERSITIES. FURTHER, DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC, MANY INSTITUTIONS WERE FORCED TO SWITCH TO VIRTUAL CLASSES AND HALT IN-PERSON LABORATORY ACTIVITIES. IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL DESIGN, DEVELOP, AND DEPLOY LOW-COST YET USER-FRIENDLY PAIRED VIRTUAL AND REMOTE LABORATORIES (VR-LABS) FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE-LEVEL FOOD SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING COURSES, AND WE WILL ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE VR-LABS ON STUDENT LEARNING. WE AIM TO DEVELOP WEB-BASED VIRTUAL LABORATORIES (VL) AND REMOTE LABORATORIES (RL) FOR FOOD SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING RELATED TOPICS. THE PROJECT WILL BRING TOGETHER EDUCATORS AND SCIENTISTS FROM FIVE INSTITUTIONS (I.E., WASHINGTON STATE UNIVERSITY, CORNELL UNIVERSITY, CAL POLY POMONA, THE OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY AND RUTGERS UNIVERSITY) WITH COMPLEMENTARY EXPERIENCE IN THE TEACHING OF FOOD SCIENCE, FOOD ENGINEERING, AND FOOD PACKAGING AND PROCESSING TECHNOLOGY COURSES. THE TEAM MEMBERS ALSO COMPLEMENT EACH OTHER WITH EXPERTISE IN THE AREAS OF COMPONENT DESIGN AND FABRICATION, COMPUTER SIMULATION, STUDENT LEARNING PEDAGOGY, INSTRUCTIONAL DESIGN AND EFFECTIVE DELIVERY TECHNIQUES. THE DEVELOPMENT OF VIRTUAL AND REMOTE LABORATORIES (VR-LABS) WILL PROVIDE A PROMISING SOLUTION TO SUPPORT EDUCATION IN THE FANH SCIENCES AND PROVIDE EQUAL ACCESS TO ALL, INCLUDING STUDENTS IN ONLINE DEGREE PROGRAMS AND STUDENTS WITH PHYSICAL DISABILITIES THAT PREVENT THEM FROM ACCESSING LABORATORY BUILDINGS. VIRTUAL LABORATORIES (VL) WILL BE BUILT USING COMMONLY USED SOFTWARE PROGRAMS ON PERSONAL COMPUTERS THAT WILL ALLOW USERS TO PERFORM EXPERIMENTS IN SIMULATED LAB ENVIRONMENTS. WE WILL UTILIZE THE LATEST EDUCATIONAL TOOLS, SUCH AS COMPUTER ANIMATION, SIMULATION, STUDENT LEARNING MANAGEMENT SYSTEM, AND STUDENT DISCUSSION FORUMS IN VL. THE VR-LABS WILL ADVANCE THE STUDENTS MASTERY OF THEORETICAL AND PRACTICAL KNOWLEDGE IN THE AREAS OF FOOD SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING. WE WILL DEVELOP LOW-COST, TAKE-HOME KITS THAT REPLICATE LABORATORY EQUIPMENT USING INEXPENSIVE SCALE MODELS. WE WILL EMPLOY SIMPLE DEVICES AND SENSOR TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF LOW-COST EXPERIMENTAL TAKE-HOME KITS FOR USE IN THE RL. A VARIETY OF TOOLS, INCLUDING 3D PRINTERS AND CNC MACHINE WILL BE UTILIZED TO FABRICATE PARTS FOR THE LABORATORY KITS. EACH OF THE EIGHT PAIRED ONLINE MODULES AND TAKE-HOME KITS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED, AT LEAST BY TWO OF THE TEN PARTICIPATING INSTITUTIONS ACROSS THE NATION, NAMELY CAL POLY-SAN LUIS OBISPO, CHAPMAN UNIVERSITY, CAL STATE-LA, ILLINOIS INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY, NORTH CAROLINA STATE UNIVERSITY, UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA ATHENS, UNIVERSITY OF FLORIDA GAINESVILLE, UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN - STOUT, AND SAN JOSE STATE UNIVERSITY. A COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION PLAN WILL ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE VR-LAB EXERCISES IN ORDER TO IMPROVE THE COURSE CURRICULUM AND INSTRUCTION; TO ATTRACT, RECRUIT, AND RETAIN QUALIFIED AND DIVERSE STUDENTS; AND TO PREPARE GRADUATES WITH THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO MEET THE DEMANDS OF THE WORKPLACE. THE PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL BE DISSEMINATED TO A LARGE NATIONAL AUDIENCE OF STAKEHOLDERS AND POLICYMAKERS. WE WILL DISSEMINATE INFORMATION RELATED TO VR-LAB EXERCISES TO PEERS IN ACADEMIA THROUGH JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS, PROFESSIONAL CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, AND SHARE MAJOR FINDINGS ON SOCIAL MEDIA. OUR PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL ALSO PROMOTE ACCESS TO EDUCATION FOR TRADITIONALLY UNDER-REPRESENTED GROUPS AND IMPROVE THE EDUCATION QUALITY OF FANH SCIENCES PROGRAMS IN 1862 AND 1890 INSTITUTIONS BY IMPLEMENTING VR-LAB MODULES AT THESE INSTITUTIONS. THE VR-LAB IS A FORM OF ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY THAT HAS POTENTIAL TO HELP REDUCE EDUCATIONAL INEQUALITIES AND PROMOTE ACCESS TO LEARNING FOR ALL, REGARDLESS OF LOCATION, DISABILITY, OR SOCIAL STATUS. THE VR-LABS ARE IDEALLY SUITED FOR GEN-Z LEARNERS. FOR CONVENTIONAL ON-CAMPUS EDUCATION PROGRAMS IN FANH SCIENCES ACROSS THE NATION, OUR VL WILL BE FLEXIBLE AND COST EFFECTIVE FOR COMBINATION WITH PHYSICAL EXPERIMENTS IN HYBRID OR MIXED-REALITY LABORATORIES. OUR RL CAN SUPPLEMENT EXISTING CAMPUS LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS AND CAN ALSO HELP STUDENTS GAIN HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE WHILE CONDUCTING THEIR LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS AWAY FROM CAMPUS SETTINGS. ULTIMATELY, THIS PRACTICE OF UTILIZING VR-LABS WILL PROMOTE DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION IN HIGHER EDUCATION BY PROVIDING TEACHING AND LEARNING TOOLS WITH GREATER ACCESSIBILITY AND AT LOWER COST TO ALL TERTIARY EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS IN THE UNITED STATES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THE GAP THAT EXISTS BETWEEN THE EXPECTATIONS OF THE FOOD INDUSTRY EMPLOYERS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS RELATED TO NEW GRADUATES' FOOD PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT (FPD) SKILLS AND THE REAL PERFORMANCE OF THESE GRADUATES WHEN TASKED WITH MANAGING AND LEADING FPD PROJECTS.WHY FOCUS ON FPD COURSES? (1) FPD IS A CAPSTONE COURSE IN MOST FOOD SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMS, YET IT IS NOT INCLUDED AS AN INDEPENDENT COURSE IN THE GUIDELINES FOR INSTITUTE OF FOOD TECHNOLOGISTS (IFT) APPROVAL OF UNDERGRADUATE FOOD SCIENCE AND FOOD TECHNOLOGY PROGRAMS. (2) WHILE THERE ARE NO FPD-SPECIFIC IFT ESSENTIAL LEARNING OUTCOMES (ELOS) DEFINED1, 2, NUMEROUS IFT ELOS ARE RELEVANT AND ARE APPLIED TO ASSESS FPD COURSES NATIONWIDE. (3) FPD REQUIRES THE TEACHING AND APPLICATION OF CORE CONCEPTS LEARNED IN THE FUNDAMENTAL FOOD SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY COURSES SUCH AS FOOD MICROBIOLOGY AND SAFETY, FOOD PROCESS AND ENGINEERING, FOOD CHEMISTRY, AND SENSORY EVALUATION OF FOODS COMBINED WITH OTHER DISCIPLINES RELATED TO THE BUSINESS ASPECT OF THE COURSE SUCH AS ECONOMICS AND MARKETING. (4) CURRENTLY, THERE IS NO BROADLY ACCEPTED TEXTBOOK OR RESOURCE MATERIALS WITH WHICH TO TEACH THE COURSE UNLIKE OTHER TEXTBOOKS COMMONLY USED IN FOOD SCIENCE CURRICULA NATIONWIDE.TEACHING FOOD PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT (FPD) EFFECTIVELY FACES SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES. THESE CHALLENGES INCLUDE LACK OF TRAINING, THE ABSENCE OF A STANDARD TEXTBOOK, AND THE DISPARITY OF THE FPD CURRICULUM ACROSS INSTITUTIONS. TO OVERCOME THESE CHALLENGES, THE PROPOSED PROJECT SEEKS TO DEVELOP CONTENT FOR INSTRUCTORS TEACHING FPD. OUR GOAL IS TO CREATE A STANDARDIZED FPD CURRICULUM AND PEDAGOGY TO BRIDGE THE GAPS BETWEEN THE INDUSTRY, EDUCATORS, AND STUDENTS TO CREATE ROBUST AND JOB-READY PRODUCT DEVELOPERS. WE ENVISION DEVELOPING 35-50 MODULES ACCESSIBLE TO UNIVERSITIES AND INDUSTRY TO SUPPORT HIGH-QUALITY FPD TEACHING FOR BOTH INDUSTRY AND ACADEMIA AND ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE FOR HIGHER EDUCATION, BRIDGING THEINDUSTRY WITH FACULTY AND STUDENTS, AND PREPARING QUALITY GRADUATES FOR THE FOOD INDUSTRY.

OUR GLOBAL POPULATION IS PROJECTED TO EXCEED NINE BILLION BY 2050; THEREFORE, WE FACE UNPRECEDENTED CHALLENGES TO PRODUCE ENOUGH FOOD, FEED, FIBER, AND BIOFUEL FEEDSTOCK. STRENGTHENING THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY IS ESSENTIAL TO MEETING THIS CHALLENGE. TO FULFILL SUCH DEMANDS, HOWEVER, AGRICULTURALISTS WILL BE REQUIRED TO PRODUCE MORE FOOD OVER THE NEXT 40 YEARS THAN HAS BEEN PRODUCED OVER THE PAST 10,000 YEARS COMBINED, AS WELL AS SUFFICIENT BIOFUEL FEEDSTOCK TO ENSURE A SECURE AND INDEPENDENT ENERGY SUPPLY ON A LAND AREA WITH FEWER INPUTS (UNITED NATIONS, 2015). FAILURE TO MEET THESE GOALS COULD CAUSE FOOD INSECURITY IN MANY PARTS OF THE WORLD, LEADING TO INSTABILITY IN THE GLOBAL, GEOPOLITICAL LANDSCAPE. COUPLED WITH THIS CHALLENGE IS THE GROWING DEMAND FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AND LOCALLY GROWN FOOD. AS A RESULT, AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS WILL ALSO BE REQUIRED TO PROVIDE FRESH FOOD PRODUCTS FOR CHANGING DIETARY AND HEALTH HABITS OF INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE GLOBE. THE UNITED NATION'S FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL ORGANIZATION (2015) ESTIMATED THAT AGRICULTURE COLLECTIVELY ACCOUNTS FOR 40% OF THE CURRENT GLOBAL WORKFORCE. HOWEVER, TO MEET THE AFOREMENTIONED DEMANDS, MORE SKILLED LEADERS AND LABORERS MUST BE RECRUITED INTO THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR, WHICH WILL HAVE TO BE TRAINED THROUGH THE NATION'S LAND GRANT AND NON-LAND GRANT COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE. WITH THIS MIND THESE INSTITUTIONS WILL HAVE TO IDENTIFY MECHANISMS AND STRATEGIES TO ATTRACT POTENTIAL STUDENTS INTO THE ACADEMIC PROGRAMS THEY OFFER, SINCE DIRECT COMPETITION EXISTS FROM OTHER INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER LEARNING FOR STUDENT CLIENTELE.INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION ARE UNDER MOUNTING SCRUTINY AS THEY FACE REDUCED STUDENT ACCESS, RISING COSTS, AND CALLS TO DEMONSTRATE MORE PROFOUND OUTCOMES (BEALE, 2012; KRETOVICS, 2011). AS A RESULT, TRENDS REGARDING STUDENT ENTRANCE, RETENTION, AND GRADUATION WERE USED AS KEY INDICATORS OF INSTITUTIONAL SUCCESSES AND FAILURES. ALTHOUGH EXISTING EVIDENCE HAS REVEALED THAT SUCH METRICS ARE AFFECTED BY A NUMBER OF CONTEXTUAL FACTORS (ALLEN, ROBBINS, CASILLAS, & OH, 2008; SHRESTHA, SUVEDI, & FOSTER, 2011), THEY REMAIN OF CENTRAL IMPORTANCE TO UNIVERSITIES BECAUSE STUDENT DROPOUT RESULTS IN FEWER INDIVIDUALS PREPARED TO ENTER THE WORKFORCE AS WELL AS THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS IN UNREALIZED REVENUE FOR INSTITUTIONS (BEALE, 2012; KRETOVICS, 2011). ALSO, NOT COMPLETING A COLLEGE DEGREE HAS BEEN SHOWN TO NEGATIVELY AFFECT LEAVERS' SOCIAL, PHYSIOLOGICAL, AND ECONOMIC WELLBEING (BRUFFAERTS ET AL., 2018; PERVIN, REIK, & DALRYMPLE, 2015). FOR EXAMPLE, PREVIOUS RESEARCH HAS REPORTED STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS WHO DROP OUT OF COLLEGE AND THEIR SENSE OF SOCIAL ISOLATION AND DEPRESSION AS WELL AS A LOWER CAREER EARNING POTENTIAL (BRUFFAERTS ET AL., 2018; PERVIN ET AL., 2015). MOREOVER, WITH NATIONAL STUDENT LOAN DEBT TOPPING $1.5 TRILLION IN 2019, AND STUDENTS GRADUATING IN 2017 HAVING AN AVERAGE OF $28,650 IN LOANS, THE SUCCESS OF UNIVERSITIES AND STUDENTS REMAIN DEEPLY ENTWINED (FRIEDMAN, 2019).TO FURTHER COMPLICATE THIS ISSUE, NEARLY ALL AGRICULTURAL, FOOD, AND NATURAL RESOURCE (AFNR) SECTORS ARE EXPERIENCING A SHORTAGE OF QUALIFIED WORKERS (GOECKER ET AL., 2015). FOR INSTANCE, IT IS EXPECTED THAT MORE THAN 20,000 AFNR RELATED JOBS WILL GO UNFILLED BY AN UNQUALIFIED CANDIDATE IN 2020 (GOECKER ET AL., 2015). THEREFORE, IT IS IMPERATIVE TO IMPROVE THE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE TO ENSURE THAT QUALIFIED LEADERS SUPPLY THE AFNR CAREER PIPELINE IN THE FUTURE (NATIONAL RESEARCH COUNCIL, 2009; STEM FOOD AND AGRICULTURE COUNCIL, 2014). PREVIOUS RESEARCH ON THIS ISSUE, HOWEVER, HAS DEPICTED THE RIFT BETWEEN THE SUPPLY AND DEMAND OF AFNR GRADUATES AS AN ISSUE OF STUDENT RECRUITMENT (BAKER, SETTLE, CHIARELLI, & IRANI, 2013; KOON, FRICK, IGO, 2009; RAYFIELD, MURPHREY, & SKAGGS, 2013; ROCCA & WASHBURN, 2005; STAIR, DANJEAN, BLACKBURN, & BUNCH, 2016). HOWEVER, LESS ATTENTION IS PLACED ON THE ROLE THAT RETENTION PLAYS IN SOLVING THIS PROBLEM (DUNN, HAINES, & EPPS, 2013). IN RESPONSE, KOON ET AL. (2009) CALLED FOR COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE TO CONSIDER RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION AS FACTORS OF EQUAL VALUE. AS AN ILLUSTRATION, BY PLACING AN IMPROVED EMPHASIS ON RETENTION EFFORTS, COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE COULD BETTER ADDRESS THE NATIONAL STUDENT LOAN DEBT BY GRADUATING STUDENTS PROMPTLY WHILE ALSO KEEPING MORE INDIVIDUALS IN THE AFNR CAREER PIPELINE (KOON ET AL., 2009).PREVIOUS RESEARCH HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT TARGETED UNIVERSITY RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION PROGRAMMING CAN POSITIVELY INFLUENCE INDIVIDUALS' CHOICE TO PURSUE COLLEGE AS WELL AS THEIR DECISION TO PERSIST THROUGHOUT THEIR DEGREE PROGRAM (BOBBIT, 2006; ROCCA, 2013). IN PARTICULAR, THE LITERATURE ON RECRUITMENT FOR COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE HAS REPORTED THAT COMMUNICATING AND BUILDING RELATIONSHIPS WITH PARENTS IS CRITICAL BECAUSE THEY ARE HIGHLY INFLUENTIAL IN THEIR CHILD'S DECISION TO PURSUE A CAREER IN AGRICULTURE AS WELL AS THE PARTICULAR UNIVERSITY THEY WILL ULTIMATELY CHOOSE TO ATTEND (BOBBIT, 2006; RAYFIELD ET AL., 2013; ROCCA, 2013). HOWEVER, VARIABLES SUCH AS CAMPUS VISITS, COST, COMMUNICATION EFFORTS FROM COLLEGES AND DEPARTMENTS, DEPARTMENTAL ATMOSPHERE, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, FACULTY APPROACHABILITY, AND SCHOLARSHIP OPPORTUNITIES HAVE ALSO BEEN REPORTED TO INFLUENCE AGRICULTURE STUDENTS' DECISIONS (BAKER ET AL., 2013; RAYFIELD ET AL., 2013; ROCCA & WASHBURN, 2005; STAIR ET AL., 2016).

THIS PROJECT IS AN INTEGRATED PROPOSAL WITH THE PRIMARY FOCUS ON OUTREACH (EWE) FUNCTIONS TO SERVE SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED POPULATIONS. THE PROPOSED ABIC WILL ALSO SERVE AS A CONVENER TO SUPPORT REGIONAL AND NATIONAL PARTNERSHIP IN PROVIDING ACCESS TO PRIVATE VENTURE CAPITAL, DATA TRACKING AND ANALYSIS, EVALUATION, AND MEASUREMENT FOR EFFECTIVE PROGRAMMING IN OUTREACH. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS HBCU ABIC ARE TWOFOLD: (1) TO PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMS, FIRMS, AND INDIVIDUALS WITH INTERESTS IN AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN ENTREPRENEURIAL ACADEMY, WHICH WILL OFFER (A) A PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT CERTIFICATION PROGRAM PROVIDING ENTREPRENEURIAL TRAINING, CONSULTATION, WORKSHOPS, AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL RESOURCES AND ACTIVITIES, (B) A TOURNAMENT OF IDEAS COMPETITIVE SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM FOR SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMS, FIRMS, AND STUDENTS FOR BUSINESS STARTUP, MARKETING, AND FUNDRAISING ASSISTANCE, AND (C) A MODEL FOR SUPERVISED AGRIBUSINESS ENTREPRENEURSHIP BEYOND TRAINING TO INCUBATE BUSINESS IDEAS, AND (2) TO PROVIDE WORKFORCE-ORIENTED ENTREPRENEURIAL TRAINING THROUGH STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING PROGRAMS. positiveFlows.title: ** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY WILL COLLABORATE WITH ALABAMA A&M UNIVERSITY, SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY, FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY, AND LANGSTON UNIVERSITY TO HOST THE 1890 CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR NATURAL RESOURCES, RENEWABLE ENERGY, AND THE ENVIRONMENT (COE-NREE): A CLIMATE SMART APPROACH. THE PRIMARY GOALS AND THRUST AREAS OF THE COE-NREE ARE 1) NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION, 2) SUSTAINABLE ENERGY AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, 3) ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND EQUITY, AND 4) WORKFORCE TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT. THESE FOUR THRUST AREAS WILL PROVIDE COLLABORATIVE OPPORTUNITIES AMONG 1890 INSTITIUTIONS AND NOVEL APPROACHES TO TACKLE CONTEMPORARY ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES THAT IMPACT TERRESTRIAL AND AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS. THROUGH THIS COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH, THIS CENTER OF EXCELLENCE WILL DEVELOP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO CONSERVE AND PROMOTE NATURAL RESOURCES, EXPLORE RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES, AND DEVELOP CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION PRACTICES WITH THE AIM OF REDUCING CARBON DIOXIDE IN THE ATMOSPHERE AND IMPROVING THE ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND SUSTAINABILITY. THE COE-NREE WILL HOST A VARIETY OF TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, POST-DOCTORAL RESEARCH ASSOCIATES, AND FACULTY AVAILABLE FOR ALL 1890 INSTITUTIONS. WE WILL DEVELOP THESE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES WITH A VARIETY OF PROJECT PARTNERS, INCLUDING THE COUNCIL OF AMERICAN OVERSEAS RESEARCH CENTERS, NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION AGENCY, UNITED STATES GEOLOGICAL SURVEY, AND THE ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE ACADEMY. COLLECTIVELY, THE COE-NREE WILL PROVIDE A COLLABORATIVE OPPORTUNITY TO ADVANCE NOVEL SCIENCE AS IT RELATES TO GLOBAL CHANGE, WHICH WILL BENEFIT A VARIETY OF FEDERAL, STATE, NON-PROFIT AND PUBLIC STAKEHOLDERS.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE CENTER FOR FARMING SYSTEMS, RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY (CFSRPES) IS FOR 1890 LAND GRANT UNIVERSITIES (LGUS) TO DEVELOP, LEVERAGE AND SHARE BEST PRACTICES, INNOVATIONS, TECHNOLOGIES AND PERSONNEL ACROSS AN EIGHTEEN STATE REGION ADDRESS THE PROFITABILITY, SUSTAINABILITY AND PROSPERITY CHALLENGES OF SMALL FARMERS, RANCHERS AND FORESTLAND OWNERS (SFRLS). EMPHASIS IS PLACED ON SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERSERVED FARMERS. CFSRPES BUILDS ON AND INCORPORATES THE STRUCTURE AND LEARNINGS FROM THE CENTER FOR INNOVATION AND SUSTAINABILITY OF SMALL FARMS, RANCHES AND FORESTLANDS (CISFRL), AN 1890 CENTER OF EXCELLENCE CURRENTLY FUNDED BY USDA NIFA (2020-2022). CFSRPES USES AN INTEGRATIVE RESEARCH- EDUCATION-EXTENSION APPROACH WITH MULTIPLE DISCIPLINARY UNIVERSITY PARTNERSHIPS, PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR PARTNERSHIPS TO BENEFIT AND STRENGTHEN SFRLS AND ENGAGE AND EDUCATE STUDENTS IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES AT THE1890 LGUS. CFSRPES HAS FIVE THRUST AREA (THA) TEAMS WITH FOUR TO EIGHT MEMBERS PER TEAM FROM 19, 1890 LAND GRANT UNIVERSITIES. THE THA TEAMS ARE FARM COMMODITIES, PROCESSES AND SYSTEMS; RANCH COMMODITIES, PROCESSES AND SYSTEMS; FOREST COMMODITIES, PROCESSES AND SYSTEMS; VALUE ADDED TECHNOLOGY; AND INTEGRATED ENVIRONMENT, ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL IMPACTS. ALL THA TEAMS INCLUDE MARKETING AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP COMPONENTS. CROSS-THA AND INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATIONS ARE ENCOURAGED.

AFRICAN AMERICANS (AAS) REMAIN THE LEAST HEALTHY ETHNIC GROUP IN THE USA. DIET IS A KEY CONTRIBUTOR TO DISPARITIES IN MANY CHRONIC DISEASES AND CONDITIONS. AA COMMUNITIES HAVE TRUSTED THE 1890 INSTITUTIONS FOR MORE THAN A CENTURY, THEREFORE, THEY CAN PLAY IMPORTANT ROLES IN ASSISTING AAS TO COMBAT DIET-RELATED DISPARITIES ESPECIALLY OBESITY AND ITS RELATED CHRONIC DISEASES. ESTABLISHING AN 1890 CENTER OF EXCELLENCE (COE) FOR NUTRITION, HEALTH, WELLNESS, AND QUALITY OF LIFE IS VERY TIMELY AND WILL STRENGTHEN 1890 INSTITUTION'S CAPACITIES IN RESEARCH, TEACHING AND EXTENSION TO ADDRESS DIET-RELATED HEALTH DISPARITIES IN AAS. LOUISIANA, NORTH CAROLINA, AND ALABAMA ARE AMONG THE TOP 10 MOST OBESE STATES IN NON-HISPANIC BLACK ADULTS. SOUTHERN UNIVERSITY AND A&M COLLEGE, NORTH CAROLINA A&T STATE UNIVERSITY, AND TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY HAVE COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS IN RESEARCH, TEACHING, AND EXTENSION, AND ARE IN A UNIQUE POSITION TO WORK AS A TEAM TO ESTABLISH A COE, WHICH IS ON THE TRIPARTITE "LAND-GRANT" MISSION OF RESEARCH, TEACHING, AND EXTENSION TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF UNDERSERVED AND MINORITY POPULATIONS. THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS COE IS TO INCREASE THE CAPACITIES OF 1890 INSTITUTIONS TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITY THROUGH NUTRITION RESEARCH, TEACHING, AND EXTENSION. THE GLOBAL FOOD SYSTEM REMAINS VULNERABLE TO CHALLENGES POSED BY NEW PESTS, NATURAL DISASTERS AND EXTERNAL SHOCKS SUCH AS COVID-19. THE CENTER WILL FUND TEACHING, RESEARCH, EXTENSION, AND INTEGRATED PROJECTS DESIGNED TO SUPPLY THE COUNTRY WITH A GLOBALLY EDUCATED WORKFORCE AND SUPPORT CRITICAL NEEDS IN THE AREA OF GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND DEFENSE. MORE SPECIFICALLY, THE CEGFSD WILL SUPPORT PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS THE CENTER'S FOUR BROAD GOALS AS FOLLOWS: (1) STRENGTHEN AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT IN DEVELOPING COUNTRIES; (2) ADDRESS NEW AND EMERGING ANIMAL AND PLANT PESTS AND DISEASES; (3) ENGAGE IN AGRICULTURAL DISASTER RECOVERY; AND (4) CONTINUE THE EXISTING CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT'S ACTIVITIES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND EASTERN SHORE.

THE PROJECT "STRENGTHENING UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS LEARNING THROUGH IMPROVEMENT OF TEACHING ACTIVITIES" WILL ALSO STRENGTHEN INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITIES TO DEVELOP METHODS OF INSTRUCTION AND ENHANCE SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION.WE WANT TO RECRUIT HIGHLY QUALIFIED UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE HISPANIC STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: SUMMER WORKSHOPS; MENTORING PROGRAMS; INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING; SCIENTIFIC SYMPOSIUM PARTICIPATION; AND SCIENTIFIC ARTICLE WRITING.THE PROJECT WILL PROMOTE OPEN COMMUNICATION, THE EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION, AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESOURCES THAT ACCELERATE EDUCATION AND PLACEMENT OF HISPANICS INTO USDA OR OTHER FEDERAL AGENCIES ADDRESSING USDA PRIORITIES AMONG UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS.AS A RESULT, STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN THE PROJECT WILL ACQUIRE LEADERSHIP AND RESEARCH SKILLS AND WILL DEVELOP THE QUALITIES NEEDED THE NEW WORKFORCE.

WITH THE PROJECTED SHORTAGE OF GRADUATES (CSREES, 2005) TO FILL THE AVAILABLE POSITIONS (GOECKER, SMITH, FERNANDEZ, ALI, & THELLER, 2015) THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY NEEDS TO IDENTIFY AND PUT INTO PRACTICE METHODS TO RECRUIT A MORE DIVERSE AND WELL-PREPARED FANH WORKFORCE. A STUDY CONDUCTED BY MYERS, THORON, AND THOMPSON (2009) INVESTIGATED THE NEEDS OF THE NATIONAL AGRISCIENCE TEACHER AMBASSADORS WHO IDENTIFIED THE NEED FOR (1) CURRICULUM, (2) PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND (3) COLLABORATION IN AN EFFORT TO TEACH STEM CONCEPTS MORE EFFECTIVELY IN THEIR CLASSROOMS. THOSE THREE NEEDS ARE EACH A COMPONENT OF THIS PROPOSAL AS DETAILED BELOW.IN REGARDS TO CURRICULUM NEEDS, A SURVEY OF KANSAS AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION TEACHERS (N = 236) WAS CONDUCTED IN JANUARY 2017 TO DETERMINE THEIR LEVEL OF KNOWLEDGE, ABILITY, AND CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH ASSISTING THEIR STUDENTS WITH AGRISCIENCE RESEARCH. SEVENTY-NINE TEACHERS (33% RESPONSE RATE) COMPLETED THE SURVEY. ALMOST 30% OF THE RESPONDENTS HAD NOT PERFORMED THEIR OWN RESEARCH PROJECT AND NEARLY 50% HAD ONLY PERFORMED A RESEARCH PROJECT WHEN THEY THEMSELVES WERE A SECONDARY STUDENT. WHEN ASKED IF THEIR COLLEGE EDUCATION ADEQUATELY PREPARED THEM TO CONDUCT RESEARCH 40 (51%) DISAGREED OR WERE NEUTRAL. ADDITIONALLY, 73% OF THE RESPONDENTS DID NOT CURRENTLY HAVE ANY STUDENTS CONDUCTING RESEARCH.PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WAS ANOTHER NEED IDENTIFIED IN THE MYERS, THORON, AND THOMPSON (2009) STUDY. IT IS CRUCIAL THAT FUTURE SCIENTISTS ARE ABLE TO TRANSFER THEIR CLASSROOM LEARNING TO REAL-WORLD SETTINGS. IN AN EFFORT TO HELP STUDENTS MAKE THOSE CONNECTIONS, AGRICULTURE TEACHERS NEED TO BE TRAINED IN STRATEGIES TO USE WHEN TEACHING EMPLOYABILITY SKILLS FOR FUTURE FANH SCIENTISTS (HUGHES & BARRICK, 1993). THE WORKSHOP PLANNED IN YEAR TWO OF THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THE NEED FOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDE SUPPORT FOR BOTH THE RESEARCH SCIENTISTS AND THE SECONDARY AGRICULTURE TEACHERS. COMPONENTS OF THE MENTORING WORKSHOP WILL FOCUS ON CONTENT, LINKING PREVIOUS KNOWLEDGE TO NEW CONCEPTS, AND RELATIONSHIP BUILDING (DESIMONE, 2009). ADDITIONALLY, TIME FOR THE COMPLETION OF RESEARCH STUDIES COULD BE CREATED IF THE AGRICULTURE TEACHERS WERE MORE COMFORTABLE INTEGRATING SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS INTO THEIR EXISTING CURRICULUM.RESEARCH IN KANSAS, OKLAHOMA, AND IDAHO CAN BE INTERPRETED TO JUSTIFY THAT TEACHERS ARE INTERESTED IN THE FFA AGRISCIENCE FAIR PROGRAM BUT DO NOT FEEL COMFORTABLE WITH THE NUANCES OF CONDUCTING A SCIENTIFIC EXPERIMENT. THEREFORE, THEY DO NOT ENCOURAGE OR SUPPORT THEIR STUDENTS WITH THEIR OWN RESEARCH PROJECTS. SIMILARLY, IDAHO HAS HAD LIMITED PARTICIPATION IN THE IDAHO FFA AGRISCIENCE FAIR, WITH FEWER THAN 15 PARTICIPANTS EACH YEAR FOR THE PAST FOUR YEARS. TEACHERS IN IDAHO HAVE EXPRESSED CONCERN THAT THEY DO NOT KNOW HOW TO MOTIVATE STUDENTS TO ENGAGE IN THE FFA AGRISCIENCE FAIR. THIS EXPLORATORY DATA SERVES AS A GOOD FOUNDATION TO ESTABLISH THE NEED OF THIS RESEARCH PROPOSALAND THE IMPORTANCE OF PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS.FINALLY, THERE IS A NEED FOR COLLABORATION IN AN EFFORT TO CREATE NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND STRENGTHEN RELATIONSHIPS, BECAUSE "A STRONGER RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AND WITHIN YOUTH, ADULTS, AND OTHER COMMUNITY ENTITIES STRENGTHENS COMMUNITIES" (GRAHAM, ARNOLD & JAYARATNE, 2016, P. 50). THE NATIONAL RESEARCH COUNCIL (2009A) ALSO ENCOURAGED MORE COLLABORATIONS AND PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN UNIVERSITIES AND SECONDARY STUDENTS AND TEACHERS, INCLUDING FFA MEMBERS. THERE ARE A NUMBER OF COLLABORATIONS AT WORK IN THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL.PAIRING SCHOOL-BASED AGRICULTURE PROGRAMS WITH UNIVERSITY RESEARCH CENTERS WILL BUILD THE FOUNDATION FOR LOCAL MENTORS WHO CAN INCREASE PARTICIPATION BY SHARING THEIR EXPERTISE AND CAN BUILD MOTIVATION BY HELPING STUDENTS BE SUCCESSFUL. AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS IDENTIFIED SOFT SKILLS THAT ARE VITAL IN FUTURE EMPLOYEES (CRAWFORD, LANG, FINK, DALTON, & FIELITZ, 2011) AND PLACED THEM IN 7 CLUSTERS: 1) EXPERIENCES,2) TEAM, 3) COMMUNICATION, 4) LEADERSHIP, 5) DECISION MAKING/PROBLEM-SOLVING, 6) SELF-MANAGEMENT, 7) PROFESSIONALISM. THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECT WILL ALLOW SECONDARY AGRICULTURE STUDENTS TO DEVELOP IN EACH OF THE SEVEN CLUSTER AREAS AS THEY WORK WITH RESEARCH SCIENTISTS.STUDENTS' ABILITY TO LINK THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF CONCEPTS TO NEW IDEAS AND APPLICATIONS IS CRITICAL (NATIONAL RESEARCH COUNCIL, 2012). STUDENTS NEED HELP AND ASSISTANCE IN LEARNING TRANSFERABLE SKILLS SUCH AS INTERPERSONAL COMMUNICATION, CRITICAL THINKING, PROBLEM SOLVING, WRITING, AND COMPUTING (NATIONAL RESEARCH COUNCIL, 2009B). THE COLLABORATION AMONG THE SECONDARY STUDENTS, AGRICULTURE TEACHERS, AND RESEARCH SCIENTISTS WILL HELP FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE CRUCIAL EMPLOYABILITY SKILLS AND BEHAVIORS.COLLABORATION BETWEEN THE THREE UNIVERSITY FACULTY MEMBERS ON THIS GRANT PROPOSAL WILL ENCOURAGE THE CREATION OF THIS INNOVATIVE PRACTICE, MENTORING GUIDES, AND COMMUNICATION TOOLS. WE WILL ALSO SHARE BEST PRACTICES AS WE WORK WITH THE RESEARCH CENTER SCIENTISTS. AN ESSENTIAL COLLABORATIVE EFFORT WILL OCCUR DURING THIS PROJECT AS WE WORK TO COLLABORATE WITH THE POPULATIONS SURROUNDING THE UNIVERSITY RESEARCH CENTERS. USDA RECOGNIZES THE NEED FOR A DIVERSE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE. "DIVERSE EXPERIENCES, BACKGROUND AND EDUCATION ARE VITAL TO A HEALTHY AGRICULTURAL SECTOR THAT CONTINUES TO MEET THE CHALLENGES OF A CHANGING WORLD AND THE DEMANDS OF MARKETS AT HOME AND ABROAD" (USDA ANNOUNCES..., 2016, PARA. 8). TO HELP MEET THE NEED FOR A DIVERSE AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE, YOUNG PEOPLE NEED TO BE EXPOSED AND ENCOURAGED TO PURSUE A CAREER IN THE FANH INDUSTRY. "ENGAGING YOUNG PEOPLE IN THESE FIELDS NOW IS AN INVESTMENT IN THE FUTURE OF AMERICA'S ECONOMIC HEALTH AND SECURITY" (USDA ANNOUNCES..., 2016, PARA. 8). EACH OF THE PARTNERING STATES, AND THUS THE REGIONAL RESEARCH CENTERS, SERVE DIVERSE POPULATIONS.AS WE WORK TO GROW THE NUMBER OF FANH SCIENTISTS, WE NEED TO CONSIDER HOW PEOPLE MAKE CAREER CHOICE DECISIONS. LEARNING EXPERIENCES, SKILLS, GENETIC ENDOWMENT AND SPECIAL ABILITIES CAN ALL INFLUENCE CAREER CHOICE (MITCHELL & KRUMBOLTZ, 1990). THIS GENERATION OF STUDENT WANTS TO "FEEL IMPORTANT" AND "BELIEVE THAT THEY ARE MAKING A PERSONAL IMPACT" (TWENGE, 2014, P. 271). THIS RESEARCH PROPOSAL WOULD ENABLE YOUTH TO TAKE OWNERSHIP OF THEIR OWN RESEARCH PROJECT, DEVELOP A WORKING RELATIONSHIP WITH A RESEARCH SCIENTIST, AND HELP IMPROVE THEIR LOCAL AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITY WITH RELEVANT RESEARCH PROJECTS.

PUERTO RICO HAS ABOUT 4 MILLION SQUARE FEET IN VACANT INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES RESULTING FROM A REDUCTION IN MANUFACTURING ECONOMIC ACTIVITY. PR NEEDS TO RETHINK THE USE OF THIS PHYSICAL CAPITAL. WITH A SMALL INVESTMENT, ALL THESE INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES CAN BECOME PRODUCTIVE AGAIN, BUT IN THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. INDOOR CROP PRODUCTION (ICP) SPECIFICALLY REFERS TO THE USE OF AN ENCLOSED, CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT SYSTEM USED TO GROW CROPS WITHOUT THE USE OF SOLAR LIGHT (OR SUPPLEMENTING SOLAR LIGHT WITH AN ARTIFICIAL SOURCE). SUCH AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY HAS BEEN SUCCESSFULLY ADOPTED IN THE USA, AND OTHER COUNTRIES, WITH DOCUMENTED ADVANTAGES SUCH AS DECREASED HAND LABOR, REDUCED FLOOR SPACE, MINIMAL LOSES DUE TO PATHOGENS AND/OR INSECTS, AND INCREASE IN HARVEST CYCLES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT SEEKS TO GAIN HANDS-ON UNDERSTANDING OF ICP TECHNOLOGY AND DETERMINE ITS ECONOMIC FEASIBILITY FOR PUERTO RICO. THIS IS ACHIEVED BY INSTALLING COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE ICP TECHNOLOGY AND ESTABLISHING THE ICPLAB AT UPRM. THE FACILITY WILL BE OPERATED TO PRODUCE LETTUCE (I.E., TROPICANA VARIETY), A WELL UNDERSTOOD CROP, SO THAT EFFORTS CAN FOCUS ON OPTIMIZATION OF SYSTEMS PARAMETERS. ULTIMATELY, THE PROJECT SHOULD PROVE THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH ICP CAN BE PROFITABLE FOR PUERTO RICO AGRICULTURE. SUCH UNDERSTANDING SHALL ENABLE THE USE OF VACANT INDUSTRIAL FACILITIES TO PRODUCE CROPS.
