negativeFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROMOTE ADVANCES IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN FANH SCIENCES THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY. TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE THROUGH THE AGRICULTURE EXPERIENCE TRACKER, ADOPTED BY THE NATIONAL FFA ORGANIZATION AND 48 STATE FFA ASSOCIATIONS, WILL CREATE A TRANSFERABLE CERTIFICATE PATHWAY ALIGNED TO SOFT SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AND CAREER READINESS PRACTICES. HIGH SCHOOL AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION TEACHERS ARE ACCUSTOMED TO THE CAREER TECHNICAL EDUCATION (CTE) PATHWAY THAT PROVIDES FANH CURRICULUM FOR DEVELOPMENT OF HARD SKILLS, SUCH AS PLANT SCIENCE, ANIMALS SCIENCE, AND AGRICULTURE MECHANICS. THESE ESTABLISHED PATHWAYS ALIGN WITH CTE PATHWAYS ESTABLISHED AT THE COMMUNITY COLLEGE LEVEL AND TO AGRICULTURAL MAJORS AT THE UNIVERSITY LEVEL. ADDING THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY AS A COMPANION TO THE CTE PATHWAY, WILL BRING AWARENESS TO THE IMPORTANCE OF ACQUIRING BOTH SETS OF SKILLS: HARD SKILLS AND SOFT SKILLS. THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATION PATHWAY IS A FOCUSED STRATEGY AIMED TO CREATE A SYSTEM-WIDE PATHWAY (HIGH SCHOOL TO UNIVERSITY) TO EMPOWER STUDENTS' SUCCESS AND PREPAREDNESS TO BECOME THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL LEADERS THROUGH COLLABORATIONS WITH THE AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY, FACULTY, AND LEADERS IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION. EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EXPERIENCES SHARED WITH FELLOW CLASSMATES, COLLABORATION WITH ACRS21 ADVISORY COMMITTEE, AND INTERACTION WITH THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY WILL PROMOTE STUDENT DISCOVERY, DIVERSITY, AND DISTINCTION AS THEY PROGRESS THROUGH THE CERTIFICATE PATHWAY (I.E. THE STATED CORE VALUES OF FRESNO STATE). EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING WILL ADVANCE INCLUSIVE RELATIONSHIPS THAT FOSTER PERSONAL PASSION, POTENTIAL AND A SENSE OF BELONGING. THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY SUPPORTS FRESNO STATE'S OWN INSTITUTIONAL STRATEGIC PLAN IN ALL FOUR-PRIORITY AREAS. PRIORITY ONE- ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL DEVELOP SOFT SKILLS AND CAREER READINESS SKILLS FOR MORE HSI STUDENTS WHO WILL HAVE ACCESS TO CO-CURRICULAR SERVICES THAT PROMOTE STUDENT ENGAGEMENT AND A SENSE OF BELONGING. PRIORITY TWO- NATIONAL, STATE, AND REGIONAL WORKSHOPS WILL PROVIDE ADDITIONAL TRAINING, LEADERSHIP, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FACULTY AND STAFF MEMBERS. PRIORITY THREE- TEACHING MODULES, STUDENT SELF-ASSESSMENTS, AND THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL BE MANAGED ONLINE THROUGH THE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIENCE TRACKER (AET), THEAET.COM, AND THE DIGITAL AGRICULTURE SOLUTION HUB (DASH) WEBSITES. PURSUING ACRS21 CERTIFICATES WILL PROMOTE STUDENT INVOLVEMENT IN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES AND, THEREBY, CONTRIBUTE TO A HEALTHIER, MORE SUSTAINABLE CAMPUS ENVIRONMENT. PRIORITY FOUR- PARTNERSHIPS CREATED THROUGH ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY WILL TRACK STUDENT INVOLVEMENT FROM HIGH SCHOOL TO COMMUNITY COLLEGE AND/OR UNIVERSITY. WEB-BASED TECHNOLOGY WILL TRACK STUDENT PROJECTS, SERVICE-LEARNING, JOB SHADOWING, INTERNSHIPS, AND STUDENT GROWTH IN PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT. FIVE TO TEN YEARGOALS PROJECT THAT 35,460 STUDENTS, INCLUDING 17,185 UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS, WILL BE IMPACTED BY THE ACRS21 CERTIFICATE PATHWAY: 35,000 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, 1517 TEACHERS, 450 UNDERGRADUATE, AND 10 GRADUATE STUDENTS.THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE (NIFA) SEEKS TO PROMOTE AND STRENGTHEN THE ABILITY OF HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTIONS (HSI) TO CARRY OUT HIGHER EDUCATION PROGRAMS THAT ATTRACT, RETAIN, AND GRADUATE OUTSTANDING STUDENTS CAPABLE OF ENHANCING THE NATION'S FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN SCIENCE PROFESSIONAL AND SCIENTIFIC WORK FORCE (GRANT EXECUTIVE SUMMARY). THIS GOAL MIRRORS THE STRATEGIC GOALS OF FRESNO STATE. ADDITIONALLY, JCAST SEEKS TO ENHANCE THE ABILITY OF STUDENTS TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THEIR CAREERS AND MAKE POSITIVE CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE QUALITY OF LIFE IN THEIR COMMUNITIES (JCAST HOME PAGE). THIS PROJECT'S OBJECTIVES WILL BE REFLECTIVE OF NIFA'S GOAL, JCAST'S GOAL, AND FRESNO STATE'S STRATEGIC GOALS.

ARKANSAS IS KNOWN AS THE BIRTHPLACE OF WARM WATER AQUACULTURE IN THE UNITED STATES. TODAY THE AQUACULTURE INDUSTRY IN ARKANSAS HAS EXPANDED TO INCLUDE OVER 20 SPECIES OF FISH AND SHELLFISH. ARKANSAS IS RANKED SECOND IN TOTAL AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION AND RANKS FIRST IN THE PRODUCTION OF BAITFISH, SPORTFISH, LARGEMOUTH BASS, HYBRID STRIPED BASS FRY, AND CHINESE CARP. IN SUMMERY AQUACULTURE HAS HAD A MAJOR IMPACT IN ARKANSAS, ESPECIALLY IN THE DELTA, WHERE THE MAJORITY OF AQUACULTURE PRODUCTION OCCURS. OF THE TWO LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES IN THE STATE OF ARKANSAS, THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF (UAPB) HAS THE ONLY AQUACULTURE/FISHERIES CENTER OF EXCELLENCE (AQFI) IN THE STATE. WE ARE THE ONLY STATE-SUPPORTED INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION IN ARKANSAS THAT HAS STATEWIDE RESPONSIBILITY FOR BOTH RESEARCH AND EXTENSION IN AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES. AS WE MOVE THROUGH THE 21ST CENTURY, A PROMINENT ADVANCEMENT IN AQUACULTURE HAS BEEN THE USE OF SELECTIVE BREEDING, STRAIN SELECTION, PLOIDY MANIPULATIONS, GENETICS, AND GENOMICS TO BOOST CROP PRODUCTIVITY AND QUALITY. A FOUNDATIONAL COMPONENT OF THE ABOVE-MENTIONED TECHNOLOGIES IS REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY OF FISH (RPF). THE MAIN FRESHWATER AQUACULTURE PRODUCING STATES (MISSISSIPPI, ARKANSAS, ALABAMA, LOUISIANA, AND TEXAS), ALL HAVE MAJOR UNIVERSITIES WITH AQUACULTURE RESEARCH PROGRAMS AFFILIATED WITH THE INDUSTRY. AUBURN UNIVERSITY IN AL, MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY IN MS, LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY IN LA, TEXAS A&M IN TX, AND OF COURSE UAPB IN AR. OF THE ABOVE-MENTIONED AQUACULTURE PROGRAMS, UAPB IS THE ONLY ONE THAT LACKS A REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY, FISH BREEDING OR AN AQUACULTURE GENETICS PROGRAM. UAPB DOES NOT HAVE THE TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE OR RESOURCES DEVOTED TOWARDS A FISH REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY, HATCHERY MANAGEMENT, SELECTIVE BREEDING OR A GENETICS PROGRAM. THIS LACK OF TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE TO CONDUCT RESEARCH ON THE REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY OF FISHES AT UAPB IS A GLARING DEFICIENCY. THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT WILL INVOLVE RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION AT UAPB. IT WILL ENHANCE SUSTAINABLE AQUACULTURE THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH CAPACITY IN REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY OF FISHES. THE RESEARCH COMPONENT WILL INVOLVE XENOGENEICS, A NOVEL METHOD INVOLVING GERM CELL TRANSFER AND TRANSPLANTATION TECHNOLOGY TO PRODUCE BLACK CRAPPIE X WHITE CRAPPIE HYBRID FRY. THE CRAPPIE IS OF GREAT INTEREST AND COMMERCIAL IMPORTANCE TO THE SPORT-FISH INDUSTRY WITHIN ARKANSAS AND THE US. THE MAJOR OBSTACLE TO SUCCESSFUL CULTURE AND STOCKING OF CRAPPIE IS THEIR EXTREMELY HIGH REPRODUCTION RATE, WHICH CAN SOON LEAD TO OVERCROWDING AND STUNTING IN COMMERCIAL AQUACULTURE. HYBRID CRAPPIE ARE THE FIRST GENERATION CROSS BETWEEN A BLACK CRAPPIE MALE AND A WHITE CRAPPIE FEMALE. THIS RESULTING HYBRID DISPLAYS LIMITED REPRODUCTION AND INCREASED GROWTH. RESEARCH INDICATES THAT F1 HYBRID CRAPPIE GROWS FASTER AND WEIGH MORE THAN BOTH BLACK CRAPPIE AND WHITE CRAPPIE. HYBRIDS HAVE BEEN KNOWN TO GET AS LARGE AS 3 LBS., DEPENDING ON AVAILABLE FORAGE AND FEED. THE CURRENT METHOD OF HYBRID CRAPPIE PRODUCTION INVOLVES HORMONE INDUCED ARTIFICIAL SPAWNING TECHNIQUES. IN THIS METHOD, FEMALE WHITE CRAPPIE ARE INDUCED TO OVULATE WITH THE USE OF A SPAWNING AID. THE EGGS ARE HAND STRIPPED AND COLLECTED. AS MALE CRAPPIE DO NOT RELEASE THEIR SPERM WHEN STRIPPED BY HAND, BLACK CRAPPIE MALES ARE EUTHANIZED, THE TESTES ARE REMOVED AND MACERATED, AND THEN THE TESTICULAR MATERIAL IS MIXED WITH THE EGGS. WATER IS ADDED, AND THE SPERM AND EGGS ARE MIXED TO FERTILIZE. THIS ARTIFICIAL SPAWNING PROCEDURE IS LABOR AND TIME CONSUMING, CAN BE COSTLY, HAVE HIGH EMBRYONIC MORTALITY RATES AND LOW HATCH RATES. IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL PROVIDE AN INNOVATIVE METHOD FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HYBRID CRAPPIE VIA NATURAL SPAWNING. OUR GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A PROTOCOL FOR THE INTERSPECIFIC TRANSFER OF PRIMORDIAL GERM CELLS (PGCS) BETWEEN THE TWO DIFFERENT SPECIES OF CRAPPIE. WE WILL INVESTIGATE TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PRODUCTION OF HYBRID CRAPPIE: FIRST BY TRANSPLANTING BLACK CRAPPIE PGCS INTO TRIPLOID WHITE CRAPPIE MALES SO THAT THEY PRODUCE BLACK CRAPPIE SPERM, AND MATING THEM WITH NORMAL WHITE CRAPPIE FEMALES. THE SECOND APPROACH WILL BE TO TRANSPLANT WHITE CRAPPIE PGCS INTO TRIPLOID BLACK CRAPPIE FEMALES SO THAT THEY PRODUCE WHITE CRAPPIE EGGS, AND MATING THEM WITH NORMAL BLACK CRAPPIE MALES. IF SUCCESSFUL, EITHER OF THESE APPROACHES WOULD RESULT IN THE DESIRED HYBRID THROUGH NATURAL SPAWNING IN CULTURE PONDS. OUR APPROACH IS FIRST TO PRODUCE STERILE WHITE CRAPPIE MALE AND STERILE BLACK CRAPPIE FEMALE HOSTS. STERILITY WILL BE ACHIEVED BY TRIPLOIDIZATION. NEXT DONOR PGC STEM CELLS WILL BE OBTAINED FROM JUVENILE BLACK AND WHITE CRAPPIE BY HARVESTING THEM FROM THEIR GONADS. THE HARVESTED CELLS WILL BE ISOLATED, PROCESSED AND TAGGED SO THAT PGCS CAN BE IDENTIFIED. THE PGC'S WILL THEN BE CRYOPRESERVED FOR LONG-TERM STORAGE, OR TRANSPLANTED INTO THE GONADS OF THE STERILE TRIPLOID HOSTS. BLACK CRAPPIE PGC'S WILL BE TRANSPLANTEDINTO TRIPLOID WHITE CRAPPIE MALES AND WHITE CRAPPIE PGCS INTO TRIPLOID BLACK CRAPPIE FEMALES. THIS TRANSPLANTATION OF PGCS INTO THE HOST SHOULD REESTABLISH THE FERTILITY OF THE XENOGENEIC HOST. HOWEVER, THE HOST WILL PRODUCE GAMETES (EGGS AND SPERM) THAT OF THE DONOR. THE SUCCESS OF THE XENOGENEIC TRANSPLANTATION WILL BE EVALUATED BY LOOKING FOR THE PRESENCE OF THE TAGGED VIABLE PGC, 30,60 AND 90 DAYS POST IMPLANTATION BY SACRIFICING 2-3 FISH, DISSECTING THE GONADS, AND CHECKING FOR THE PRESENCE OF FLUORESCENCE OR BY USING REAL-TIME PCR (QPCR) TO DETECT THE PRESENCE OF DONOR GENETIC MATERIAL. CONFIRMATION OF XENOGENESIS WILL BE DONE BY INDUCED SPAWNING OF THE XENOGENIC BROODSTOCKS. SPERM FROM XENOGENEIC WHITE CRAPPIE MALES WILL BE USED TO FERTILIZE EGGS FROM WHITE CRAPPIE FEMALES, AND EGGS FROM XENOGENEIC BLACK CRAPPIE FEMALES WILL BE FERTILIZED WITH BLACK CRAPPIE MALE SPERM. THE PRODUCTION OF BLACK CRAPPIE X WHITE CRAPPIE, HYBRID FRY FROM EITHER OF THESE CROSSES WILL CONFIRM SUCCESSFUL XENOGENESIS. THE FOLLOW UP TO THIS WILL BE NATURAL RACEWAY OR POND SPAWNING OF THE XENOGENEIC BROODSTOCK WITH THEIR CONSPECIFICS TO PRODUCE A NATURALLY SPAWNED F1 HYBRID CRAPPIE POPULATION. A GOAL FOR THE FINAL YEAR OF THIS PROJECT WOULD BE TO ISOLATE CRAPPIE PGCS WITHOUT TAGGING THEM WITH GREEN FLUORESCENT PROTEIN (GFP). WE HOPE TO CHARACTERIZE IN DETAIL PGCS ISOLATED USING GFP TO IDENTIFY A DISTINCTIVE CHARACTERISTIC (I.E., SIZE, VOLUME OR OPTICAL DENSITY) THAT CAN BE USED AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO GFP. THIS WOULD BE A UNIQUE METHOD TO IDENTIFY AND ISOLATE PGCS IN CRAPPIE WITH THE POTENTIAL OF BEING USED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH WITH ANOTHER TELEOST. IF OUR PROTOCOL FOR THE PRODUCTION OF THE CRAPPIE HYBRID IS SUCCESSFUL, THIS WILL REPRESENT THE FIRST APPLICATION OF THIS BREAKTHROUGH TECHNOLOGY IN SPORT-FISH. AS THIS IS A RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INTEGRATED PROJECT, DIFFERENT STAGES OF SEED PRODUCTION, TRIPLOID PRODUCTION, HYBRID PRODUCTION AND NATURAL POND SPAWNING WILL BE DONE IN COLLABORATION WITH FISH PRODUCERS AND INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS. THE OUTCOMES FROM THIS PROJECT WILL BE DISSEMINATED VIA A SERIES OF PUBLICATIONS, POSTERS, AND PRESENTATIONS. THE OUTCOMES FROM THE RESEARCH COMPONENTS OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE PRESENTED AND DISSEMINATED TO THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY BY PUBLISHING THE RESULTS, PROTOCOLS, AND DATA IN PEER-REVIEWED SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS. SEPARATE COMPONENTS OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL BE SUBMITTED TO DIFFERENT JOURNALS BASED ON THEIR TARGET AUDIENCE AND FOCUSED DISCIPLINE. EXTENSION COMPONENTS WILL BE DISSEMINATED VIA EXTENSION PUBLICATION AND WILL TARGET LOCAL AQUAFARMERS, PRODUCERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS. UAPB EXTENSION PROGRAM WILL ALSO PUBLISH SEVERAL FACT SHEETS AND MANUALS ON THE PRODUCTION OF HYBRID CRAPPIE AND XENOGENIC CRAPPIE. THE ESTABLISHMENT OF DEMONSTRATION SITES AT UAPB AND SEVERAL COMMERCIAL AQUACULTURE FACILITIES WITHIN ARKANSAS WILL ALSO AID IN THE DISSEMINATION OF INFORMATION.

NANO-ENABLED AGRICULTURAL FERTILIZERS AND PESTICIDES HAVE A GREATER POTENTIAL FOR DIRECT, MASSIVE INTRODUCTION OF MANMADE NANOMATERIALS INTO THE ENVIRONMENT THAN ANY OTHER USE OF NANOPARTICLES. HOWEVER, OUR CURRENT UNDERSTANDING OF NANOMATERIAL FATE AND TRANSPORT IN THE AGRICULTURE ENVIRONMENT REMAINS LIMITED. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS DEVELOP AN INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROGRAM TO GAIN INSIGHT INTO THE PHYSICAL, CHEMICAL AND BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES THAT CONTROLLED BY PROPERTIES OF NANOPARTICLE, SUCH AS SIZE, COATING AND AGING. THE RESEARCH IS STRUCTURED AROUND FOUR TASKS: 1, DETERMINATION OF NANOPARTICLE DISSOLUTION RATES AS A FUNCTION OF SURFACE SIZE, COATING AND AGING EFFECT; 2, ELUCIDATION OF KEY ASPECTS OF NANOPARTICLE-PLANT-SOIL INTERACTIONS IN RHIZOSPHERE SOIL; 3, IDENTIFICATION OF THE FUNDAMENTAL PROCESSES CONTROLLING NANOPARTICLES TOXICITY TO SOIL MICROBE IN AGRICULTURAL SOILS; 4, EVALUATION OF THE FUNDAMENTAL PROCESSES CONTROLLING NANOPARTICLES RETENTION IN DYNAMIC TRANSPORT SYSTEM IN AGRICULTURAL SOILS. THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED THROUGH THIS PROJECT REGARDING THE RISKS RELATED TO UTILIZING NANO ENABLED AGROCHEMICALS WILL PLAY A KEY ROLE IN GUIDE NANOPARTICLES SAFE DESIGN, ADMINISTRATION, REGULATION AND RESPONSIBLE APPLICATION. INTEGRATED WITH PLANT SCIENCE, SOIL SCIENCE AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMISTRY PROGRAMS, SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL INCREASE UAPB'S RESEARCH CAPACITY ON NANO ENABLED AGRICULTURE DEVELOPMENT FOR SUSTAINABILITY.

positiveFlows.title: THE RAPID DEVELOPMENT OF PLANT-BASED FOODS HAS PROVIDED OPPORTUNITIES FOR GROWERS TO EXPLORE NEW STRATEGIES FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION WITH POSITIVE ECOLOGICAL AND ECONOMIC IMPACTS. THE MAIN GOAL OF THIS INTEGRATED EDUCATION (EP) AND RESEARCH (EQ) PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH AN AI-DRIVEN PRODUCTION MODALITY TO CONVERT GRAIN PEAS CURRENTLY USED PRIMARILY AS AN ANIMAL FEED IN NORTH CAROLINA INTO PEA PROTEIN ISOLATE THEREBY CREATING AND PROVIDING AN ADDITIONAL INCOME STREAM FOR THE GROWERS. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT SEEKS TO SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE THE FOOD SCIENCE EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM AT NC A&T BY INTEGRATING BOTH FOUNDATIONAL AI AND APPLIED AI TEACHING MODULES INTO THE CORE CURRICULUM. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE 1) ENABLING AI-ASSISTED PEA PROTEIN EXTRACTION AND IMPROVEMENT OF THE FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF PEA PROTEIN INCLUDING MACHINE LEARNING-BASED OPTIMIZATION OF ULTRASONIC EXTRACTION OF PEA PROTEIN AND PH-SHIFTING AND SONICATION COMBINED TREATMENT TO MODIFY FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF PEA PROTEIN ISOLATE; 2) AI-ENABLED OPTIMIZATION OF NON-THERMAL PEA PROTEIN DRYING PROCESS FOR ENERGY REDUCTION AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVING A DYNAMIC REAL-TIME SEQUENTIAL DECISION-MAKING OPTIMIZATION EMPOWERED BY DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING ALGORITHMS AND DIGITAL TWIN; AND 3) TRAINING OF NEXT-GENERATION FOOD TECHNOLOGISTS WITH ENHANCED AI CAPACITY. BY WORKING WITH A COMPUTER SCIENTIST AND NC A&T AND A COMPUTATIONAL ENGINEER AT UNIVERSITY OF ILLINOIS WE WILL DEVELOP TEACHING MODULES COVERING FOUNDATIONAL AI CONCEPTS IN FOOD CHEMISTRY FOOD MICROBIOLOGY AND FOOD PROCESSING COURSES AS WELL AS TO CREATE CASE STUDIES THAT DEMONSTRATE REAL-WORLD APPLICATION OF AI UTILIZING THE WORK RELATED TO OPTIMIZATION OF PEA PROTEIN PRODUCTION. THE MAJOR OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WOULD BE AN INCREASED NUMBER OF SKILLED WORKFORCES THAT SUPPORT EXECUTIVE ORDER FOR EXCELLENCE AND INNOVATION AT HBCU.

positiveFlows.title: THE INCREASING IMPACTS OF DISASTROUS WEATHER ON AGRICULTURE PRODUCERS' LIVELIHOODS AND FOOD SECTORS ALONG WITH PROJECTED US POPULATION GROWTH HIGHLIGHT THE NEED TO TRAIN THE NEXT-GENERATION WORKFORCE. THIS WORKFORCE MUST ADDRESS AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SECURITY ISSUES USING SCIENCE-DRIVEN APPROACHES AND ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES LIKE AI AND REMOTE SENSING. THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE 1890 AND 1862 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS TO ENGAGE RECRUIT RETAIN TRAIN AND SUPPORT STUDENTS AND ENHANCING THE WORKFORCE IN FOOD AGRICULTURE NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN SCIENCES (FANH) BY: 1) PROVIDING UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS FROM ALL COMMUNITIES WITH AN 8-WEEK EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING (ELP) AND OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT PROJECT (OEP) IN EXTENSION AND APPLIED RESEARCH THROUGH THE PAID EXTENSION SCHOLAR PROGRAM (ESP); 2) ESTABLISHING A STUDENT COHORT FROM ALL COMMUNITIES TO ENHANCE KNOWLEDGE OF FANH CAREERS CAREER/LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT SKILLS AND EXPOSURE TO GLOBAL AGRICULTURE IN AN INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE WITH PARTNERSHIP WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF BELIZE; 3) PAID STUDENT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM (SSP) WITH 3-CREDITS FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS FROM ALL COMMUNITIES PARTICIPATING IN A 10-WEEK EXTENSION SCHOLAR PROGRAM (INCLUDING 8-WEEK INTERNSHIP); AND 4) HANDS-ON OEP EXPERIENCES FOR MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL YOUTH TO INTRODUCE THEM TO VARIOUS FANH CAREERS. WE EXPECT TO TRAIN 30 UNDERGRADUATE EXTENSION SCHOLARS, 15 HIGH SCHOOL EXTENSION SCHOLARS (DSU ONLY) AND OVER 500 HIGH- AND MIDDLE-SCHOOL STUDENTS FROM GENERAL POPULATIONS. THE STEP FORWARD TRAINING WILL INCREASE RECRUITMENT RETENTION AND GRADUATION OF STUDENTS AND BETTER EQUIP THE FUTURE WORKFORCE FOR CHALLENGING JOB MARKETS AND HIGH-PAID CAREERS IN FANH DISCIPLINES VIA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAMS ACTIVITIES COOPERATIVE RESEARCH TECHNOLOGY APPLICATION AND GLOBAL TRAINING. THE MAJOR OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WOULD BE AN INCREASED NUMBER OF SKILLED WORKFORCES AND ENHANCED ENROLLMENT AND RECRUITMENT IN FANH. THIS WOULD ADDRESS THE AMERICAN FIRST GOAL OF THE ADMINISTRATION, BY PROVIDING STUDENTS INSIGHTS INTO GLOBAL AGRICULTURAL AND INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE.

THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY BY STUDYING SALMONELLA CONTAMINATION ACROSS THE POULTRY SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM FARMS TO PROCESSING AND DISTRIBUTION. THE STUDY WILL USE A NEW RAPID DETECTION TOOL, GENOPATHX, TO MAP SALMONELLA PRESENCE AND TYPES AT VARIOUS STAGES. SAMPLES, SUCH AS AIR FILTERS AND BOOT SWABS FROM FARMS AND MEAT PRODUCTS FROM PROCESSING PLANTS, WILL BE COLLECTED AND ANALYZED TO DETECT CONTAMINATION TRENDS. ADDITIONALLY, AN AI-POWERED SYSTEM WILL BE DEVELOPED TO INTEGRATE GENOPATHX DATA WITH PROCESSING INFORMATION, HELPING PREDICT AND REDUCE SALMONELLA RISKS USING MACHINE LEARNING. PRIVACY-FOCUSED DATA-SHARING METHODS WILL ALSO BE EXPLORED TO ENCOURAGE COLLABORATION AMONG FOOD PRODUCERS WITHOUT EXPOSING SENSITIVE DATA. THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE CREATION OF AN AI-ENABLED BIOSENSOR, WHICH WILL PROVIDE FAST, ON-SITE DETECTION OF MULTIPLE PATHOGENS, ALLOWING REAL-TIME MONITORING AND DECISION-MAKING. LASTLY, THE INITIATIVE WILL OFFER VALUABLE LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS, TRAINING THEM IN ADVANCED FOOD SAFETY TECHNOLOGIES AND PREPARING THEM FOR CAREERS IN FOOD PRODUCTION SAFETY. THIS COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH AIMS TO IMPROVE FOOD SAFETY PRACTICES AND REDUCE THE RISK OF SALMONELLA OUTBREAKS IN POULTRY PRODUCTS.

MISSOURI'S FORESTS, HOME TO AT LEAST 730 WILDLIFE SPECIES, ARE FACING URGENT HEALTH ISSUES FROM INVASIVE SPECIES PESTS AND THEIR IMPACTS NECESSITATING EFFECTIVE MONITORING METHODS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO IMPROVE FOREST HEALTH MONITORING BY INTEGRATING GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGIES WITH ADVANCED AI MODELS TO DEVELOP A FOREST HEALTH EARLY WARNING SYSTEM (FHEWS). WE WILL COMBINE SATELLITE IMAGERY, UAV-BASED MULTISPECTRAL AND LIDAR DATA, ECOLOGICAL INFORMATION AND LOCATION-BASED FOREST HEALTH METRICS TO CREATE A COMPREHENSIVE GEOSPATIAL DATABASE. AI MODELS WILL ANALYZE THIS DATA FOR FOREST HEALTH MONITORING. KEY OBJECTIVES OF THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT INCLUDE: 1. DEVELOPING AND TRAINING AI MODELS TO DETECT EARLY SIGNS OF FOREST HEALTH ISSUES AND CREATING A USER-FRIENDLY INTERFACE FOR MISSOURI STAKEHOLDERS. 2. PROMOTING EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AT LINCOLN UNIVERSITY (LU) AND INCREASING STUDENT INVOLVEMENT IN FORESTRY, GEOSPATIAL SCIENCE AND AI THROUGH MENTORING SCHOLARSHIPS AND PROVIDING STUDENT EXPERIMENTAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES. 3. HOSTING WORKSHOPS TO DISSEMINATE FINDINGS AND TRAIN MISSOURI STAKEHOLDERS IN USING FHEWS TO FACILITATE KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER AND PRACTICAL APPLICATION. CO-PD WITH EXPERTISE IN REMOTE SENSING AND FOREST HEALTH WILL BE CRITICAL IN DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING AI MODELS. AIFARMS INSTITUTE AT UIUC WILL ENHANCE LU'S AI CAPABILITIES. BRAD GRAHAM FROM THE MISSOURI DEPARTMENT OF CONSERVATION WILL ORGANIZE WORKSHOPS TO ENSURE EFFECTIVE KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH THE CBG PROGRAM BY EDUCATING STUDENTS, STRENGTHENING PARTNERSHIPS AND ENHANCING EDUCATION, RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AT LU. IT SUPPORTS USDA'S FOCUS ON BUILDING AI AND MACHINE LEARNING CAPACITY IN FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES.

SIGNIFICANT POSTHARVEST LOSSES OF FRESH PRODUCE ARE REPORTED EVERY YEAR DUE TO PHYSIOLOGICAL DEGRADATION AND FUNGAL ATTACKS BECAUSE OF THEIR HIGH NUTRIENT CONTENT. GENERALLY, COLD STORAGE AND FUNGICIDES ARE USED TO CONTROL POSTHARVEST DISORDERS AND DISEASES. HOWEVER, DUE TO GROWING PUBLIC CONCERN SURROUNDING RESIDUAL CHEMICALS IN FRESH PRODUCE FUNGICIDE ALTERNATIVES MUST BE DEVELOPED. WE PROPOSE THIS COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROJECT TO BUILD RESEARCH TEACHING AND EXTENSION CAPACITY IN THE POSTHARVEST RESEARCH PROGRAM AT VSU. THE PROGRAM AIMS TO 1) EXTEND THE SHELF LIFE OF FRESH PRODUCE THROUGH INNOVATIVE AND ALTERNATIVE POSTHARVEST PRACTICES 2) TRAIN STUDENTS AND 3) DISSEMINATE THE RESULTS. PLANTS PRODUCE VOLATILES AS A NATURAL SELF-DEFENSE SYSTEM. WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AN ACTIVE PACKAGE WITH EXTEND-RELEASE TECHNOLOGY TO RELEASE PLANT VOLATILES (ESSENTIAL OILS) IN STRAWBERRY PACKAGES THEREBY IMPROVING THE SHELF LIFE OF STRAWBERRIES AND FEEDING AMERICA WITH HEALTHY FRESH PRODUCE. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES ALL THREE NIFA-CBG PROGRAM GOALS: ENHANCE MENTORING STUDENTS TO STRENGTHEN LINKAGES AMONG THE 1890 INSTITUTIONS THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE PROJECT AND ENHANCE AND STRENGTHEN THE QUALITY OF ALL PROGRAMS BY INCORPORATING RECENT ADVANCES IN SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY. THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) DEVELOP AN ECOFRIENDLY ACTIVE PACKAGE INSERT FOR THE EXTENDED RELEASE OF ESSENTIAL OILS 2) IDENTIFY EXPRESSION LEVELS OF GENES INFLUENCING FRUIT FIRMNESS 3) IDENTIFY THRESHOLDS FOR CONSUMER DETECTION AND REJECTION OF COLOR TEXTURE OR FLAVOR CHANGES CAUSED BY ESSENTIAL OILS 4) DEVELOP MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO PREDICT CONSUMER LIKING 5) DEVELOP HUMAN CAPITAL, ALTERNATIVE POSTHARVEST PRACTICES AND DISSEMINATE OF THE RESULTS. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS HBCU EXECUTIVE ORDER BY IMPROVING WORKFORCE PREPAREDNESS.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THIS PROJECT OFFERS A LEADERSHIP PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR EXTENSION AGENTS WORKING IN 1890S INSTITUTIONS. THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED THROUGH AN ONLINE MASTER'S IN NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT COMBINED WITH A SUMMER GEOSPATIAL SCIENCES TRAINING COURSE. THIS OPPORTUNITY WILL SUPPORT AGENTS IN ENROLLING IN THE FULL ONLINE GRADUATE DEGREE CURRICULUM WHILE CONTINUING TO FULFILL THEIR EXTENSION APPOINTMENTS, WITH ALL EXPENSES RELATED TO THE PRESCRIBED COURSEWORK COVERED. THE ONLINE MS CURRICULUM WILL INCLUDE NATURAL RESOURCES POLICY, LEGISLATION, AND MANAGEMENT. ALSO INCLUDED WILL BE A NEW COURSE ON COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT THAT WOULD PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY FOR THE EXTENSION AGENTS TO BETTER ASSIST THEIR COMMUNITIES. THE ANNUAL GEOSPATIAL SCIENCES TRAINING WORKSHOP DURING THE SUMMER WILL PROVIDE HANDS-ON TRAINING IN GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS, REMOTE SENSING, AND SPATIAL DATA ANALYSIS. THIS MS PROGRAM/SUMMER TRAINING COMBINATION WILL PREPARE EXTENSION AGENTS TO FIND SOLUTIONS FOR INTRICATE ENVIRONMENTAL PROBLEMS AND PROMOTE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN THEIR COMMUNITIES. AT PROJECT COMPLETION, EIGHT AGENTS WILL HAVE GRADUATED WITH THE ONLINE MS DEGREE; TWENTY-FOUR WILL HAVE COMPLETED THE GEOSPATIAL SCIENCES TRAINING; THREE TRADITIONAL STUDENTS WILL HAVE ACQUIRED NEW EXPERIENCE IN MANAGING ONLINE LEARNING CONTENT; PARTICIPATING INSTRUCTORS WILL HAVE BENEFITED FROM PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT COURSES. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE ENVIRONMENTAL LITERACY AND SKILLS AMONG EXTENSION AGENTS, FOSTER NEW PARTNERSHIPS AMONG PARTICIPATING 1890S INSTITUTIONS, AND INCREASE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES. TRAINING COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AGENTS TO ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES WILL RESULT IN SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNITY BENEFITS, AND IMPROVEMENTS IN FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCEEDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION.

A CRITICAL NEED EXISTS TO ATTRACT HIGH-CALIBER INDIVIDUALS TO AGRICULTURAL DEGREE PROGRAMS AND PREPARE QUALIFIED FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES GRADUATES TO ENTER THE WORKFORCE. DESPITE GROWING OPPORTUNITIES FOR COLLEGE GRADUATES IN THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES, ENROLLMENTS IN COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE NATIONALLY CONTINUE TO DECLINE. ALTHOUGH ENROLLMENT NUMBERS HAVE INCREASED SLIGHTLY WITHIN THE UMES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND RESOURCE SCIENCES (DAFRS), THERE IS A GREAT NEED TO RECRUIT LARGER NUMBERS OF HIGH-CALIBER STUDENTS TO AGRICULTURAL DEGREE PROGRAMS, PROVIDE INNOVATIVE WAYS TO RETAIN STUDENTS, AND ENHANCE THEIR EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO STRENGTHEN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND OUTREACH IN THE DEPARTMENT AND UMES EXTENSION BY 1) ESTABLISHING A DAFRS AGRICULTURAL MENTORING AND RESEARCH EXPERIENCE PROGRAM FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS (REU); 2) ESTABLISHING A VETERINARY SCIENCE CLINICAL SKILLS LAB TO PROVIDE HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE AND TRAINING TO ENHANCE PRE-VETERINARY STUDENTS' SKILLS, COMPETENCIES, AND COMPETITIVENESS TO PREPARE THEM FOR ACCREDITED VETERINARY MEDICAL COLLEGES AND OTHER PROFESSIONAL SCHOOLS; 3) RECRUITING LOCALLY BY ESTABLISHING A COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIP WITH THE MATH, SCIENCE, AND LEADERSHIP (MSL) SYMPHONY PROGRAM TO SERVE AS A PIPELINE PROGRAM INTO OUR AGRICULTURAL PROGRAMS; AND 4) OFFERING TRAVEL SCHOLARSHIPS TO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN THE REU PROGRAM, AND ACADEMIC SCHOLARSHIPS TO MSL STUDENTS WHO ENROLL IN THE UMES DAFRS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO BRIDGE THE GAPS AND ENHANCE THE DEPARTMENT'S LEARNING AND ENGAGEMENT, RECRUITMENT, AND RETENTION BY BUILDING HUMAN CAPACITY, STRENGTHENING STUDENTS' ACADEMIC AND PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCES, AND PREPARING QUALIFIED GRADUATES FOR PROFESSIONAL AND GRADUATE SCHOOL AND THE FUTURE AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE.

THE SKILLS, OPPORTUNITIES, INNOVATION AND LEARNING (S.O.I.L.) INITIATIVE AIMS TO POSITIVELY IMPACT SUMTER COUNTY, THROUGH A STRATEGIC WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROJECT THAT FOCUSES ON TRAINING, EDUCATIONAL ENRICHMENT, AND SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AGRICULTURE, AND MATH (STEAM) INDUSTRY (I.E. [S (BIOLOGY, CHEMISTRY, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE); T (COMPUTER PROGRAMMING, ROBOTICS, CYBERSECURITY, INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, DIGITAL LITERACY); E (CIVIL, MECHANICAL, AEROSPACE, ELECTRICAL, ARCHITECTURAL); A (AGRONOMY, HORTICULTURE, SOIL SCIENCE, SUSTAINABLE FARMING PRACTICES); M (STATISTICS, APPLIED MATHEMATICS]) MENTORSHIP. THE BLACK BELT (BB) IS THE MOST ECONOMICALLY STRAINED REGION OF THE STATE AND PERHAPS THE ENTIRE UNITED STATES. THE REGION HAS EXPERIENCED A DECLINE IN INDUSTRIES SUCH AS AGRICULTURE, MANUFACTURING AND TEXTILES, LEADING TO LOSS OF JOBS OVER THE YEARS. PEOPLE ARE NOT LIKELY TO SECURE JOBS IN SUMTER COUNTY. THEREFORE, STRUGGLES TO ATTRACT NEW INDUSTRIES AND CREATE EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES HAS RESULTED IN HIGHER UNEMPLOYMENT RATES. RESEARCH HAS DOCUMENTED THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF EDUCATION AND EMPLOYMENT IN THE BLACK BELT REGION. LIMITED ACCESS TO HIGHER EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING PROGRAMS FURTHER HAMPERS THE REGION'S ABILITY TO DEVELOP A SKILLED WORKFORCE AND ATTRACT BUSINESSES (MANN & ROGERS, 2021). THE LACK OF A SKILLED WORKFORCE PERPETUATES A CYCLE OF LIMITED ECONOMIC GROWTH AND EXACERBATES POVERTY AND INEQUALITY IN THE REGION. IN ORDER FOR ALABAMA TO INCREASE ITS RATES OF LABOR FORCE PARTICIPATION AND FULFILL THE WORKFORCE DEMANDS OF PRESENT AND FUTURE BUSINESSES AND INDUSTRIES, IT IS ESSENTIAL TO TRAIN AND RETAIN TALENTED WORKERS (KATSIANS, KEENEY, JACOBS, & WHANN, 2020). THE S.O.I.L. INITIATIVE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES.

THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ENGAGE STUDENTS FROM ALABAMA A&M UNIVERSITY IN RESEARCH AND CAREER ENHANCING ACTIVITIES THAT WILL PREPARE THEM TO BE FUTURE PROFESSIONALS IN FORESTRY. WE HAVE TWO PRIMARY OBJECTIVES: (1) EDUCATION - ENHANCE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR ALL STUDENTS IN DATA SCIENCE RELATING TO FOREST HABITATS; AND (2) RESEARCH - DEVELOP TOOLS FOR INTEGRATED FOREST DEMOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS. EDUCATION WILL BE FACILITATED BY TECHNICAL AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING IN FORESTRY TO BUILD STUDENTS' CAPACITIES IN EMERGING TECHNIQUES, MORE SPECIFICALLY IN FOREST INVENTORIES, DENDROCHRONOLOGY, LIDAR, AND OPTICAL REMOTE SENSING, GIS-BASED DATA ANALYSIS AND DATA SCIENCE. RESEARCH IN THIS PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON UNDERSTANDING THE FOREST ARCHITECTURE BASED ON TREE-LEVEL SAMPLING AND LARGE-SCALE IMAGE ANALYSIS. STUDENTS WILL BE INSTRUCTED IN FIELD TECHNIQUES SUCH AS COLLECTING TREE MEASUREMENTS, DENDROCHRONOLOGICAL SAMPLES TERRESTRIAL LIDAR AND HYPER-SPECTRAL IMAGES, AS WELL AS DEVELOPING ANALYTICAL SKILLS IN PROCESSING AND INTERPRETING THE DATA ASSOCIATED WITH REMOTE SENSING ANALYSES. THE MAIN GOAL IS TO BRIDGE THE GAP BETWEEN CLASSROOM KNOWLEDGE AND HANDS-ON RESEARCH TECHNIQUES AND EXPERIENCES TARGETED TOWARD STUDENTS, MAKING THEM MORE COMPETITIVE WHEN CONSIDERING CONTINUING CAREERS IN THESE AREAS. WE WILL EXPOSE THE STUDENTS TO IMMERSIVE LEARNING AT THE ALABAMA A&M RESEARCH SITE THAT IS PART OF THE SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION'SFOREST GLOBAL EARTH OBSERVATORY (FORESTGEO) NETWORK. SIX STUDENTS PER YEAR WILL PARTICIPATE IN A SPRING SEMESTER INTERNSHIP TO PREPARE THEM FOR A SUMMER RESEARCH INTERNSHIP WITH COLLABORATING INSTITUTIONS (THE JONES CENTER AT ICHAUWAY, OAK RIDGE NATIONAL LABORATORY, THE NATURE CONSERVANCY, HARVARD FOREST, AND SMITHSONIAN)

COLORECTAL CANCER (CRC) POSES A SIGNIFICANT HEALTH DISPARITY AMONG HIGH-RISK COMMUNITIESWITH OVER 20% HIGHER INCIDENCE RATES AND POORER OUTCOMES COMPARED TO HIGH-RISKCOMMUNITIES. ADDRESSING THIS DISPARITY NECESSITATES INNOVATIVE APPROACHES LEVERAGINGDIETARY FIBER AND GUT MICROBIOME-DERIVED METABOLITES. MUSCADINE GRAPES (MG) AREEXTENSIVELY CULTIVATED IN THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES CONTRIBUTING SIGNIFICANTLY TO THEREGIONAL AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY. DESPITE THEIR ECONOMIC VALUE MUSCADINE GRAPE PROCESSING(MGP) GENERATES 30% UNUTILIZED FIBER-RICH MATERIAL. THE FIBER-RELATED HEALTH OUTCOMES OFMGP PARTICULARLY ITS INTERACTIONS WITH THE HUMAN GUT MICROBIOME AND PRODUCTION OF SHORT-CHAIN FATTY ACIDS (SCFAS) REMAIN LARGELY UNEXPLORED. PREVIOUS RESEARCH SHOWED THE EFFICACYOF MG BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS IN INHIBITING CANCER CELLS. THE PROJECT TEAM WILL INVESTIGATE THEPOTENTIAL OF MGP SOLUBLE AND INSOLUBLE FIBER IN COMBINATION WITH GUT-MICROBIOME-DERIVEDSCFAS TO INHIBIT CRC CELL GROWTH SPECIFICALLY WITHIN HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS. WE WILL CONDUCTCOMPREHENSIVE ANALYSES TO CHARACTERIZE MGP FIBER CONTENT AND COMPOSITION ACROSSVARIOUS CULTIVARS IDENTIFYING OPTIMAL PROFILES FOR CRC PREVENTION AND EXPLORE IN-VITROFERMENTATION OF MGP BY THE GUT MICROBIOME OF HEALTHY AMERICANS TO GENERATE SCFASFOCUSING ON ELUCIDATING THEIR EFFECTS ON CRC CELL GROWTH INHIBITION. USING IN-VITRO CRC CELLMODELS WE WILL EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF INVESTIGATIVE GUT-MICROBIOME-DERIVED SCFAS ININHIBITING CRC CELL PROLIFERATION AND INDUCING APOPTOSIS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL ASSESS THEIMPACT OF INVESTIGATIVE-DERIVED FIBER AND SCFAS ON THE GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION ANDFUNCTION TO ELUCIDATE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY PROJECT PROMISES TOINFORM PERSONALIZED CRC PREVENTION STRATEGIES AND IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR ADISPROPORTIONATE HIGH-RISK POPULATION NATIONWIDE. THIS PROJECT ENHANCES HEALTHYALTERNATIVE APPROACHES IN DISEASE MANAGEMENT BY ALIGNING WITH THE MAHA INITIATIVE FORDISEASE PREVENTION THROUGH BETTER NUTRITION.

THIS EXPONENTIAL GROWTH COUPLED WITH THE UNIQUE FOOD AND CULINARY TRADITIONS GENERATESSIGNIFICANT DEMAND FOR TRADITIONAL OR LESS COMMON FRUITS AND VEGETABLES IN KENTUCKY.CURRENTLY THIS DEMAND IS PRIMARILY FULFILLED FROM PRODUCTION IN FLORIDA, HOWEVER, THERE IS ANOPPORTUNITY FOR GROWERS IN KENTUCKY TO LOCALLY PRODUCE THESE VEGETABLES AND MEET THEDEMAND. THIS INTEGRATED RESEARCH TEACHING AND EXTENSION PROPOSAL AIMS TO STRENGTHEN THECAPACITY OF KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY AND ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF GROWERS IN EXPLORING THEPRODUCTION AND MARKETING OF TRADITIONAL OR LESS COMMON VEGETABLES. THE PROPOSALOBJECTIVES ARE TO: 1) IDENTIFY THE TOP FIVE DESIRED TRADITIONAL OR LESS COMMON VEGETABLESBASED ON THEIR SCOPE AND MARKETING POTENTIAL IN KENTUCKY; 2) DEVELOP YEAR-ROUNDPRODUCTION AND MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR KENTUCKY'S SOILS AND ENVIRONMENT; 3)DISSEMINATE TECHNICAL PRODUCTION AND MARKETING KNOWLEDGE TO AUDIENCE THROUGH THEDEVELOPMENT OF NEW EXTENSION CURRICULUMS; AND 4) PROVIDE HANDS-ON EXPERIENTIAL LEARNINGAND CRITICAL THINKING EXPERIENCES TO STUDENTS. RESEARCH RESULTS ON TRADITIONAL OR LESSCOMMON VEGETABLE PRODUCTION WILL BE DISSEMINATED AT WORKSHOPS CONFERENCES CLASSROOMTEACHING EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FIELD VISITS AND YOUTUBE VIDEOS AND FORSTUDENTS, EXTENSION AGENTS AND SMALL-SCALE GROWERS. THIS COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH WILLENHANCE THE ACCESS OF LOCALLY PRODUCED FRESH VEGETABLES TO CONSUMERS THEREBY SUPPORTINGLOCAL AGRICULTURE AND COMMUNITY HEALTH.

FORESTS ARE DYING AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION IS BEING ABANDONED IN THE MID-ATLANTIC REGION DUE TO INUNDATION SALINITY INTRUSION AND ELEVATED STORM SURGE RESULTING IN THE LOSS OF ESSENTIAL ECOSYSTEM SERVICES INCLUDING FOOD PRODUCTION, PHOTOSYNTHESIS, NUTRIENT FILTRATION, HABITAT PROVISION AND BUFFERING. SOIL SALINIZATION AND INUNDATION TRIGGER A CASCADE OF EVENTS AND FEEDBACK RANGING FROM THE MICROBIAL TO ECOSYSTEM LEVEL BUT MANY OF THE ASSOCIATED MECHANISMS ARE NOT YET UNDERSTOOD WITH VEGETATION AND SOIL MICROBIAL RESPONSE TO SALINIZATION NEEDING MORE CLARITY. THIS PROPOSAL INCREASES RESEARCH AND EDUCATIONAL CAPACITY THROUGH (1) THE INSTALLATION OF A PAIRED IN-SITU MESOCOSM IN BOTH FOREST AND CULTIVATED SYSTEMS TO ALLOW FOR NEW EXPERIMENTATION THAT CAPTURES NATURAL VARIABILITY AND (2) THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT COURSE FOCUSED ON NEED FOR THE 1890 LAND GRANT COMMUNITY AND THROUGH THE INCORPORATION OF THE PROJECT MESOCOSM INTO EXISTING COURSES AT UMES THROUGH INTEGRATIVE MODULES. THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES ALIGN WITH UNIVERSITY OF MARYLAND EASTERN SHORE SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL SCIENCES.

AS THE HUMAN POPULATION INCREASES WORLDWIDE THERE IS A GROWING DEMAND TO PROVIDE SUFFICIENT AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD. AS A RESULT, THERE IS AN INCREASE IN THE JOB MARKET FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO ARE KNOWLEDGEABLE AND TRAINED IN THE AREAS OF FOOD AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES. THUS, WE MUST DEVELOP A DIVERSE WORKFORCE OF WELL-TRAINED AGRICULTURAL SCIENTISTS, NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS AND NUTRITIONAL EXPERTS THAT CAN GENERATE AND IMPLEMENT INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS. TO DEVELOP AN EFFECTIVE WORKFORCE THAT IS WELL-TRAINED KNOWLEDGEABLE AND EQUIPPED WE NEED TO PROVIDE GRADUATE STUDENTS THE OPPORTUNITIES TO PARTICIPATE IN EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES INVOLVING RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ENGAGEMENT. THIS WILL ALLOW STUDENTS TO GAIN SOFT TECHNICAL AND RESEARCH SKILLS, SO THEY ARE ABLE TO MAKE THE LINK BETWEEN COURSE WORK AND PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS IN THE WORK ENVIRONMENT. THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO: 1) EXPAND GRADUATE STUDENTS' KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE THROUGH SUPERVISED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROJECTS IN ANIMAL PLANT NATURAL RESOURCES AND/OR NUTRITIONAL SCIENCES; AND 2) DEVELOP STUDENTS' SOFT AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS THROUGH PEER MENTORING LEADERSHIP TRAINING AND DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH DATA AT CONFERENCES AND EXTENSION WORKSHOPS. THESE GOALS ARE ALIGNED WITH BOTH INSTITUTIONAL GOALS AND USDA HIGH PRIORITY AREAS IN FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES AND OTHERS. THIS PROJECT IS A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT INCLUDING DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY AND TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY. IMPLEMENTATION WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ENHANCE THE RESEARCH EXTENSION AND TEACHING CAPACITY AT BOTH INSTITUTIONS AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF WELL-TRAINED STUDENTS PURSUING A GRADUATE DEGREE IN AGRICULTURAL NATURAL RESOURCES AND NUTRITIONAL SCIENCES. THIS PROJECT ALIGNED WITH THE EO 14283 ON HBCUS TO BOLSTER WORKFORCE PREPARATION IN KEY INDUSTRIES.

SPOTTED WING DROSOPHILA (DROSOPHILA SUZUKII, MATSUMURA), SWD, NATIVE TO ASIA, IS AMONG THE MOST DESTRUCTIVE PESTS OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES WORLDWIDE. THIS INVASIVE SPECIES WAS FIRST FOUND IN THE WESTERN US IN 2008 AND THEN IN MID-ATLANTIC REGIONS IN 2011. SINCE THEN, IT HAS RAPIDLY COLONIZED MANY FRUIT-PRODUCING UNITED STATES REGIONS. FOLLOWING ITS INTRODUCTION, IT CREATES THE GREATEST RISK TO THE FARMING INDUSTRY, WHICH CAUSES HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS OF DOLLARS IN ECONOMIC DAMAGE YEARLY. SPOTTED WING DROSOPHILA HAS A WIDE HOST RANGE OF THIN-SKINNED HOSTS FRUITS, SUCH AS BLACKBERRIES (RUBUSSPP.), BLUEBERRIES (VACCINIUMSPP.), CHERRIES (PRUNUSSPP.), STRAWBERRY FRAGARIA&TIMES;ANANASSADUCHESNE), RED RASPBERRY (RUBUS IDAEUSL.), BLACK RASPBERRY (RUBUS OCCIDENTALISL.) AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO DAMAGE MANY OTHER FRUITS AS WELL. CURRENT CHEMICAL CONTROL MEASURES FOCUS ON ADULTS, NOT LARVAE OR EGGS IN THE FRUIT. SWD HAS A HIGH REPRODUCTIVE RATE AND IS DIFFICULT TO CONTROL. THEREFORE, FREQUENT SPRAYING IS REQUIRED, WHICH MAY INCREASE THE CHANCE OF INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE AND RESIDUAL EFFECTS ON THE FRUITS. FOR INSTANCE, FARMERS IN OUR REGION ARE FORCED TO SPRAY WEEKLY TO CONTROL SWD. ON THE DELMARVA PENINSULA, SWD IS CONSIDERED A SIGNIFICANT PEST OF BERRIES. THEREFORE, FARMERS REQUIRE MORE INFORMATION ON SWD PROTECTION TECHNIQUES. HERE, WE PROPOSE DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING SWD MONITORING AND MANAGING TACTICS IN BERRY FIELDS USING GREEN PESTICIDES, REPELLING FROM THE FRUITS, AND ATTRACTING TO THE TRAPS (PUSH AND PULL STRATEGY). GREEN PESTICIDES AREPESTICIDES DERIVED FROM ORGANIC SOURCES THAT ARE CONSIDERED ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY AND CAUSE LESS HARM TO HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH, HABITATS, AND THE ECOSYSTEM. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE PROJECT IS TO ENHANCE THE PRODUCTION OF BERRIES IN THE REGIONS BY HELPING GROWERS ADOPT IPM PRACTICES TO MANAGE THE POPULATION OF SWD. MORE IMPORTANTLY, THIS PROJECT MIGHT HELP REDUCE THE FREQUENT USE OF CHEMICAL PESTICIDES. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP AND DISSEMINATE EFFECTIVE IPM PROGRAMS TO TARGET SWD AND OTHER INSECT PESTS AFFECTING BERRY PRODUCTION. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO:MONITORING SWD DENSITY ON BERRIES FARMS SUCH AS BLUEBERRY, STRAWBERRY, AND ELDERBERRY IN DELMARVA AND NEW JERSEY USING COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE SPOTTED WING DROSOPHILA TRAPS. IDENTIFY THE DIFFERENT SPECIES OF ADULT FRUIT FLIES AND OTHER ARTHROPODS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL COMPARE SWD ADULT CATCHES WITH THE NUMBER OF EGGS AND LARVAE FROM COLLECTED FRUIT SAMPLES.EXAMINE AND SCREEN GREEN PESTICIDES AND THEIR ANALOG BLENDS FOR TOXICITY (FLASK BIOASSAY) AND REPELLENCY (CAGE BIOASSAY) AGAINST SWD USING LABORATORY-MAINTAINED COLONIES OF FRUIT FLIES.EVALUATE THE CATCH EFFICACY OF LAB AND GREENHOUSE-SELECTED INSECT ATTRACTANT AND REPELLENT BIOCHEMICAL PESTICIDES AND COMPARE WITH COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE SWD TRAPS UNDER FIELD CONDITIONFIELD TESTING OF SUITABLE BLENDS WITH PROMISING GREEN PESTICIDES IN A PUSH-PULL SYSTEM (REPELLENT AND ATTRACTANTS) AGAINST SWD AND OT,HER IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL INSECT PESTS OF BERRIES.DEVELOP AN EXTENSION OUTREACH PROGRAM TO INTRODUCE THE SWD MANAGEMENT METHOD AND EDUCATE FARMERS ON THE IMPACT OF SWD ON THIN-SKINNED FRUITS SUCH AS BLACKBERRIES, ELDERBERRIES, BLUEBERRIES, CHERRIES, STRAWBERRIES, AND RED AND BLACK RASPBERRIES.APPROACH AND PROJECT PLAN OBJECTIVE 1. EXAMINE AND SCREEN GREEN PESTICIDES AND THEIR ANALOG BLENDS FOR TOXICITY (FLASK BIOASSAY) AND REPELLENCY (CAGE BIOASSAY) AGAINST SWD USING LABORATORY-MAINTAINED COLONIES OF FRUIT FLIESOVIPOSITION BIOASSAY: THE OVIPOSITION PREFERENCES OF SWD FEMALES WILL BE ASSESSED IN A 40 X 40 CM CAGE BIOASSAY. IF MB AND THE ANALOGS HAVE AN OVIPOSITIONAL DETERRENT OR ATTRACTANT EFFECT WILL BE DETERMINED. THE OVIPOSITION BEHAVIOR OF FEMALE SWD ON BERRIES SPRAYED WITH SELECTED MB AND ITS ANALOGS WILL BE EVALUATED IN CAGES IN THE GREENHOUSE. TWO TREATED (WITH MB AND ITS ANALOGS) AND TWO UNTREATED BERRIES OR TREATED WITH SOLVENT(CONTROLS) WILL BE PRESENTED TO FEMALE SWD IN CHOICE OVIPOSITION BIOASSAYS.FUMIGATION TOXICITY: THE TOXICITY EXPERIMENT WILL BE SET IN 250ML ERLENMEYER FLASKS USING LAB-MAINTAINED COLONIES OF SPOTTED WING DROSOPHILA. THREE-EIGHT DAYS OLD, TEN MALE OR FEMALE SWD ADULTS WILL BE USED FOR THE FUMIGATION EXPERIMENT. EACH OF THEM WILL BE PLACED IN FIVE DIFFERENT ERLENMEYER FLASKS (250ML) WITH THE SWD DIET (1.25-1.3G). THE MB AND ITS DERIVATIVE COMPOUNDS WILL BE PREPARED AT DIFFERENT CONCENTRATIONS USING ACETONE, AND ACETONE WILL BE USED AS CONTROL. .(DETAILS ARE IN THE FULL PROPOSAL)OBJECTIVE 2 . ASSESS SWD ANTENNAL RESPONSE TO SELECT ATTRACTANT AND REPELLENT COMPOUNDS SELECTED FROM OBJECTIVE ONE USING GAS CHROMATOGRAPHY COUPLED WITH AN ELECTROANTENNOGRAM DETECTOR (GC-EAD) AND Y-TUBE OLFACTOMETER.GAS CHROMATOGRAPHY COUPLED WITH AN ELECTROANTENNOGRAM DETECTOR (GC-EAD) BIOASSAYS: THE COMPOUNDS WILL BE FIRST IDENTIFIED AND CONFIRMED IN GC-FID. THE COMPOUNDS WILL BE DIRECTED TO THE EAG SYSTEM THROUGH THE SPLIT LINE. THE EAG TECHNIQUE WILL BE USED TO RECORD THE ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES OF ADULT SWD TO VOLATILES OBTAINED FROM DIFFERENT ANALOGS OF MB. .(DETAILS ARE IN THE FULL PROPOSAL)Y-TUBE OLFACTOMETER: THE COMPOUNDS WITH THE BIOLOGICAL RESPONSE FROM THE ABOVE GC-EAD STUDY WILL BE SUBJECTED TO A Y-TUBE OLFACTOMETER. THE RESPONSE OF ADULT SWD TO THE MB AND ITS ANALOG VOLATILES WILL BE TESTED IN Y-TUBE (ANALYTICAL RESEARCH SYSTEMS, INC., GAINESVILLE, FL = ARS), USING PROTOCOLS DESCRIBED IN CHEN AND FADAMIRO (2007). .(DETAILS ARE IN THE FULL PROPOSAL)OBJECTIVE 3. EVALUATE THE CATCH EFFICACY OF LAB AND GREENHOUSE-SELECTED COMPOUNDS AND COMPARE WITH COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE SWD TRAPS UNDER FIELD CONDITIONS USING VICTOR® YELLOW JACKET TRAP.TRAP COMPARISONS: TO COMPARE THE CATCH EFFICACY OF COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE TRAPS WITH THE LAB AND GREENHOUSE-SELECTED BIOCHEMICALS, TRAPS WILL BE PURCHASED FROM GREATLAKES WITH TR&EACUTE;C&EACUTE; PHEROCON SWD LURES AND VICTOR® M362 POISON-FREE REUSABLE YELLOW JACKET TRAP WILL BE BOUG,HT FROM SOLUTIONS PEST AND LAWN. THE TRAPS WILL BE HUNG AT DIFFERENT LOCATIONS TO AVOID COMPETITION AMONG TRAP TYPES. EACH TRAP WILL BE REPLICATED AT LEAST THRICE AND MOUNTED ABOVE THE BERRY BUSHES. FIELD TESTING OF SUITABLE BLENDS WITH PROMISING GREEN PESTICIDES IN A PUSH-PULL SYSTEM (REPELLENT AND ATTRACTANTS) AGAINST SWD AND OTHER IMPORTANT AGRICULTURAL INSECT PESTS OF BERRIESUSING BLUEBERRY, STRAWBERRY, RASPBERRY, AND ELDERBERRY AS A MODEL SYSTEM. PUSH (REPELLENT CHEMICAL), PULL (ATTRACTANT CHEMICAL), PUSH-PULL (BOTH ATTRACTANT AND REPELLENT CHEMICALS), AND CONTROL (NO CHEMICALS) TRAPS WILL BE SET UP AT RANDOMIZED COMPLETE BLOCK DESIGN. EACH TRAP WILL BE REPLICATED AT LEAST THRICE AND MOUNTED ABOVE THE BERRY BUSHES EXCEPT FOR THE PUSH CHEMICALS TRAP (DETAILS ARE IN THE FULL PROPOSAL).OBJECTIVE 5 (RESEARCH) EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF THE SELECT ATTRACTANTS AND REPELLENTS ON BENEFICIAL INSECTSASSESSING THE IMPACT OF MB AND ANALOGS ON POLLINATORS AND NATURAL ENEMIES: THE IMPACT OF MB AND ANALOGS ON BENEFICIAL INSECTS WILL BE EVALUATEDUSING THE FOLLOWING EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN DESCRIBED FOR OBJECTIVE FOUR. EACH EXPERIMENTAL PLOT WILL BE ASSESSED FOR POLLINATOR ACTIVITY, SUCH AS FLOWER VISITS, WHICH WILL BE ASSESSED WEEKLY BY MAKING VISUAL OBSERVATIONS FOR TWO MINUTES ON EACH PLOT (PUSH, PULL, PUSH-PULL, AND CONTROL) AT TWO TIME POINTS (DETAILS ARE IN THE FULL PROPOSAL).

AGRICULTURE IS CRITICAL TO OUR SURVIVAL, ECONOMY, HEALTH, HABITAT AND SECURITY. LIKE OTHER STEMFIELDS, THE PRODUCTION AND CONSUMPTION OF FOOD AND FOOD SYSTEMS AMIDST A DATA REVOLUTION.MASSIVE QUANTITIES OF DATA ARE GENERATED DAILY IN AGRICULTURAL FIELDS BIO-ECOSYSTEMS ANDFOOD TRANSPORT AND SAFETY. THE DEMAND FOR TRAINED APPLIED DATA SCIENTISTS' EXPERTS WHO CANUNCOVER THE HIDDEN INFORMATION FROM COMPLEX AGRICULTURAL DATASETS AND CORRECTLY CONVEY ITTO THE PRODUCERS AND DECISION-MAKERS IS INCREASING AS EVIDENCED BY PROJECTED WORKFORCENEED PREDICTIONS. THE OVERARCHING MISSION OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP NATIONALLYRECOGNIZED GRADUATE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM IN AGRI-ECOSYSTEM DATA SCIENCE ATAAMU BY DEVELOPING A DATA SCIENCE SPECIALIZATION WITHIN THE EXISTING MS AND PHD DEGREEPROGRAMS THAT SUPPORT PLANT AND SOIL SCIENCE NATURAL RESOURCE AND ECOLOGY. THE TWO MAJORGOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) DEVELOP THE CURRICULUM FORTHESPECIALIZATION THAT FEATURESINTERDISCIPLINARY ENGAGEMENT OF LIFE SCIENCE FIELDS (BIOSTATISTICS BIOINFORMATICSGEOSTATISTICS GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS (GIS) AND REMOTE SENSING) BY INTEGRATINGCRITICAL DATA SCIENCE COURSES FROM RELEVANT ACADEMIC AREAS SUCH AS COMPUTER SCIENCE ANDMATHEMATICS; AND 2) INTEGRATE DATA SCIENCE WITH THE ONGOING APPLIED RESEARCH INAGRICULTURAL AND BIO-ECOSYSTEM FIELDS WITH THE EMPHASIS OF PROVIDING HANDS-ON RESEARCHTRAININGS FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS. THE DATA SCIENCE SPECIALIZATION WILL NOT ONLY TOUCH THE LANDGRANT TRIUMVIRATE OF TEACHING RESEARCH AND EXTENSION BUT ALSO OTHER PUBLIC AND PRIVATEENTITIES AND ENHANCE THE STUDENT RECRUITMENT. THE MAJOR OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WOULD BEAN INCREASED NUMBER OF SKILLED WORKFORCES THAT SUPPORT HBCU EXECUTIVE ORDER BYIMPROVING WORKFORCE PREPAREDNESS.

FOLLOWING UNIVERSITY INITIATIVES AND OHIO STATE WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PRIORITIES, THIS PROJECT (1) ENHANCES THE SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE CURRICULA, BY DEVELOPING NEW EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES, INSTITUTIONAL AND INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS, AND NEW ACADEMIC PROGRAMMING AT CSU, (2) DEVELOPS MULTIDISCIPLINARY LEARNING COMMUNITIES TO BOLSTER LEADERSHIP AND CAREER COMPETENCIES TO BETTER PREPARE STUDENTS FOR THE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE, AND (3) STRENGTHENS RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION STRATEGIES AIMED AT AGRICULTURAL STUDENTS TO ATTRACT MORE DIVERSE STUDENTS TO CSU AND THE U.S. AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY. THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON IMPROVING CURRICULUM BY IMPLEMENTING EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE CLASSROOM AND DEVELOPING A CERTIFICATE PROGRAM FOR NONTRADITIONAL LEARNERS. MULTIDISCIPLINARY LEARNING COMMUNITIES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED TO DEVELOP STUDENTS' LEADERSHIP AND WORKFORCE COMPETENCIES; FOSTER RESEARCH SKILLS IN COOPERATION WITH THE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM; AND UTILIZE THE KNOWLEDGE OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES THROUGH INSTITUTIONAL AND INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS. PROJECT RESOURCES PROVIDE FACULTY PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WORKSHOPS, ENHANCE TEACHING CAPABILITIES, AND IMPROVE TECHNOLOGICAL ACCESS FOR STUDENTS. THE PROJECT SUPPORTS STUDENT INTERNSHIPS AND ENCOURAGES UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH INCLUDING PRESENTING AT SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS. PROJECT PARTNERSHIPS ALLOW SHARING OF RESOURCES AND CURRICULUM, MENTORING STUDENTS, AND COMBINING INSTITUTIONAL NETWORKS. REACHING THESE GOALS STRENGTHEN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE PROGRAMS AT CSU TO POSITIVELY IMPACT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE GAUGED THROUGH PUBLICATION OF STUDENT AND FACULTY RESEARCH, INCREASED NUMBERS OF STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN INTERNSHIPS AND GRADUATING INTO AGRICULTURAL GRADUATE STUDY OR CAREERS, AND THE FOUNDATION OF NEW INSTITUTIONAL NETWORKS. BEST PRACTICES IN TEACHING, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT WILL BE SHARED IN TRAINING WORKSHOPS.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXPAND BEEF CATTLE RESEARCH EXTENSION AND EDUCATION CAPACITY AT FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY ESPECIALLY FOR PRACTICES SUCH AS THE USE OF NUTRACEUTICAL SUPPLEMENTS AND BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR IMPROVING BEEF CATTLE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY. WITH THAT IN MIND THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1) EVALUATE USE OF A NUTRACEUTICAL FORAGE ON REPRODUCTION PARASITES/HEALTH AND GROWTH OF BEEF CATTLE 2) RESEARCH USE OF PRECISION LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION (PLP)/ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE/MACHINE LEARNING AND OTHER ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES FOR RAPID IDENTIFICATION OF CATTLE HEALTH AND PRODUCTION STATUS TO MITIGATE PRODUCTION INEFFICIENCIES AND 3) DEVELOP/ENHANCE BEEF CATTLE RESEARCH/DEMONSTRATION SITES TO SHARE PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS. THIS MULTIDISCIPLINARY INTEGRATED PROJECT WILL PROVIDE EXPANDED EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION FOR STUDENTS, FACULTY, STAFF AND CATTLE PRODUCERS RELATED TO PRECISION LIVESTOCK FARMING/PRODUCTION TECHNOLOGIES (INCLUDING THOSE INCORPORATING RFID/GPS/GIS AND BASIC ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE/MACHINE LEARNING CONCEPTS) AND AGRICULTURE'S ROLE IN SUPPORTING OPERATIVE AND PROFITABLE BEEF CATTLE FARMS. THE PROJECT INCLUDES RESEARCH COLLABORATIONS AND TRAINING, UPDATED COURSE CURRICULA AND DEVELOPMENT OF EXTENSION EDUCATION TOOLS THAT WILL HAVE AN IMPACT AND BE USED WELLBEYOND THE GRANTING PERIOD, ALLOWING OUR STUDENTS TO BE MORE COMPETITIVE FOR JOBS, OUR SCIENTISTS TO BE MORE COMPETITIVE FOR GRANT FUNDING AND OUR PRODUCER STAKEHOLDERS TO BE MORE PROFITABLE NOW AND INTO THE FUTURE. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS HBCU EXECUTIVE ORDER BY IMPROVING WORKFORCE PREPAREDNESS.

THE PRIMARY GOALOF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXPOSE STUDENTS TO AGRICULTURAL OPPORTUNITIES BY ADDRESSINGCOMPONENTS OF NUTRITIONAL EDUCATION, MENTAL HEALTH INTERPERSONAL SOCIAL AND WORKFORCESKILLS TO CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE YOUTH. SCHOLARSHIP OPPORTUNITIES); AND (5) TO IMPLEMENTTEACHING OPPORTUNITIES TO SU STUDENTS IN THE COLLEGE OF AG THAT PROVIDE COMMUNITY-BASEDMENTORSHIP OPPORTUNITIES SPECIALIZED AG COURSES FOCUSING ON HORTICULTURE AND ITS RELATIONTO SOCIOLOGY SERVICE-LEARNING HOURS AND STUDENT INTERNSHIPS. INSTRUCTION INVOLVES BOTHCLASSROOM AND HANDS-ON HORTICULTURAL ACTIVITIES. CERTIFICATES ARE AWARDED UPON SUCCESSFULCOMPLETION OF THE PROGRAM. THE LIFE CHANGING MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO THIS PROJECT WILLALLOW YOUTH PARTICIPANTS TO GAIN HORTICULTURAL AND NUTRITIONAL KNOWLEDGE MENTAL HEALTHINTERPERSONAL SOCIAL AND WORKFORCE SKILLS TO PROVIDE A PATHWAY TO HIGHER EDUCATION. SU AGSTUDENTS HAVE QUALITY MENTORSHIP INTERNSHIP AND SERVICE-LEARNING HANDS-ON OPPORTUNITIES.THUS POSITIONING BOTH SETS OF STUDENTS UP FOR A HEALTHY AND PRODUCTIVE LIFESTYLE WITHAGRICULTURE AS ITS BACKBONE.

SOIL ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY IS FUNDAMENTAL TO SOIL HEALTH AND EFFECTIVE LONG-TERM AGRICULTURE. RECENT WIDESPREAD USE OF ENGINEERED NANOPARTICLES (ENPS) AND COMMON HABITAT OCCURRENCE OF PER-AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) HAS RAISED SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC CONCERNS ON THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF SUCH CONTAMINANTS OF EMERGING CONCERNS (CECS). THE VAST APPLICATION OF SILVER NANOPARTICLES (AGNPS)-CONTAINING PESTICIDES AND WIDE EXPOSURE OF AGRICULTURAL SOILS TO PFAS CONTAMINATED IRRIGATION WATER AND BIOSOLID POSES SUBSTANTIAL RISKS TO SOIL HEALTH IN AGRICULTURAL SETTINGS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO COMPREHENSIVELY EVALUATE THE IMPACTS OF AGNPS AND TWO MOST PREVALENT PFAS COMPOUNDS ON THE ACTIVITIES OF EIGHT SOIL ENZYMES VIA ENZYMOLOGICAL ASSAYS AND ADVANCED METABOLOMIC ANALYSIS AND TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE MITIGATION METHODOLOGIES BASED ON THIOLFUNCTIONALIZED BIOCHAR. SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION OF THIS PROJECT WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPACTS ON SOIL MANAGEMENT AND EFFECTIVE LONG-TERM AGRICULTURE IN MISSOURI AND BEYOND. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE DATA-BASED KNOWLEDGE OF CECS IMPACTS ON SOIL ENZYMES, COST-EFFECTIVE/DEPLOYABLE MITIGATION SOLUTIONS AND DISSEMINATION OF DEVELOPED METHODS TO GROWERS AND FARMERS IN AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL HELP THE LEADING 1890 INSTITUTE (LINCOLN UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI) STRENGTHEN ITS RESEARCH AND EXTENSION CAPACITIES AND BOOST THE TRAINING OF STUDENTS THEREBY CONTRIBUTING TO SKILLED-ENHANCED WORKFORCE.

DEVELOPING BREAKTHROUGH TECHNOLOGY FOR OILSEED CROPS WELL-SUITED TO GROWING ON MARGINAL LANDS IN APPALACHIA HAS THE POTENTIAL TO ADDRESS SEVERAL CRITICAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT CHALLENGES. THE OVERALL GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) CONDUCT FACULTY AND STUDENT RESEARCH TO GENETICALLY MODIFY PENNYCRESS TO INCREASE THE PLANT'S ENERGY STORAGE CAPACITY AND NUTRITIVE VALUE AS WELL AS THE PLANT'S ABILITY TO GROW ON MARGINAL SOIL, AND 2) PROVIDE HANDS-ON EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES AND SUMMER WORKSHOPS ON PHOTOSYNTHESIS FOR STUDENTS AT WEST VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING TOOLS SUCH AS METABOLOMICS DATA SETS, TRANSFORMATION CONSTRUCTS, AND HIGH OIL-YIELDING GENE-EDITED LINES TOOLS THAT WILL BE USEFUL TO SCIENTISTS WORKING ON A WIDE RANGE OF TOPICS IN BASIC AND APPLIED AGRICULTURE RESEARCH. STUDENT LEARNING ACTIVITIES WILL INCLUDE TRAINING IN PHOTOSYNTHESIS METHODS, FIELD EXPERIENCE, SUMMER WORKSHOPS, AND MENTORSHIPS. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH THE EO ON UNLEASHING AMERICAN ENERGY BY FOSTERING DOMESTIC BIOENERGY PRODUCTION.

A WOMAN WILL HAVE A MONTHLY MENSTRUAL CYCLE FOR ABOUT 40 YEARS OF HER LIFE AVERAGING TO ABOUT 450 PERIODS OVER THE COURSE OF HER LIFETIME (NAPPI, ET AL, 2016). IT IS ALSO IMPORTANT TO RECOGNIZE THAT TRANSGENDER MEN AND PEOPLE WITH MASCULINE GENDER IDENTITIES, INTERSEX AND NON-BINARY PERSONS MAY ALSO MENSTRUATE (WEISELBERG 2022). AT ANY GIVEN MOMENT ABOUT 26% OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION IS MENSTRUATING (BARRINGTON ET AL. 2021). THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT INVOLVES RESEARCH, EXTENSION, AND TEACHING COMPONENTS PROPOSED TO ADDRESS THE GROWING CONCERNS AND ISSUES SURROUNDING MENSTRUATION, INCLUDING THE POTENTIAL HEALTH RISKS POSED TO USERS OF SYNTHETIC FEMININE HYGIENE PRODUCTS (FHP), ADVANCING RESEARCH IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF FHP THAT USE NATURAL MATERIALS, AS WELL AS PROVIDING MENSTRUAL HYGIENE MANAGEMENT (MHM) EDUCATION FOR YOUNG WOMEN AND GIRLS.THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE:A) TO PRODUCE THREE NATURAL FIBERS; REGENERATIVE COTTON, REGENERATIVE WOOL AND INDUSTRIAL HEMP (CANNABIS SATIVA);B) TO DEVELOP PATENTS FOR SUSTAINABLE FEMININE HYGIENE SANITARY PRODUCTS USING THE THREE NATURAL FIBERS;C) TO EVALUATE THE FHP MADE FROM EACH OF THE NATURAL FIBERS IN COMPARISON TO THE STANDARD SYNTHETIC PRODUCT;D) TO EDUCATE YOUNG WOMEN AND GIRLS ABOUT MHM THROUGH AN EXTENSION PROGRAM;E) TO ENHANCE INSTRUCTION FOR STUDENTS IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL, FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES ANDF) TO PROVIDE A LOCAL FIBER PROCESSING CENTER FOR FIBER GROWERS IN LOUISIANA.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** NATIONALLY, A LARGE PERCENTAGE OF THE PERSONNEL WORKING IN SEVERAL FEDERAL AGENCIES DEALING WITH NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT SCIENCES (NRES), E.G., USDA-NRCS, US-EPA, US-FOREST SERVICE, AND US-GS, ARE EXPECTED TO RETIRE IN THE NEXT DECADE. REPLACING THESE PERSONNEL WITH A DIVERSE POPULATION IS A PRIORITY FOR THESE AGENCIES. TEXAS LEADS THE NATION IN ENERGY PRODUCTION AND SEVERAL AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES SUCH AS CATTLE AND OTHER AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS. THUS, THERE IS A GREAT NEED TO TRAIN MORE NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTISTS TO ADDRESS THE INCREASING ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL DEMANDS CAUSED BY THE SURGE IN THE STATE'S POPULATION. FOR INSTANCE, HUNDREDS OF ACRES OF VALUABLE FARMLANDS AND NATURAL LANDSCAPES ARE LOST ACROSS THE STATE TO URBAN EXPANSION EVERY DAY. OVER 50% OF THE STATE'S DRINKING WATER COMES FROM GROUNDWATER AQUIFERS; HOWEVER, THESE AQUIFERS ARE THREATENED DUE TO EXCESS OVER PUMPING OR POLLUTION FROM LAND USE CHANGES AND OTHER ANTHROPOGENIC ACTIVITIES.POTENTIAL JOB OPPORTUNITIES FOR NRES GRADUATES WOULD BE IN WATERSHED MANAGEMENT, WATER RESOURCES, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, REMEDIATION, AND CONTAMINATION MITIGATION. THE NEED FOR THESE JOBS IS PRONOUNCED FOR AN ECONOMICALLY THRIVING STATE AND THE US. THE DEMAND FOR WELL-TRAINED INTER-DISCIPLINARY NRES PROFESSIONALS IS PROJECTED TO INCREASE IN THIS REGION, NATIONALLY, AND EVEN GLOBALLY.PRAIRIE VIEW A&M UNIVERSITY (PVAMU) IS ONE OF THE LEADING LAND GRANT INSTITUTIONS IN TEXAS. THE NEEDS OF THE STATE SHOULD BE MET BY TRAINING A QUALIFIED WORKFORCE TO MANAGE OUR NATURAL RESOURCES BETTER AND PROTECT OUR ENVIRONMENT. BY COMPLEMENTING THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN SCIENCES (CAHS) 'S EXISTING RESOURCES (HUMAN AND INFRA-STRUCTURAL) WITH THE FINANCIAL SUPPORT THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL PROVIDE, THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION NECESSARY FOR TRAINING NEW NRES PROFESSIONALS WILL BE GREATLY ENHANCED. THE PROPOSED INTERDISCIPLINARY NRES PROGRAM REPRESENTS A SIGNIFICANT EFFORT IN FURNISHING A MUCH-NEEDED SERVICE PRIMARILY TO UNDERSERVED TEXAS CITIZENS AND ALL TEXANS. NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES ARE CRITICAL ISSUES IN THE CHANGING CLIMATE. CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURE (CSA) IS CRITICALLY IMPORTANT TO CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES AND PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT. CSA, WHICH NEEDS ADVANCED AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES TO INCREASE CARBON SEQUESTRATION AND REDUCE GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) EMISSIONS, IS CRITICAL IN CHANGING CLIMATE. AGRICULTURE IS A SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTOR TO GHG EMISSIONS THAT INCREASE GLOBAL WARMING. THEREFORE, REDUCING AGRICULTURAL EMISSIONS AND INCREASING SOIL CARBON SEQUESTRATION COULD BE CRITICAL IN CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION.THE PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP AN INTEGRATED APPROACH TO ADVANCE RESEARCH AND EDUCATION IN CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE (CSA) TO SUPPORT NEW MS AND BS IN AGRICULTURE WITH NRES CONCENTRATION DEGREE PROGRAM IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN SCIENCES (CAHS) AT PRAIRIE VIEW A&M UNIVERSITY (PVAMU). THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRO,JECT ARE TO: I) QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON AGRI-ECOSYSTEM USING EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES (II) DEVELOP NEW EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS, AND (III) ENHANCE STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION TO PRODUCE A SKILLED NRES WORKFORCE. STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION ARE CRITICAL ISSUES IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN SCIENCES AT PVAMU. WHILE THE CAHS HAS ADDED A NEW MS DEGREE PROGRAM IN NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES (NRES) AND A NEW NRES CONCENTRATION IN BS IN AGRICULTURE DEGREE, BUILDING THE CRITICAL MASS OF STUDENTS INTO THE PROGRAM WILL BE A MAJOR CHALLENGE FOR THE NEXT FEW YEARS. THEREFORE, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL HELP CAHS TO BUILD ITS CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT NEW STRATEGIES TO INCREASE STUDENT ENROLLMENT AND RETENTION THROUGH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. THIS PROJECT IS BEING PROPOSED TO IMPLEMENT AN INTEGRATED APPROACH TO EDUCATE AND SUPPORT GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS THROUGH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND ADVANCED RESEARCH METHODS. THIS APPROACH CAN ALSO ENHANCE STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION AND INCREASE THE SKILLED WORKFORCE IN AGRICULTURE AND OTHER PROGRAMS, COLLEGES, AND INSTITUTIONS. OVERALL, THIS PROJECT WILL ENHANCE AND STRENGTHEN THE RESEARCH AND TEACHING/EDUCATION CAPACITY OF CAHS AND INCREASE THE SKILLED WORKFORCE IN NRES.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** WITH URBANIZATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE-INDUCED EXTREME HEAT, IT IS URGENT TO PROVIDE NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS SUCH AS URBAN FORESTS TO MITIGATE INCREASING HEAT HAZARDS AND PROVIDE A BETTER ENVIRONMENT FOR THE INCREASING URBAN POPULATION, ESPECIALLY IN HISTORICALLY EXCLUDED COMMUNITIES. IT IS ALSO IMPORTANT TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE NEXUS OF URBAN TREE CANOPY EQUITY, HEAT VULNERABILITY, AND COMMUNITY NEEDS AND GROW FUTURE CLIMATE-RESILIENT TREES. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO STRENGTHEN TSU'S URBAN FORESTRY PROGRAM BY ADDRESSING THE MAIN RESEARCH QUESTIONS AT THREE LEVELS: 1) AT THE CITY LEVEL, WHAT ARE THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN TREE CANOPY COVER AND HEAT EXPOSURE? HOW ARE THEY RELATED TO SOCIOECONOMIC FACTORS (E.G., INCOME, RACE, EDUCATION)? WHERE ARE THE MOST VULNERABLE AREAS AND WHERE SHOULD BE PRIORITIZED FOR FUTURE TREE PLANTING FROM AN EQUITY PERSPECTIVE? 2) AT THE COMMUNITY LEVEL, WHAT ARE THE PERCEPTIONS, EXPERIENCES, AND NEEDS OF HISTORICALLY EXCLUDED POPULATIONS REGARDING URBAN TREE CANOPY EQUITY, HEAT EXPOSURE, AND FUTURE TREE PLANTING? AND 3) AT THE SITE LEVEL, WHICH URBAN TREE SPECIES ARE BETTER FOR HEAT-TOLERANT AND/OR COOLING EFFECTS IN THE REGION? WITH A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM AND PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS, WE WILL USE SPATIAL ANALYSIS, SOCIAL SCIENCE, FIELD STUDIES, MODELING, AND EXPERT CONSULTATION TO ADDRESS THOSE QUESTIONS. IT WILL STRENGTHEN TSU'S URBAN FORESTRY PROGRAM, FILL KNOWLEDGE GAPS, TRAIN NEXT-GENERATION SCIENTISTS, ENHANCE USDA-HBCUS PARTNERSHIPS, AND HAVE LONG-LASTING IMPACTS ON DIVERSE STAKEHOLDERS IN THE REGION. IT ALSO ALIGNS WELL WITH THE CBG'S NEED AREAS AND PRIORITY AREAS OF BIOENERGY/BIOFUEL AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES AND CLIMATE CHANGE.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE THE QUALITY OF EDUCATION NEEDED TO PRODUCE DIVERSE, CULTURALLY COMPETENT TEACHERS WHO CAN STRENTHEN THE GLOBAL FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE. OUR OBJECTIVES ARE TO:1: DEVELOP PATHWAYS IN EDUCATION AND OUTREACH-ORIENTED CAREERS WITHIN AFNR FIELDS FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO DEVELOP GLOBAL COMPETENCY, WITH PRIORITY GIVEN TO PARTICIPANTS FROM MINORITY, UNDERREPRESENTED AND/OR LOW SES BACKGROUNDS.?2: PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO EXPERIENCE THE INTERSECTION BETWEEN EDUCATION, AGRICULTURE, AND CULTURE IN DIVERSE SETTINGS.3: ADVANCE THE AWARENESS OF AFNR IMPLICATIONS OF THE UNITED NATIONS SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDGS) FOR SECONDARY AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE STUDENTS.WE WILL INVOLVE 18 STUDENTS PER YEAR (6 FROM UIDAHO, 6 FROM PENN STATE, AND 6 FROM ACROSS THE NINETEEN 1890S INSTITUTIONS) WHO HAVE AN INTEREST IN A CAREER RELATED TO EDUCATION/OUTREACH THAT IS AGRICULTURALLY RELATED. ACCEPTED STUDENTS WILL:&BULL; PARTICIPATE IN PRE-IMMERSION WEBINARS&BULL; ATTEND THE BORLAUG DIALOGUES IN OCTOBER AT THE WORLD FOOD PRIZE AND RECEIVE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT ON GLOBAL LEARNING RELATED TOPICS, AND TRAINING ON TEACHING STRATEGIES.&BULL; DEVELOP LESSONS AND MATERIALS RELATED TO GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY IN VIRTUAL TEAMS (A MEMBER FROM EACH INSTITUTIONAL GROUP).&BULL; TEACH IN TRIAD GROUPS FOR A FULL WEEK (WITH REPRESENTATION FROM EACH INSTITUTION) IN DOMESTIC COMMUNITIES - FOCUSED ON TRADITIONALLY UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS.&BULL; PARTICIPATE IN A10-DAY GLOBAL IMMERSION AS A COHORT, FOCUSED ON A SERVICE-PROJECT RELATED TO EXTENDING GLOBAL PERSPECTIVES AND CULTURAL FLUENCY OF PROGRAM PARTICIPANTS.

THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL INCREASE KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S (KSU'S) CAPACITY TO OFFER EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING WITH A FOCUS ON IMPROVING AGRICULTURAL LITERACY, INCREASING ACCESS TO FRESH PRODUCE, AND IMPROVING DIETARY HABITS. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH SIX OBJECTIVES. A STUDENT-RUN FARM WILL BE ESTABLISHED TO SUPPLY PRODUCE TO KSU DINING SERVICES, INCLUDING A STUDENT-RUN CAF&EACUTE;. FARM OPERATIONS WILL BE GUIDED BY AN ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND PRODUCTION WILL TAKE PLACE YEAR-ROUND IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE NATIONAL ORGANIC PROGRAM. DEMONSTRATION AND TEACHING GARDENS WILL BE ESTABLISHED TO SHOWCASE ORGANIC VEGETABLE PRODUCTION IN URBAN AGRICULTURE SETTINGS, SUCH AS BACKYARDS AND SCHOOL GARDENS. THESE GARDENS WILL BE THE CORNERSTONE OF URBAN AGRICULTURE EXTENSION PROGRAMMING WITH CONTENT ABOUT GROWING VEGETABLES, NUTRITION, FOOD SAFETY, AND FOOD PREPARATION AND PRESERVATION. THE FARM AND GARDENS WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO EXISTING COURSE WORK AND PROGRAMMING TO FACILITATE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING. THIS WILL INCLUDE COURSES IN AGRICULTURE, FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION, MARKETING AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP, AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. A DATABASE OF LOCAL PRODUCERS WILL BE CREATED AND RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN PRODUCERS AND KSU DINING SERVICES WILL BE FOSTERED TO PROMOTE LOCAL FOODS ON CAMPUS. THE EFFECTS OF PARTICIPATING IN STUDENT-RUN AGRICULTURAL ENDEAVORS ON FOSTERING BENEFICIAL CHANGES IN STUDENT DIETARY CHOICES AND METABOLIC HEALTH WILL BE EXAMINED. STUDENTS DIETARY ATTITUDES AND BEHAVIORS WILL BE ASSESSED THROUGH A SURVEY AND STUDENT METABOLIC HEALTH WILL BE MONITORED THROUGH SHAPE-UP KSU, AN EXISTING PROGRAM. A SURVEY WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED TO INVESTIGATE COMMUNITY INTEREST IN URBAN AGRICULTURE IN LOW-INCOME NEIGHBORHOODS IN FOOD DESERTS IN FRANKFORT, KY.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES TWO PERSISTENT PROGRAMS IN THE FANH-RELATED AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES: 1) EQUITY GAPS IN THE PARTICIPATION AND PERSISTENCE OF UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS PURSUING UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE PROGRAMS AND RELATED CAREERS IN FANH SCIENCES, AND (2) LACK OF EXPERIENTIAL ACTIVITIES TO PREPARE STUDENTS TO ENTER GRADUATE SCHOOL AND JOIN THE WORKFORCE. CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, MONTEREY (CSUMB) WILL PARTNER WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, SANTA CRUZ (UCSC) IN THIS PROJECT TO PROMOTE BROADENING PARTICIPATION IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE EDUCATION BY WORKING COLLABORATIVELY TO SUPPORT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND JOB PLACEMENT FOR UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY COLLEGES, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, AND THE REGIONAL AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY. AT CSUMB, UNDERGRADUATES MAJORING IN A NEW FANH-RELATED SCIENCES DEGREE WILL PARTICIPATE IN A TWO-YEAR SCHOLARS PROGRAM AIMED AT BOLSTERING SELF-CONFIDENCE, SELF-EFFICACY, AND EXPOSURE TO AUTHENTIC RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO SUPPORT FACULTY IN DEVELOPING FANH-RELATED COURSE-BASED RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AT CSUMB. THE PROJECT WILL FORGE STRONG TIES BETWEEN CSUMB UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND UCSC GRADUATE PROGRAMS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON FANH-RELATED SCIENCES, FACILITATING CURRICULAR ARTICULATION BETWEEN THE TWO INSTITUTIONS. AT UCSC, GRADUATE STUDENTS AND FACULTY WILL MENTOR UNDERGRADUATES FROM CSUMB ENTERING INTO GRADUATE TRAINING, WHILE ALSO PROVIDING FOR MENTORING AND RESEARCH SUPPORT. OVERALL, THE PROJECT WILL ATTRACT AND SUPPORT UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS IN ORDER TO PREPARE THEM FOR CAREERS RELATED TO THE FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES IN THE UNITED STATES, ALIGNING THE EFFORTS OF TWO HSIS AND OTHER NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS TO SUPPORT ACADEMIC DEVELOPMENT AND CAREER ATTAINMENT OF UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE NEW BEGINNINGS FOR CHOCTAW TRIBAL STUDENTS (NBCTS) PROGRAM IS A COLLABORATIVE GRANT PROPOSAL SUBMITTED BY MISSISSIPPI STATE UNIVERSITY (MSU) AND THE MISSISSIPPI BAND OF CHOCTAW INDIANS (MBCI). THE PROPOSAL ALIGNS WITH GOAL FOUR OF THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) - TO FACILITATE RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, DEVELOP AN EFFECTIVE AND DIVERSE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE, AND COLLECT GRADUATION DATA OF TRIBAL STUDENTS. THE NBCTS PROGRAM WILL TARGET MBCI HIGH SCHOOL AND COLLEGE STUDENTS ATTENDING MSU. RECRUITMENT PROGRAM EFFORTS WILL TARGET STUDENTS WHO ATTEND CHOCTAW CENTRAL HIGH SCHOOL (CCHS) OR PARTICIPATE IN THE YOUTH OPPORTUNITY PROGRAM (YOP). THESE RECRUITMENT EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON INSPIRING MBCI STUDENTS THROUGH PROGRAMMING ON CAREERS IN AGRICULTURE. SUPPORTING THE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF AI/AN STUDENTS WILL IMPROVE GRADUATION RATES AT MSU. WITH A MORE HIGHLY EDUCATED WORKFORCE, THE MBCI WILL BE ABLE TO BETTER FULFILL THEIR AGRICULTURAL, ENGINEERING, AND HEALTHCARE NEEDS, FACILITATING RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. RETENTION PROGRAM EFFORTS WILL MORE BROADLY TARGET AI/AN STUDENTS CURRENTLY ENROLLED AT MSU, WITH A FOCUS ON THE UNIVERSITY'S MBCI STUDENTS.TO INCREASE THE RETENTION AND GRADUATION RATE OF TRIBAL STUDENTS AT MSU, THE PROPOSED NBCTS PROGRAM INCLUDES STRATEGIES TO STRENGTHEN THE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF MBCI STUDENTS AT MSU. RECRUITMENT EFFORTS WILL FOCUS ON HIGH SCHOOL PREPARATION THROUGH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE 4-H BUILD YOUR FUTURE CURRICULUM WHICH INCLUDES EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES AND MSU RECRUITMENT PROGRAMS INCLUDING CAREER DAYS, PREVIEW WEEKENDS, AND ADMISSIONS COUNSELOR SEMINARS. RETENTION EFFORTS WILL DRAW ON EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, THE SUPPORT AND DEVELOPMENT OF STUDENT SERVICES, AND INCREASED ACADEMIC ADVISING THROUGH INFORMAL AND FORMAL MENTORSHIP PROGRAMS. THE NBCTS PROGRAM WILL FOCUS RETENTION EFFORTS THROUGH THE NATIVE AMERICAN STUDENT ASSOCIATION (NASA) AND PAID RESEARCH INTERNSHIPS FOR MBCI STUDENTS. STRATEGIES TO STRENGTHEN NASA INCLUDE DEVELOPING A SCHOLARLY LEARNING COMMUNITY THROUGH TECHNOLOGICAL AND PROGRAMMATIC SUPPORT CENTERED AROUND PEER MENTORING AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. NASA MEMBERS WILL PROVIDE PEER MENTORING TO STUDENTS ATTENDING CCHS. THE NASA WILL ALSO PROVIDE A TRIBAL CULTURAL CALENDAR TO MSU AND WILL RECEIVE FINANCIAL AND TRANSPORTATION SUPPORT TO RETURN HOME FOR KEY CULTURAL HOLIDAYS WITH THE MBCI. RESEARCH INTERNSHIPS WILL PROVIDE MBCI STUDENTS WITH FACULTY MENTORS WHO WILL FACILITATE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND ACADEMIC ADVISING AIMED AT SUPPORTING SUCCESSFUL TRANSITION INTO GRADUATE SCHOOL OR EMPLOYMENT UPON GRADUATION. TO INFORM RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION EFFORTS, FOCUS GROUPS AND A CLIMATE SURVEY WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH TRIBAL STUDENTS AT MSU. FUTURE PROGRAMMING WILL BE INFORMED BY DATA COLLECTED ON THE APPLICATION, DROP-OUT, AND GRADUATION RATES OF MBCI STUDENTS. THE COMBINATION OF THESE EFFORTS WILL FACILITATE TRIBAL PROSPERITY BY CREATING AN EFFECTIVE AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** ENROLLMENT OF INDIGENOUS STUDENTS IN GRADUATE NATURAL RESOURCES PROGRAMS IS SEVERELY UNDERREPRESENTED. BUILDING TRIBAL EXPERTISE AND CAPACITY IN NATURAL RESOURCES DISCIPLINES IS ESSENTIAL BECAUSE TRIBES MAINTAIN SOVEREIGNTY OVER NATURAL RESOURCES ON THEIR LANDS. MORE BROADLY, NATURAL RESOURCES GRADUATE PROGRAMS HAVE HISTORICALLY SEEN LOW ENROLLMENT OF BLACK, INDIGENOUS AND OTHER PEOPLE OF COLOR (BIPOC). INCREASINGLY, CLIMATE CHANGE AND ECOLOGICAL DISTURBANCES HAVE CHALLENGED THE WAY THAT WE ADDRESS NATURAL RESOURCE CHALLENGES. MOREOVER, TRAINING STUDENTS TO WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH OTHERS, INCLUDING ACROSS DIVERSE LAND OWNERSHIPS AND DISCIPLINES, WILL BE REQUIRED FOR SUCCESSFUL NATURAL RESOURCE RESEARCHERS AND MANAGERS IN THE 2020S AND BEYOND. THE CHALLENGES IN FOREST AND NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT IS RELEVANT TO THE NATIONAL NEEDS PROGRAM GOALS BY INCREASING THE NUMBER OF TRAINED SPECIALISTS FROM DIVERSE BACKGROUNDS. THIS SITUATION CREATES THE DEMAND FOR A NEW GENERATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES RESEARCHERS AND MANAGERS TO INTEGRATE INFORMATION FROM A VARIETY OF DISCIPLINES. IN RESPONSE TO THIS DEMAND, WE PROPOSE AN INTEGRATED GRADUATE TRAINING COHORT WITH TWO MASTER'S AND TWO DOCTORAL STUDENTS FOCUSED ON FOREST RESOURCES WITH AN EMPHASIS ON CONSERVATION AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES. OUR PROJECT GOALS ALIGN WITH THE USDA'S CHALLENGE AREA FOR AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES SCIENCE FOR CLIMATE VARIABILITY AND CHANGE. THE PROPOSED PROGRAM WILL (1) ESTABLISH A TRIBAL NATURAL RESOURCES PROGRAM TRACK IN THE UNIVERSITY OF MINNESOTA'S NATURAL RESOURCES SCIENCE AND MANAGEMENT GRADUATE PROGRAM AND (2) INCREASE THE NUMBER OF BIPOC STUDENTS MATRICULATED AND GRADUATED FROM THE PROGRAM.

negativeFlows.title: IN THE LAST 20 YEARS OR SO, THE GOAT INDUSTRY IN THE UNITED STATES HAS PROFITED BY AMERICAN'S INCREASED DESIRE TO PRODUCE FOOD WITHOUT CHEMICALS AND PESTICIDES, AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF COMMERCIAL ENTERPRISES FOR PROCESSING MEAT AND MILK PRODUCTS. THE DOE IS SEASONALLY POLYESTROUS AND THE BREEDING SEASON IS GENERALLY RESTRICTED TO THE AUTUMN AND WINTER. MANY OTHER FACTORS INCLUDING NUTRITION, TEMPERATURE, DISEASE, PRESENCE OF THE MALE, AND GENETIC VARIATIONS MAY ALSO INFLUENCE THE SEASONALITY, AND HENCE, REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECT WILL EVALUATE THE EFFECTS OF GRAZING LEGUMES AND GRASSES MIXTURES ON IMPROVING THE REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY OF GOATS IN ORDER TO INCREASE FARM INCOME PER UNIT ANIMAL OF PRODUCTION UNDER INTENSIVE AND ROTATIONAL GRAZING SYSTEMS. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE: 1.TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTS OF DIVERSE GRASS AND LEGUME FORAGES ON THE OCCURRENCE OF ESTRUS, LENGTHS OF ESTROUS CYCLES AND OVERALL REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY IN THE SPANISH AND KIKO GOATS. 2.TO ASSESS THE FEASIBILITY OF THREE KIDDINGS IN TWO YEARS BY INDUCING FERTILE ESTRUS DURING THE NON-BREEDING SEASONS IN THE SPANISH AND KIKO GOATS. 3.TO DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF DIVERSE FORAGES IN CONTROLLING PARASITES IN GOATS TO REDUCE THE OVERALL LEVELS OF PASTURE CONTAMINATION. THE INNOVATIVE NATURE OF THIS PROPOSAL LIES ON THE COMBINED RESEARCH EFFORT OF MIXING LIVESTOCK SPECIES, INTENSIVE ROTATIONAL MANAGEMENT FOR FORAGE SUSTAINABILITY, AND SEQUENTIAL GRAZING TO OPTIMIZE UTILIZATION OF AVAILABLE FORAGES TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF REPRODUCTION AND PARASITES IN SMALL RUMINANTS, AND THE REDUCTION OF INPUTS FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES.

MAKING AGRICULTURE SUSTAINABLE REQUIRES UNDERSTANDING WHERE BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (BMPS) WILL BE MOST EFFECTIVE IN THE LANDSCAPE TO MAINTAIN THE CONDITION OF NEARBY ECOSYSTEMS, SINCE HUMANS RECEIVE DIVERSE BENEFITS FROM NATURAL ECOSYSTEMS AS WELL AS AGRICULTURAL LANDS. WETLANDS IN PARTICULAR PROVIDE A WIDE VARIETY OF THESE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, INCLUDING NUTRIENT TREATMENT, CARBON STORAGE, POLLINATION, AND FLOOD MITIGATION. PLANNING FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE IN DELAWARE IS ESPECIALLY CHALLENGING WITH SEA LEVEL RISE. WE PROPOSE TO ASSESS THE IMPACTS OF SEA LEVEL RISE ON AGRICULTURE AND WETLAND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND EXPLORE NOVEL USES OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES MAPPING FOR PLANNING BMPS. IN OUR RESEARCH (PRIMARY FOCUS), WE WILL (A) EVALUATE HOW WETLAND SERVICES CHANGE WITH PROXIMITY TO AGRICULTURE, (B) STATISTICALLY PINPOINT "HOTSPOTS" WITH HIGH DELIVERY OF DIVERSE BENEFITS AND INVESTIGATE THE BMPS PROMOTING HOTSPOTS NEAR AGRICULTURAL LANDS, AND (C) USE SEA LEVEL PREDICTIONS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL MARGINAL CROPLANDS (CANDIDATES FOR DIFFERENT BMPS) AND SERVICE HOTSPOTS THAT MAY BE LOST. OVERALL, UNDERSTANDING THE FEEDBACKS BETWEEN LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS AND THE FULL ARRAY OF BENEFITS THAT OUR LANDS PROVIDE WILL HELP US INCREASE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES. THE PROJECT ALSO STRENGTHENS DELAWARE STATE UNIVERSITY'S RESEARCH AND TEACHING CAPABILITIES IN SPATIAL ANALYSIS. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, WE WILL (A) IMPROVE INFRASTRUCTURE AND INFORMATION-SHARING FOR SPATIAL RESEARCH, (B) DEVELOP A NEW COURSE AND WORKSHOPS IN ADVANCED SPATIAL ANALYSIS AND UPDATE MATERIALS IN OTHER COURSES, AND (C) SHARE RESEARCH PRODUCTS WITH FARMERS, PROFESSIONAL DATA USERS, AND K-12 AUDIENCES.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** AS ALABAMA CITIES AND ECONOMIES ARE GROWING, THE REALITIES OF SOCIAL AND RACIAL INEQUITIES CONTINUE TO CREATE BARRIERS TO SUSTAINABLE, HIGH-WAGE EMPLOYMENTIN LIMITED-RESOURCE COMMUNITIES.ALTHOUGH MANY AMERICANS BELIEVE HARD WORK CAN CREATE ECONOMIC MOBILITY, DEFINED AS IMPROVED WELL-BEING IN ONE'S LIFETIME, ONLY 5.2% OF POOR ALABAMIANS WILL MAKE IT INTO THE WEALTHY CLASS. FURTHERMORE, DATA SHOWS THAT INEQUITY IS EXACERBATED ALONG RACIAL LINES, MEANING THAT LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES OF COLOR EXPERIENCE THE MOST CHALLENGES IN ECONOMIC ADVANCEMENT. TO ADDRESS THESE ISSUES, ALABAMA COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SYSTEM AT ALABAMA A&M UNIVERSITY WILL IMPLEMENT A 2-YEAR PROJECT TO INVESTIGATE THE STATE OF ECONOMIC MOBILITY IN FOUR ALABAMA URBAN CENTERS, CONVENE CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERS TO CREATE NEW RESOURCES AND OPPORTUNITIES, AND IMPLEMENT HOLISTIC PROGRAMS THAT PROVIDE BUSINESS TRAINING AND SUPPORTTO LIMITED-RESOURCED ENTREPRENEURS OF COLOR.THE UPWARD ALABAMA PROJECT CENTERS AROUND ONE KEY QUESTION: HOW CAN WE PROVIDE COLLABORATIVE AND HOLISTIC RESOURCES TO CHRONICALLY UNEMPLOYED AND UNDER-EMPLOYED ALABAMIANS AND CREATE PATHWAYS TOWARDS ECONOMIC MOBILITY? THE PROJECT WILL BE IMPLEMENTED IN TWO PHASES: COMMUNITY RESEARCH AND PROGRAMMING. FIRST,WE WILL COLLECT DATA FROM TARGETED COMMUNITIES IN HUNTSVILLE, BIRMINGHAM, MONTGOMERY, AND MOBILE TO ANALYZE THE VARIOUS CHALLENGES, NEEDS, AND SERVICE GAPS THAT ARE PERPETUATING ECONOMIC INEQUITIES.WE WILL THEN APPLY FINDINGS TO THE CREATION OF THE GO-GETTER PROGRAM, WHICH WILL COMBINE COMMUNITY PARTNER HUBS, COHORT-BASED WORKSHOPS, AND MENTORSHIP TO TRANSFORM LIVELIHOODS THROUGH SMALL BUSINESS ENTREPRENEURSHIP. THIS PROJECTWILL PRODUCE NEW KNOWLEDGE ON URBAN ECONOMICS VIA THE COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS OF HUNDREDS OF SURVEYS; WILL INCREASE CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION TOWARDS EQUITYBY CONVENING DOZENS OF COMMUNITY PARTNERS, PRIVATE EMPLOYERS, AND MAJOR INSTITUTIONS; AND ULTIMATELY CATALYZE ECONOMIC MOBILITY FOR HUNDREDS OF ALABAMIANS. CONTINUATION PLANS BEYOND THIS GRANT PERIOD INCLUDETHE EXPANSION OF THE GO-GETTER PROGRAM INTO TWO PATHWAYS, ONE FOR ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND ANOTHER FOR CAREER DEVELOPMENT. RESEARCH AND PROGRAM EVALUATION FINDINGS WILL BE SHARED BROADLY TO SUPPORT ECONOMIC EQUITY PROJECTS IN OTHER COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE COUNTRY.

DUE TO PROXIMITY, PESTICIDE CONCENTRATIONS IN AMBIENT AIR ARE HIGHER IN AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES AND NEAR TREATED FIELDS. DURING THE PESTICIDE APPLICATION, THE DIRECTION DRIFT OF PESTICIDE IS CRITICAL TO ITS IMPACT ON NEARBY COMMUNITIES. SOME OF THE HEALTH PROBLEMS THAT AFFECT POPULATIONS LIVING IN THE URBAN-RURAL INTERFACE IS BELIEVED TO STEM FROM EXPOSURE TO PESTICIDE VAPORS THAT ARE PRESENT IN THE ATMOSPHERE FOLLOWING THE APPLICATION OF THE PRODUCT BY FARMERS. THE EXTENT OF THIS ON POPULATIONS LIVING IN THE URBAN-AGRICULTURAL INTERFACE IS NOT CLEAR, ALTHOUGH SOME RESIDENTS IN THE URBAN AGRICULTURAL INTERFACE HAVE ATTRIBUTED VARIOUS AILMENTS (ALLERGIES, CANCER, BIRTH DEFECTS, MALE STERILITY,CONTAMINATION OF BREAST MILK, GENETIC MUTATIONS, RESPIRATORY DISEASES, AND MANY MORE) TO PESTICIDEEXPOSURE.THERE IS A LIMITED RESEARCH DONE IN INTEGRATING CURRENT KNOWLEDGE ON WEATHER PREDICTION INTO PESTICIDE APPLICATION PRACTICES. THERE IS, THEREFORE, A NEED FOR DEVELOPING METHODS FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATING THE EXTENT OF PESTICIDE EXPOSURE ON THE URBAN-AGRICULTURAL INTERFACE AND THE EFFECT OF WEATHER PATTERNS ON PESTICIDE DRIFT. IN ADDITION, THERE IS A NEED TO RAISE THE AWARENESS OF RESIDENTS IN URBAN-AGRICULTURAL INTERFACES ABOUT THE POSSIBLE RISKS POSED BY SUCH TYPE OF POLLUTION.THE PROPOSED STUDY, THEREFORE, SEEKS TO EVALUATE PRESENT METHODS FOR MONITORING AND MODELING THE ATMOSPHERIC SPREAD OF PESTICIDE POLLUTANTS IN URBAN-AGRICULTURAL AREAS, IDENTIFY HOTSPOTS OF OCCURRENCE, AND ASSESS THE VULNERABILITY OF AFFECTED COMMUNITIES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT THE PROJECT WILL LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF A DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL THAT WILL BE BENEFICIAL FOR COMMUNITIES LIVING IN URBAN-AGRICULTURAL INTERFACES.

OUR INTENT IS TO MORE EFFECTIVELY LINK TEACHING, RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO PROVIDE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS TO LIMITED RESOURCE AND UNDERSERVED FARMERS AND CONSUMERS, WHICH WILL MAXIMIZE PROFITS AND BENEFITS FROM THE SWEETPOTATO VALUE CHAIN. THE FSEC, A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT AMONG FNS, CE AND EXTENSION WILL BE CONTINUED AS A RESIDENT AND ON-LINE OFFERING AT TU. OUR CONTINUATION PLAN INCLUDES RETENTION OF THE NUTRITION AND WELLNESS COORDINATOR TO STRENGTHEN ACTIVITIES (INCLUDING THE SWEETPOTATO SERIES) GEARED TOWARDS THE PRODUCERS/FARMERS, PROCESSORS, AND CONSUMERS. THE SUSTAINABLE, CONTINUATION PLAN ALSO INCLUDES SCALING-UP OTHER SWEETPOTATO PRODUCTS SUCH AS THE BEVERAGE, CEREAL AND BREAD FOR THE GRADUATE RESEARCH COMPONENT OF THIS PROJECT AND THUS CONTINUE TO ENHANCE THE SWEETPOTATO VALUE CHAIN.
